questions.stem:
A yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), glucose and water are mixed in a test tube. 
The diagrams show the test tube at the start and after one hour. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/1-1-image-4-yeast.png)Which process causes this change?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (respiration) because: Yeast is a living organism that can respire both aerobically and anaerobically. The gas carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is always produced as one of the waste products, the main point of the reaction being to release energy. The bubbles of gas seen after one hour are bubbles of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). A is incorrect because reproduction is the process by which more of the same kind of organism is made and doesn’t directly result in the release of carbon dioxide. C is incorrect because growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass caused by an increase in cell number or cell size (or both). D is incorrect because sensitivity is the ability to detect or sense stimuli in the internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses.

questions.stem:
The salivary glands contain cells which are responsible for producing salivary amylase, a digestive enzyme.
Which organelles would be present in large numbers in cells of the salivary glands?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (mitochondria and ribosomes) because: Salivary amylase is an enzyme ; enzymes are made from protein . Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in all cells Production of proteins requires significant amounts of energy and therefore cells which manufacture digestive enzymes. that need to be made and then transported out of the cell would contain a lot of mitochondria , as this is where respiration takes place A and B are incorrect because although mitochondria and ribosomes would be required in large numbers, each cell only ever possesses one nucleus. C is incorrect because vacuoles are present in plant cells; salivary glands are animal cells.

questions.stem:
The image below shows a pyramid of biomass for a food chain in a rainforest ecosystem.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/image-10.png)What would be an appropriate pyramid of numbers for this food chain?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/image-11.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The first diagram shows a pyramid of biomass, although the trees are few in number, they are large organisms with a very high biomass. Remember that biomass is the biological mass of the organisms after water has been removed. The aphids have a small biomass; therefore a very large number are needed to support the next trophic level so in a pyramid of numbers this will be a much larger box than the producers. Remember that the producers are always at the bottom of a pyramid. Pyramids of biomass are always pyramid shaped but pyramids of numbers may not be . A & D are incorrect because there will only be a few trees supporting many of the next level in the chain. In a pyramid of numbers, when the producers are very large organisms, they will be represented by a smaller box. B is incorrect because if there were only a very small number of aphids there would not be enough to support the next level in the chain.

questions.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly describes the structures present in a bacterial cell?


|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | cell membrane | cell wall | chromosome | nucleus |
| A | ✘ | ✔ | ✘ | ✘ |
| B | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✘ |
| C | ✔ | ✔ | ✘ | ✘ |
| D | ✔ | ✘ | ✘ | ✔ |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Bacterial cells have a cell membrane and a cell wall. They contain a relatively large circular chromosome that is not bound inside a nucleus. The other answers are incorrect because they do not show the correct structures present in bacterial cells. The diagram below shows a typical bacterial cell.

questions.stem:
The kidneys excrete excess water in urine. 
The main component of urine is water.
State two other substances that are excreted by healthy kidneys.
questions.explanation: Two other substances that are excreted by healthy kidneys are: Any two from the following: Urea; [1 mark] Salt(s) / (named) ions / (named) minerals; [1 mark] Any other valid and correct substance e.g. hormones; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] Make sure you read all the question information carefully; it can be tempting to put water here as part of your answer but this has already been included for you in the question.

questions.stem:
A student investigates the rate of emission of thermal radiation by four metal containers, W, X, Y, and Z. The metal containers are identical except for the texture and colour of their surfaces.
The student fills the metal containers with equal volumes of water at the same temperature.
The graph shows how the temperature of the water in the containers varies with time.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/02/54856-cie-p1-q15-cooling-curves.png)
Which row correctly identifies the four surfaces?


| ['', 'W', 'X', 'Y', 'Z'] |
|---|
| A | shiny white | dull white | shiny black | dull black |
| B | dull black | shiny black | dull white | shiny white |
| C | shiny black | dull black | shiny white | dull white |
| D | dull white | shiny white | dull black | shiny black |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The containers are identical, and each contains the same amount of water at the same initial temperature This means that the only thing that affects the rate of emission of thermal radiation (how quickly the temperature falls) is the type of surface Black surfaces are better emitters of radiation than white surfaces Dull surfaces are better emitters of radiation than shiny surfaces The surface that is the best emitter of radiation will lose energy at the fastest rate, which is shown by the steepest curve on the graph Dull black surfaces are the best emitters of thermal radiation, so this must be surface Z The surface that is the worst emitter of radiation will lose energy at the slowest rate, which is shown by the shallowest curve on the graph Shiny white surfaces are the worst emitters of thermal radiation, so this must be surface W The rate of cooling, from fastest to slowest, by surface is: dull black (Z)  >  shiny black (Y)  > dull white (X) > shiny white (W) This is shown by option A

questions.stem: Element X contains 4 electrons in its outer shell and 125 neutrons in its nucleus. What is element X?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Elements are arranged on the Periodic table in increasing atomic number where each element has one proton more than the element preceding it. The Group number gives the number of electrons in the outer shell of each element. X is in Group IV so has four electrons in its outer shell. X also has 125 neutrons , which corresponds to lead (Pb) only (as lead has a mass number of 207 and an atomic number of 82, so  207- 82 = 125 neutrons). A is incorrect as beryllium has 2 electrons in its outer shell and carbon has 4 in its outer shell. B is incorrect as although carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell, it has a mass number of 12 and therefore only 6 neutrons in its nucleus (12 - 6 =6). C is incorrect as tin has 69 neutrons, 119 - 50 = 69.

questions.stem:
A student decided to investigate the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme lipase.
Five different test tubes are set up. Each test tube contains a mixture of the enzyme lipase and its substrate, a lipid.
Which condition should not be kept the same in each of the five test tubes?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (pH) because: If the condition being investigated is pH, then this is the independent  variable and should be different in each test tube to get a good range of results. A is incorrect because the temperature is one factor that can affect enzyme activity and should not be changed if pH is being altered. B is incorrect because the concentration of the enzyme is another factor that needs to be kept the same (not changed) to make the experiment fair as it can also affect enzyme activity. C is incorrect because the volume of the lipid solution is one of the things that needs to be kept the same to make the experiment valid; the more lipid (substrate) there is, the longer it will take for the reaction to complete.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows a section through a leaf. 
Which cell type would have the highest concentration of oxygen on a bright, sunny day?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/6-q7-cross-section.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: A is a palisade mesophyll cell which is where most photosynthesis takes place (due to palisade mesophyll cells having the highest concentration of chloroplasts). The more photosynthesis occurring, the greater the amount of oxygen produced as a waste product. Some oxygen will be used up by each type of plant cell in the process of aerobic respiration, but the amounts are similar in each type of cell. B is incorrect because it is part of the vascular bundle (xylem and phloem); these tissues do not contain chloroplasts. C is incorrect because it is a spongy mesophyll cell which has fewer chloroplasts than the palisade cells (so photosynthesises less). D is incorrect because it is an epidermal cell. Epidermal cells do not contain chloroplasts so do not photosynthesise.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows a light ray incident on the boundary between a glass block and air at point O.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/02/41168-refraction-in-semicircular-block.png)The angle of incidence  is . The critical angle for the glass is .
Which path does the light ray take after point O?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B When light travels from an optically denser medium (glass) to a less dense medium (air), it refracts away from the normal Total internal reflection only occurs if the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle In this case, the angle of incidence (  ) is less than the critical angle (  ), so the light will refract out into the air Path B shows the ray bending away from the normal as it enters the air A is incorrect as it shows the ray bending towards the normal. C is incorrect as the light only travels along the boundary if the angle of incidence is exactly  . D is incorrect as total internal reflection only occurs if the angle of incidence is greater than  . Remember the key rule: when light passes from a denser to a less dense medium, it bends away from the normal. Always compare the angle of incidence to the critical angle first: if the angle of incidence is less than the critical angle  , refraction occurs if the angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle  , light travels along the boundary if the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle  , total internal reflection occurs

A & D are incorrect because there will only be a few trees supporting many of the next level in the chain. In a pyramid of numbers, when the producers are very large organisms, they will be represented by a smaller box. B is incorrect because if there were only a very small number of aphids there would not be enough to support the next level in the chain.

questions.stem:
A student heats the top of a test tube of water until the water boils. A piece of ice, held at the bottom of the test tube by a metal gauze, remains frozen.
Which of the following statements is a correct conclusion from this experiment?
options: A. Water is a good conductor of thermal energy.
B. Water is a poor conductor of thermal energy.
C. Convection currents travel downwards in liquids.
D. The metal gauze is a good thermal insulator.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B The ice at the bottom of the tube does not melt even though the water at the top is boiling This demonstrates that thermal energy is not being transferred effectively from the top to the bottom through the liquid by conduction Convection cannot transfer the energy downwards because the heated water at the top becomes less dense and stays at the top A is incorrect because if water were a good conductor, the thermal energy would have reached the bottom and melted the ice. C is incorrect because convection currents are caused by heated fluids rising, not sinking. D is incorrect because metals are good conductors; the gauze is only used to keep the ice submerged at the bottom of the tube.

questions.stem:
A student was measuring the rate of reaction using the apparatus in the diagram.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/ms3-6-1-easy-cie-igcse-chemistry.png)What reaction is the student studying?
options: A. CaO + H 2 SO 4 → CaSO 4 + H 2 O
C. Fe + H 2 SO 4 → FeSO 4 + H 2
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C The diagram shows that the reactants are a liquid and a solid . The flask is sealed and a gas syringe is connected to the flask, hence one of the products must be a gas . C is the only option that includes a solid (Fe) and liquid (H 2 SO 4 ) reactants, and a gaseous product (H 2 ). A, B and D are incorrect as there are not any gaseous products formed in these reactions.

questions.stem:
What are the characteristics of birds?


|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | skin covered in feathers | maintain a constant body temperature | jelly-covered eggs | external ears present |
| A | ✔ | ✘ | ✔ | ✘ |
| B | ✘ | ✘ | ✘ | ✔ |
| C | ✔ | ✔ | ✘ | ✘ |
| D | ✘ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Birds are animals that, like mammals, maintain a constant body temperature, and their skins are covered in feathers. Birds lay eggs covered with a hard shell on land, and don’t have external ears.

questions.stem:
A student collected some of the solution from the phloem in the stem of a plant. 
Which of the following would be present in the liquid?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Amino acids would be the only substance from the options given to move through the phloem (as well as sucrose). A is incorrect because glucose is never transported through the phloem; however, sucrose (a disaccharide that contains one glucose molecule) is transported through the phloem. B and D are incorrect because starch and cellulose are large biomolecules that are insoluble in water, therefore they cannot be moved around the plant.

questions.stem:
Which row of the table below shows the correct chambers of the heart, from those with the thinnest walls to those with the thickest?


|  |  |
|---|---|
|  | thinnest → thickest |
| A | left ventricle | right ventricle | left atrium |
| B | left atrium | left ventricle | right ventricle |
| C | right ventricle | left atrium | left ventricle |
| D | left atrium | right ventricle | left ventricle |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Ventricles have much thicker muscle walls than atria because the atria are just passing the blood onto the ventricles whereas the ventricles have to generate enough force to push blood out of the heart The left ventricle has a thicker muscle wall than the right ventricle as the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, which are right next to the heart, whereas the left ventricle is pumping blood to the entire body and so has to generate a higher pressure to pump it a greater distance

questions.stem:
The image below shows a house mouse, whose scientific name is Mus musculus.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/1-1-image-1-mouse.png)Which genus does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C ( Mus ) because: In the binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus, the first name of the two is the genus that the organism belongs to. It is always written with a capital letter The second name is the name of its species and always has a small initial letter. Both should be italic ised A is incorrect because mammal is the class that the house mouse belongs to. B is incorrect because musculus is the species name (it begins with a lower case m). D is incorrect because a vertebrate is the phylum that the house mouse belongs to.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences show the correct path of oxygen as it enters the lungs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (trachea → bronchus → bronchiole → alveolus) because: Air containing oxygen is inhaled through the mouth or nose, moving down the trachea which branches into the left bronchus and right bronchus (plural bronchi ), the bronchi then divide into smaller branches (or airways) called bronchioles which eventually lead to a cluster of alveoli (singular alveolus).

questions.stem:
The image below shows two solutions separated by a partially permeable membrane.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/picture7.png)Which of the statements below would be true in relation to the image?
options: A. There is no net movement of water from W to X
B. There would be movement of water molecules from W to X
C. Osmosis of sugar molecules would occur from the dilute solution (W) to the concentrated solution (X)
D. Solution X is more dilute and therefore has a higher water potential than solution W
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (There would be movement of water molecules from W to X) because: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane Net movement’ means ‘overall movement’ - more water molecules will move from solution W to solution X, but water molecules are able to move in either direction (they don’t choose to move from one solution to another, because they can’t tell if the solution they’re in is dilute or concentrated) A is incorrect because the net movement of water would be from W (dilute solution) to X (concentrated solution). C is incorrect because osmosis only refers to the movement of water molecules, not sugar molecules. D is incorrect because solution X is more concentrated than W since there are more sugar molecules and less free water molecules in X.

questions.stem:
Which of the following processes is/are involved in the loss of water from the leaves of plants?
• diffusion

• osmosis

• condensation

• evaporation
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (1 and 4) because: Water molecules evaporate from mesophyll cells, forming water vapour (a gas) which diffuses from an area of higher concentration in the air spaces inside the leaf to a lower concentration in the air outside the leaf (unless it’s very humid and the air is saturated with water!) A is incorrect because diffusion is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but condensation (change in the stage of gas to a liquid) is not. B is incorrect because diffusion is only one of the processes involved in water loss from the leaves of a plant. C Is incorrect because evaporation is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but diffusion is also involved.

questions.stem:
Different salts can be prepared by titrating an alkali with an aqueous acid.
Three pieces of apparatus, P, Q and R, used to measure volumes of liquid are shown below.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/10/fig-1-q1b-1cho-1f-paper-1-nov-2021.png)What are the names of the three pieces of apparatus, P, Q and R?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | P | Q | R |
| A | pipette | burette | measuring cylinder |
| B | burette | pipette | conical flask |
| C | pipette | volumetric flask | burette |
| D | burette | pipette | measuring cylinder |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D P is a burette, it is used to add varying volumes which can be measured to a high degree of accuracy Q is a pipette, it is used to measure a specific quantity of liquid to a high degree of accuracy R is a measuring cylinder, it is used to measure volumes of liquids but the degree of accuracy is not as high as using a pipette or burette A is incorrect as the names of P and Q are the wrong way round B is incorrect as R is not a conical flask C is incorrect as all of the names are incorrect

questions.stem:
The drawing shows a food test being carried out in a laboratory.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/HdWe4kL0_4-1-q4e---mcq.png)Which food test is being shown and which food group is being tested for?
options: B. DCPIP test for Vitamin C
C. Benedict's test for reducing sugars
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Benedict's test for reducing sugars) because: The Benedict's test requires a heating step and a colour change is observed in a positive test. A is incorrect because the test for protein (the Biuret test) does not require a heating step, even though a colour change is observed in a positive protein test. B is incorrect because the test for Vitamin C (using DCPIP) does not require a heating step, even though a colour change is observed in a positive protein test. D is incorrect because the emulsion test for fats (using ethanol and water) does not require a heating step. This would also be dangerous, with flammable ethanol near a naked flame.

questions.stem:
Which of the following options is the best explanation for the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
Chlorophyll...
options: A. transfers light energy from the Sun because it has magnesium ions
B. transfers chemical potential energy from sunlight into organic molecules which can be used to synthesise carbohydrates such as glucose
C. transfers light energy from the Sun into chemical energy in inorganic molecules which can be used for growth
D. transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates) because: chlorophyll absorbs light energy (from the Sun or artificial light sources) light energy is used to drive a reaction between water and carbon dioxide, producing glucose (a carbohydrate) glucose can be converted into other carbohydrates, such as sucrose, starch and cellulose A is incorrect because chlorophyll molecules do contain magnesium ions, but this doesn’t outline its role in photosynthesis. B is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs light energy, not chemical potential energy, to drive the synthesis of organic molecules such as glucose (light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy stored in the bonds of glucose molecules). C is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs energy from sunlight to drive reactions between inorganic molecules (carbon dioxide and water) to produce glucose (an organic molecule). Glucose can then be converted into other molecules (such as amino acids) which are used in growth.

questions.stem:
Magnesium reacts with iron(III) oxide in the following reaction.
magnesium + iron(III) oxide → magnesium oxide + iron
Which statement about this reaction is correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Oxidation is defined as the gain of oxygen and reduction as the loss of oxygen Magnesium is oxidised as it gains oxygen in the reaction to form magnesium oxide A is not correct as magnesium oxide is a product formed by the oxidation of magnesium B is not correct as iron is a product formed by the reduction of iron(III) oxide D is not correct as iron(III) oxide is reduced as it loses oxygen to form iron

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows part of the nitrogen cycle. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/f8MF0E4W_image-4-1.png)Which letter would represent denitrification?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The process of denitrification removes nitrates from the soil, releasing it back into the atmosphere as nitrogen gas. This process occurs naturally by denitrifying bacteria in the soil, and it reduces soil fertility. A is incorrect because this arrow shows decomposition of animals into ammonium compounds. B is incorrect because this arrow refers to nitrification which is carried out by nitrifying bacteria. D is incorrect because this arrow depicts nitrogen fixation by bacteria in root nodules and lightning.

questions.stem:
To remain healthy, a person must be able to excrete a number of waste products produced as a result of metabolism.
A list of excretory products is given below.
Which of the following would be lost from both the kidneys and lungs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (water) because: Both the kidneys and the lungs are involved in the loss of water from the body. B is incorrect because carbon dioxide is not excreted by the kidneys. Carbon dioxide is mainly excreted by the lungs. C is incorrect because glucose is not excreted (under normal conditions) by either the kidneys or the lungs. Excess glucose is transported to the liver to be converted into glycogen for storage. D is incorrect because the lungs do not excrete urea, that is the role of the kidneys.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is a correct cause and effect?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | deficiency | cause | effect |
| A | iron | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver | brittle bones (rickets) |
| B | iron | lack of sunlight, fish and eggs | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues |
| C | vitamin D | lack of sunlight | brittle bones (rickets) |
| D | vitamin D | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: A vitamin D  deficiency leads to brittle  bones , as it is required for bones to be able to absorb  calcium ions in the bloodstream . Calcium is the mineral which is needed to strengthen bones; the less calcium the weaker they are. Vitamin D can be synthesized in the body when cholesterol in skin cells is converted into Vitamin D ; this reaction is driven by UV from sunlight. A is incorrect because the effect is not linked to a deficiency in iron. B is incorrect because the cause is incorrect. D is incorrect because the deficiency does not match the cause or the effect.

questions.stem:
Many metals can be extracted from their ores by heating the metal oxide with carbon.
Which of these metals can’t be extracted using carbon?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because Aluminium is more reactive than carbon. The method used to extract a metal from its ore depends on the reactivity of the metal in the reactivity series . Metals lower than carbon in the reactivity series can be reduced by heating with carbon. Metals above carbon in the reactivity series will either need to be reduced by another more reactive element or extracted via electrolysis. Extraction by electrolysis is used to extract aluminium. A,  B and D are incorrect as zinc, copper and iron are all below carbon in the reactivity series and can be extracted by reduction with carbon.

questions.stem:
HIV is an STI. The following statements are about changes that could occur in the body.
• Reduced antibody production

• Reduction in red blood cells

• Reduction in white blood cells

• Reduced volume of blood plasma

Which of these statements would be correct for HIV?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (1 and 3) because: HIV infects lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell) eventually leading to a reduction in their number. As the lymphocytes produce antibodies which enhance an immune response to infection, the reduction in antibody production eventually results in a reduced ability to fight infection (at this point a person has AIDS) HIV is a sexually transmitted disease; that is the HIV virus is passed from one person to another via body fluids A is incorrect because while HIV will reduce antibody production, it will not directly decrease the levels of red blood cells. B is incorrect because neither of these statements would be correct for a direct effect of HIV. C is incorrect because while HIV will reduce white blood cells it will not directly reduce the volume of plasma produced.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be transmitted by contact with contaminated surfaces?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (Salmonella and athletes foot) because: Both these diseases are transmitted when a person comes into contact with a surface that contains these pathogens. A is incorrect because malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. B is incorrect because typhoid is transmitted by the consumption of water or food contaminated with the faeces of people infected with typhoid. C is incorrect because influenza spreads by inhaling droplets in the air carrying the virus while dengue fever is spread by the bite of a specific species of mosquito ( Aedes aegypti ).

questions.stem: Which shows the correct size order of structures, starting with the smallest?
options: A. gene →  DNA strand →  chromosomes →  nucleus
B. DNA strand →  chromosomes →  gene → nucleus
C. chromosomes →  gene →  DNA strand →  nucleus
D. nucleus →  chromosomes →  DNA strand →  gene
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (gene →  DNA strand →  chromosomes →  nucleus) because: A gene is the smallest structure of those listed; a gene is a section of a single DNA strand.  DNA coils itself around to form chromosomes; chromosomes are found in the nucleus which is the largest structure.

questions.stem:
Two individuals are crossed. One is homozygous dominant (TT), the other heterozygous.
What will the genotypes of the offspring be?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (50% TT, 50% Tt) because: The parents have the genotypes TT (homozygous) and Tt (heterozygous) The gametes produced by the homozygous dominant individual will all contain the allele ‘T’ The possible gametes for the heterozygous parent will contain either ‘T’ or ‘t’ T T T TT TT t Tt Tt

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct definition of ‘adaptive features’?
options: A. A change in the environment that is an advantage to an organism.
B. An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce.
C. A change in phenotype that is caused by the environment.
D. An action that aids an organism's ability to survive.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce) because: Adaptive features are features that increase the chance of an organism surviving and reproducing in its environment. A is incorrect because there may be changes in an environment that will give certain phenotypes an advantage, however, this is not an adaptive feature. C is incorrect because a change in phenotype is not caused by the environment, but mutations in genes which can be inherited . D is incorrect because this answer describes behavioural adaptations such as mating rituals.

questions.stem:
An island’s entire population of a species of butterfly are descended from just two parents. These were introduced from the mainland.
Which of the following statements about this species of butterfly, compared with that of the mainland, is correct?
options: A. The population shows more genetic variety.
B. The population will adapt more slowly to environmental changes.
C. The population shows more phenotypic variation.
D. The population is less in danger of collapsing from disease.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (the population will adapt more slowly to environmental changes) because: The whole population has descended from just two parents, this will mean the population has very little genetic diversity (a small gene pool) Reduced variation in a population means that they are less likely to survive any changes in the environment Natural changes will occur due to random mutations , but these must occur in gametes that form new individuals to possibly introduce variation into the population; such changes will be slow The other answers are incorrect because all of these statements refer to a population that has a large gene pool and a large genetic diversity.

questions.stem: Which of the equations show the incomplete combustion of methane?
options: B. CH 4 + O 2 → C + 2 H 2 O
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Incomplete combustion of alkanes in general produces carbon and/or carbon monoxide along with water hydrocarbon + oxygen → carbon monoxide + carbon + water Carbon dioxide is formed with a plentiful supply of oxygen, during complete combustion Carbon monoxide is formed with a limited supply of oxygen Carbon is formed with a very limited supply of oxygen Exam questions will sometimes indicate if the product of incomplete combustion is carbon monoxide or carbon A is incorrect as this is the balanced symbol equation for the complete  combustion of methane C is incorrect as hydrogen is not a product of the combustion of alkanes D is incorrect as this is not a balanced equation and has hydrogen gas as a product.

|---|---|---|---|
|  | absorption | assimilation | egestion |
| A | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| B | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| C | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| D | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Absorption is the movement of soluble food molecules and ions through the intestinal wall into the blood to be transported to the cells. Once it reaches the cells these food molecules and ions will cross the cell membrane during assimilation in order to become part of the cell. Any food that hasn't been digested or absorbed will move along the alimentary canal and leave the body through the anus during egestion . A is incorrect because egestion does not involve excretion. The waste products that leave the body during the process of excretion comes from metabolic reactions that occur within cells . Waste products that leave the body during egestion was created outside cells . C is incorrect because the description of absorption and assimilation has been switched around. D is incorrect because all three descriptions is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

 OR 
 It provides enzymes; [1 mark] The amount of yeast in the mixture increases because: Yeast cells grow / multiply / reproduce / undergo budding / breed; [1 mark] iii) A higher temperature not used in this process because: Heat / high temperature would kill yeast (cells)

| A | atrioventricular valve | semilunar valve | septum |
| B | semilunar valve | atrioventricular valve | septum |
| C | semilunar valve | semilunar valve | atrioventricular valve |
| D | atrioventricular valve | atrioventricular valve | septum |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Semilunar valves are found in the two arteries connected to the heart (the only arteries in the body to contain valves); they prevent the backflow of blood into the heart when it relaxes after contracting The atrioventricular (AV) valves are located between the atria and the ventricles; they prevent the backflow of blood from the ventricles to the atria when the ventricles contract. The AV valve shown by Y in the question image is called the bicuspid or mitral valve The septum separates the two sides of the heart; preventing the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

questions.stem:

What group of cells were they referring to?
options: C. Red and white blood cells
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. (Male and female gametes) because: ‘Many, minute and motile’ refers to sperm cells. They are produced in very large numbers and are much smaller than the ovum (the egg) - they are much less energy intensive to produce which is why more of them can be made. They also have a tail to swim to the ovum ‘Few, fat and fixed’ refers to an ovum (egg cell). Generally, only one egg is released each month in the menstrual cycle . They are much larger than sperm cells and are unable to move independently, instead, they rely on the ciliated cells in the oviduct to waft them through to the uterus A common misconception here is that these statements are referring to animal and plant cells, students often think of animal cells being smaller and motile and plant cells being large and fixed.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs are responsible for removing excretory products from the blood?

A is incorrect because the bladder is not responsible for removing excretory products from the blood , it removes it from the body. C is incorrect because the liver is responsible for producing many of the excretory products, but it is not directly responsible for the excretion of these products. questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the effect of root hairs on absorption?
options: A. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water and ions by osmosis.
B. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
C. Increase the surface area, maximising the uptake of water by osmosis and ions by diffusion.
D. Provide a surface area, increasing the rate of absorption of water and ions by active transport.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Root hairs are extensions of the cytoplasm of root cells, increasing the surface area to maximise the absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport. A is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport. Osmosis only applies to the movement of water. C Is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport, not diffusion. D Is incorrect because there is no indication that surface area is increased in this explanation, and osmosis should be mentioned in relation to the movement of water.

A is incorrect because the nucleus contains the genetic information from the male. C is incorrect because the sperm cell has enzymes in the head (in the acrosome) to help it digest the outer layer of the egg so that it can release its nucleus into the egg. questions.stem: Element X contains 4 electrons in its outer shell and 125 neutrons in its nucleus. What is element X?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Elements are arranged on the Periodic table in increasing atomic number where each element has one proton more than the element preceding it. The Group number gives the number of electrons in the outer shell of each element. X is in Group IV so has four electrons in its outer shell. X also has 125 neutrons , which corresponds to lead (Pb) only (as lead has a mass number of 207 and an atomic number of 82, so  207- 82 = 125 neutrons). A is incorrect as beryllium has 2 electrons in its outer shell and carbon has 4 in its outer shell. B is incorrect as although carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell, it has a mass number of 12 and therefore only 6 neutrons in its nucleus (12 - 6 =6). C is incorrect as tin has 69 neutrons, 119 - 50 = 69.

options: A. The presence of an X chromosome
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (Antibody production) because: Antibodies are produced in response to any foreign cell in the body, regardless of whether that cell is a pathogenic microorganism or a cell from another member of the same or different species Don’t be distracted by the fact that the donor tissue is from a female and the recipient is a man – this has nothing to do with causing an immune response A is incorrect because the presence of an X chromosome in the grafted cells is not what provokes an immune response; it is the antigens on the surface of the cells which do that. B is incorrect because platelets are involved in blood clotting, not an immune response. C is incorrect because antibiotics are given to a patient with a bacterial infection, they don’t usually affect other human cells, and are not made by the body so do not form part of the immune response.

questions.stem:
The human body has a number of barriers to prevent infection by pathogens some of which are listed below.
• Skin

• Mucus

• Hairs in the nose

• Antibodies

• Stomach acid

Which of these are examples of mechanical barriers?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. (1 and 3) because: The skin and hairs in the nose forms a physical barrier that makes it more difficult for pathogens to enter the body. B and C are incorrect because mucus (2) is an example of a chemical barrier while antibodies (4) are produced by lymphocytes in response to foreign antigens entering the body, they do not act as a barrier. D is incorrect because stomach acid (5) is another example of a chemical barrier, not a mechanical one.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences show the correct path of oxygen as it enters the lungs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (trachea → bronchus → bronchiole → alveolus) because: Air containing oxygen is inhaled through the mouth or nose, moving down the trachea which branches into the left bronchus and right bronchus (plural bronchi ), the bronchi then divide into smaller branches (or airways) called bronchioles which eventually lead to a cluster of alveoli (singular alveolus).

questions.stem:
Which of the following processes would release the most energy in a cell from one molecule of glucose?
• Aerobic respiration in yeast

• Aerobic respiration in animals

• Aerobic respiration in plants
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (all of the above) because: The process of aerobic respiration is essentially the same in all eukaryotic cells, so the theoretical energy released will be the same when one molecule of glucose is broken down in any of the above cells.

questions.stem:
The statements below are about different hormones in the human body.
• Produced by the pancreas.

• Causes the voice to deepen at puberty.

• Causes an egg to mature in the menstrual cycle.

• Promotes the development of stronger muscles.

Which of these statements are correct for testosterone?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (2 and 4) because: Testosterone is the male hormone that causes secondary sexual characteristics during puberty . These include the development of stronger muscles and the voice to deepen. A is incorrect because while it does cause the voice to deepen, testosterone is not produced by the pancreas (it’s produced in the testes). C is incorrect because while it does promote the development of stronger muscles and is primarily thought of as a male hormone, women do produce small amounts of testosterone but it is not involved in the control of egg maturation in the ovaries. D is incorrect because even though this is a correct statement, it is not the only correct statement (the question is asking you for all the statements).

questions.stem:
The graph shows the relationship between the number of lichens and the levels of sulfur dioxide pollution.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/jp85qfh8_image-3.png)Which of these statements best describe the graph?
options: A. Sulfur dioxide levels do not affect lichen growth.
B. As sulfur dioxide levels increase, the number of lichen decreases.
C. Lichens cannot survive if there is sulfur dioxide present.
D. As sulfur dioxide levels increase, so does the number of lichen.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (as sulfur dioxide levels increase, the number of lichen decreases) because: The graph shows that as the levels of sulfur dioxide increase, the number of lichen species decreases. A is incorrect because there is a correlation between sulfur dioxide levels and the number of lichens. C is incorrect because some lichens are surviving even at relatively high levels of sulfur dioxide. D is incorrect because sulfur dioxide levels increase and the levels of lichens do not increase.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/05/cie-igcse-5-1h-mcq4.png)Which statement is correct?
options: A. Copper metal is deposited at the positive electrode.
B. In the external circuit the electrons move from negative to positive.
C. In the solution the electrons move from positive to negative.
D. Oxygen gas is produced at the positive electrode.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The ions present in the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate are: H + and OH - (from the aqueous solution), Cu 2+ and SO 4 2- The H + and Cu 2+ ions are attracted to the cathode and the OH - and SO 4 2- ions are attracted to the anode. At the cathode (negative electrode) the Cu 2+ ions are less reactive than the hydrogen  ions and are reduced to copper metal: Cu 2+ + 2 e - → Cu At the anode (positive electrode) the OH - ions are less reactive than SO 4 2- ions are oxidised to produce oxygen and water: 4 OH - → O 2 + H 2 O + 4 e - A is incorrect as copper ions are positive so copper metal is produced at the negative electrode (the cathode), not the positive electrode. B is incorrect as electrons in the external circuit begin at the negative terminal of the  battery and flow around the circuit and back to the positive terminal. C is incorrect as the electrons do not flow in the electrolyte, it is the ions that move and carry the current.

questions.stem:
The graph below shows the number of deaths from MRSA per 100 000 people in a population of over-65’s from 2005 to 2012.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/OFRaWUbT_image-4.png)Which of the following statements are possible explanations for the trend shown in the graph?
options: A. More effective antibiotics are being used to treat infected people.
B. A decrease in the size of the population of over-65 year olds.
C. Over-65 year olds are immune to MRSA infection.
D. Antibiotics do not affect viruses.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: It is most likely that the decrease in number of deaths from MRSA over time is a result of new or different antibiotics being used that are effective at treating MRSA infections; as a result, the death rate will fall. B is incorrect because a decrease in the population would not affect the death rate. C is incorrect because over-65’s are still dying from MRSA infection so this cannot be true or likely. D is incorrect because, while this is a true statement, it has nothing to do with the data shown.

questions.stem:
The diagrams show 3 different species of pollen grains as they appear under a microscope. The diagrams are all to the same scale.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/image-1.png)Which pollen grains are involved in insect pollination?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. (2 only) because: Pollen grains that are transferred by insect pollinators are larger and have a spiky surface to attach to insects. The pollen in picture 1 has a larger surface area with ‘wings’ and in picture 3 are small and light. These two features are more likely to be seen in wind pollinated seeds.

questions.stem:
ABO blood groups are an inherited characteristic.
What would the blood group of the offspring be when two parents have the genotypes IAIA and IAIO?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (group A) because: Blood group inheritance is an example of codominance There are three possible alleles that can be inherited; but an individual can only have a maximum of two alleles in their genotype Alleles I A and I B are dominant over I O , so because one parent is homozygous for blood group A, all of the offspring will inherit the I A allele, meaning all the offspring will be in group A (as the partner has a heterozygous genotype with the recessive I O allele I A I O I A I A I A I A I O I A I A I A I A I O

questions.stem:
The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle tissue with blood.
Fig. 1 shows a coronary artery with a blockage. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/coronary.png)Fig. 1
Explain the effect this blockage could have on heart muscle cells.
questions.explanation: The effect of the blockage on heart muscle cells is... Any two from the following: Less blood flows to the heart muscle / cells / tissue; [1 mark] Less oxygen reaches the heart muscle / cells / tissue; [1 mark] Therefore less (aerobic) respiration occurs OR less energy is released ; [1 mark] Heart cells will die; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] It is important when talking about energy from respiration that you use the term released and not produced, made or created as these terms are incorrect and will not award you marks.

questions.stem:
Two individuals are crossed. One is homozygous dominant (TT), the other heterozygous.
What will the genotypes of the offspring be?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (50% TT, 50% Tt) because: The parents have the genotypes TT (homozygous) and Tt (heterozygous) The gametes produced by the homozygous dominant individual will all contain the allele ‘T’ The possible gametes for the heterozygous parent will contain either ‘T’ or ‘t’ T T T TT TT t Tt Tt

questions.stem: Which letter shows the path of the energy from the sun?
options: A. chemical energy in sugars → stored in plants → trapped in chlorophyll
B. trapped in chlorophyll → chemical energy in sugars → stored in plants
C. stored in plants → chemical energy in sugars →  trapped in chlorophyll
D. stored in plants → trapped in chlorophyll →  chemical energy in sugars
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Energy from the sun is trapped by chlorophyll , the pigment found in chloroplasts. Light energy is then used to drive the synthesis of carbohydrates such as glucose (a sugar ); in this sense an energy transfer occurs from light to chemical potential energy within the bonds of carbohydrate molecules The sugars produced in photosynthesis are then stored as more complex molecules such as starch in the plant

questions.stem:
The diagram shows the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/q1-4-3-hard-cie-igcse-chemistry.png)What is the colour of the litmus at each electrode after five minutes?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | colour at anode | colour at cathode |
| A | blue | red |
| B | red | blue |
| C | red | colourless |
| D | colourless | blue |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride, positively  charged  hydrogen  ions are attracted to the negative  cathode where they are reduced to form hydrogen gas. At the positive  anode , the Cl - ions are oxidized to form chlorine gas. The ions that remain in solution are Na + ions and the OH - ions. These produce an alkaline solution so at the cathode the colour is blue . At the anode the solution is surprisingly colourless. This is because chlorine gas is a powerful bleaching agent and removes the colour from litmus. A, B and C are incorrect as these colours do not match with the correct results.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct definition of ‘adaptive features’?
options: A. A change in the environment that is an advantage to an organism.
B. An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce.
C. A change in phenotype that is caused by the environment.
D. An action that aids an organism's ability to survive.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce) because: Adaptive features are features that increase the chance of an organism surviving and reproducing in its environment. A is incorrect because there may be changes in an environment that will give certain phenotypes an advantage, however, this is not an adaptive feature. C is incorrect because a change in phenotype is not caused by the environment, but mutations in genes which can be inherited . D is incorrect because this answer describes behavioural adaptations such as mating rituals.

questions.stem: Which of these is not a feature of a hydrophyte?
options: B. Large air spaces in the tissues.
C. Leaves rolled up and covered with hairs.
D. Leaves with stomata on the upper surface.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (leaves rolled up and covered with hairs) because: Hydrophytes are plants that live in wet or aquatic environments Leaves rolled up and covered with hairs is an adaptation of xerophytes (plants that live in very dry environments such as sand dunes) The other answers are incorrect because all the other features listed are features of hydrophytes: They have a reduced root and xylem system as they are living in an aquatic environment so have a plentiful supply of water They have large air spaces in the tissues for gas exchange They have stomata on their upper surface as they are often floating in water, so stomata on the upper surface of the leaf are easier for gas exchange

questions.stem:
The inheritance of Huntington's disease is determined by a single gene. This gene has a dominant allele and a recessive allele. The allele for Huntington’s is dominant to the allele for non-sufferers of the condition.
The diagram shows the inheritance of Huntington’s in a family.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/huntingtons.png)What is the probability that the next child from the same parents will have Huntington’s?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (50%) because: The parent without Huntington’s (non-Huntington’s) must be homozygous recessive (hh) The parent with Huntington’s must be heterozygous (Hh) as they have one child without the disease and the sufferer must have passed on a recessive allele The Punnett square for this will be: H h h Hh hh h Hh hh This shows a 50% chance of any child from this cross being a sufferer of the disease.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows four different types of human teeth. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/7-q13-teeth.png)Which teeth would be used to grind and chew food?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (1 and 2) because: 1 is a premolar tooth and 2 is a molar tooth. Premolars and molars have larger , flatter surfaces with ridges at the edges for chewing and grinding up food. B is incorrect because 3 is an incisor , which is chisel shaped for biting and cutting. C is incorrect because 1 (premolar) is also responsible for chewing and grinding of food. D is incorrect because 3 is an incisor , which is for biting and cutting while 4 is a canine , which is pointed for tearing, holding and biting.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Alkali metals is correct?
options: A. Potassium is more dense than lithium.
B. Lithium has a higher density than sodium.
C. Potassium is less reactive than sodium.
D. The melting point of sodium is higher than lithium.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The atomic number of the elements increases and their properties change as you move down Group I. Melting and boiling points and hardness decrease while their density increases . They become more  reactive due to increasing distance between the outermost  electrons and the nucleus, making it easier for the metals to lose their outer shell electron. Potassium is below lithium in Group I so its density is higher than that of lithium. B is incorrect as lithium is less dense than sodium as it is higher up in the group. C is incorrect as potassium is below sodium in Group I and is thus more  reactive . D is incorrect as sodium has a lower melting point than lithium since it is lower down the group.

questions.stem: What is the role of ligase enzymes in genetic engineering?
options: A. To insert plasmids into bacteria.
B. To join human DNA with plasmid DNA.
D. To cut open plasmid DNA.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (to join human DNA with plasmid DNA) because: The enzyme that can join complementary sticky ends created by the activity of restriction enzymes on plasmid and human DNA is called ligase ‘Sticky ends’ can complement base-pair with each other, but ligase joins the sugar-phosphate backbones of adjacent DNA molecules together A is incorrect because ligase enzyme is not used when plasmids are taken up by the bacteria. C is incorrect because the human gene is isolated using restriction enzymes that cut the DNA at specific base sequences. D is incorrect because restriction enzymes are used to cut the plasmid open to create sticky ends.

questions.stem:
Fig. 1 shows the path of light entering the front part of the eye of a person with normal vision, whilst looking at a close object.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/06/focus-1.png)Fig. 1
As people get older (typically 40+), their lenses lose flexibility and can't spring back into a round shape when looking at close objects.
Explain what effect a less flexible lens would have on the path of light.
questions.explanation: The effect a less flexible lens would have on the path of light is as follows... Any three from the following: The light is refracted by a smaller amount / narrower angle; [1 mark] As the lens is thin / stretched; [1 mark] Images / light rays are brought into focus behind the retina; [1 mark] So (close objects) appear blurred/fuzzy; [1 mark] [Total: 3 marks] To help you answer this question, think of the lens and path of light as being similar to when looking at a distant object but as the person is looking at a near object, the amount of light refraction is not sufficient. This condition is known as presbyopia and can be corrected by wearing reading glasses.

questions.stem:
The nephron consists of several different structures such as the Bowman's capsule and glomerulus.
Describe and explain how the structure of the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule help to remove urea from the bloodstream.
questions.explanation: The structure of the Bowman's capsule and glomerulus and how it facilitates the removal of urea from the bloodstream can be explained as follows... Any four of the following: The glomerulus consists of a knot/network of capillaries; [1 mark] The glomerulus sits inside the cup-shaped Bowman's capsule; [1 mark] The capillaries (of the glomerulus) are narrow which increase the pressure of the blood (moving through them); [1 mark] The Bowman's capsule and glomerulus let small molecules (such as urea) pass into the tubules (of the nephron); [1 mark] During the process of ultra filtration; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] It is very important to be able to relate the structure of the parts of the nephron to its function so make sure you familiarise yourself with this.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (5 days) because: At 5 days this would give you the highest yield of penicillin. Penicillin is produced in a batch culture so you would want to harvest with the highest yield possible. This is also the point at which the mass of living organisms has reduced.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: This is because diffusion is the movement of particles down a concentration gradient. It is a passive process that occurs whenever there is a concentration gradient. Osmosis is the diffusion of water through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.stem:

In reversible reactions, if the forward reaction is endothermic then the reverse reaction is exothermic (and vice versa). Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride turns blue to pink when water is added. B, C and D are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe the reaction.

questions.stem:
A person leaves a room and runs very fast for 200m. When the person stops running, his breathing rate and his heart rate remain high for several minutes.
Explain why the person’s breathing rate and heart rate remain high.
questions.explanation: The person's breathing rate and heart rate remain high because: Any four from the following: Takes time for...; [1 mark] ...oxygen debt (to be repaid); [1 mark] More oxygen needed; [1 mark] Lactic acid / lactate; [1 mark] Builds up in muscles / needs to be cleared away; [1 mark] Lactic acid is broken down / respired; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] When lactic acid is broken down in the liver it reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water, which can both be easily removed from the body.

questions.stem: Which name can be given to a group of organisms that have similar morphological features and can reproduce successfully to produce fertile offspring?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (species) because: Members of the same species usually look similar or share similar features, and crucially, can reproduce to produce offspring that can in turn go on to produce fertile offspring themselves. A is incorrect because a kingdom is an extremely large group containing different phyla. For example, animals make up one kingdom, plants make up another. B is incorrect because a genus is a group containing several different species with similar characteristics and evolutionary history. C is incorrect because a family is a taxonomic classification between order and genus; a family contains many different genera.

questions.stem:
An isotope of uranium is represented by the symbol:

Which of the answers below could be a different isotope of uranium?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: uranium has 92 protons . All isotopes of the same element must have the same number of protons. A is incorrect as this atom has 91 protons, which would make it an atom of the element protactinium. C is incorrect as the nucleon and proton numbers are the wrong way around. D is incorrect as this atom has 90 protons, which would make it an atom of the element thorium.

questions.stem:
The equation shows the formation of a polymer called Kevlar.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/q3-11-3-hard-cie-igcse-chemistry.png)Which row describes Kevlar?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | how the monomer is formed | type of polymer |
| A | addition polymerisation | polyamide |
| B | addition polymerisation | polyester |
| C | condensation polymerisation | polyamide |
| D | condensation polymerisation | polyester |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: There is a carboxylic acid group (-COOH) and an amine group(-NH 2 ) at either end. The link between these two functional groups is the amide link and each one is formed as a water molecule is lost, hence the name condensation polymerisation. There is a water molecule removed in the process shown in the question, therefore it is produced by condensation polymerisation. A and B are incorrect as water is formed when the amine and carboxylic groups join together meaning this process is a condensation reaction. In addition polymerisation there are no waste products. D is incorrect as Kevlar is held together by amide (peptide) links, whereas monomers of a polyester would consist of hydroxyl (-OH) and carboxylic acid (-COOH) groups and the polymer would be held together by ester links.

questions.stem:
Four foods were tested for the following food molecules:
• reducing sugar using Benedict’s reagent

• protein using Biuret solution

• fat using ethanol

• Vitamin C using DCPIP



|  |  |
|---|---|
|  | colour of food test result |
|  | brick-red/orange | purple/lilac | colourless | milky-white |
| A | ✔ | ✘ | ✔ | ✘ |
| B | ✔ | ✘ | ✘ | ✔ |
| C | ✘ | ✔ | ✔ | ✘ |
| D | ✘ | ✘ | ✔ | ✔ |
Which food contains sugar and Vitamin C?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Benedict’s solution tests for the presence of reducing sugars. A positive colour change indicating the presence of reducing sugar is from blue to brick red / orange (sometimes green if there is not a large amount of sugar present) DCPIP solution tests for the presence of Vitamin C. It contains a blue dye that in the presence of Vitamin C turns colourless, allowing the original colour of the solution being tested to be seen B is incorrect because this food sample contains sugar and lipids (fats and oils), as ethanol has shown a positive test result. In the presence of lipids ethanol changes from colourless to form a cloudy milky-white emulsion. C is incorrect because this food sample contains protein (due to the positive colour change of the Biuret solution from blue to purple/lilac) and Vitamin C. D is incorrect because this food sample contains Vitamin C and lipids.

questions.stem:
A student decided to investigate the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme lipase.
Five different test tubes are set up. Each test tube contains a mixture of the enzyme lipase and its substrate, a lipid.
Which condition should not be kept the same in each of the five test tubes?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (pH) because: If the condition being investigated is pH, then this is the independent  variable and should be different in each test tube to get a good range of results. A is incorrect because the temperature is one factor that can affect enzyme activity and should not be changed if pH is being altered. B is incorrect because the concentration of the enzyme is another factor that needs to be kept the same (not changed) to make the experiment fair as it can also affect enzyme activity. C is incorrect because the volume of the lipid solution is one of the things that needs to be kept the same to make the experiment valid; the more lipid (substrate) there is, the longer it will take for the reaction to complete.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The next steps in the method of preparing dry crystals of the soluble salt cobalt(II) chloride-6-water from the insoluble base cobalt(II) carbonate are: Filter / centrifuge / decant; [1 mark] (Partially) evaporate / heat / boil; [1 mark] Allow to crystallise / cool / let crystals form; [1 mark] Dry crystals / dry between filter paper / leave in a warm place to dry; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] The number of marks available should give you some indication of how much detail you need to give It can be useful to bullet point your answer so that your answer is concise Aim to get as many points as there are marks available

questions.stem:
Eukaryotic cells contain mitochondria (a mitochondrion is shown below).


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/mitochondrion-mitochondria-structure-mcq-1.png)Which diagram below correctly shows the position of mitochondria in a plant cell?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/1-2--image-3--cells.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Mitochondria are usually slightly smaller than chloroplasts and are found within the cytoplasm. Mitochondria have a highly folded internal membrane, whereas chloroplasts look like they contain stacks of pancakes (sometimes!). B is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the cell wall; in fact, no organelles are found within the cell wall. C is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the vacuole. D is incorrect because this cell is an animal cell. You can tell this because of the absence of a cell wall and vacuole.

questions.stem: What causes the diffusion of carbon dioxide out of a living cell?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Random movement of molecules) because: Molecules like carbon dioxide must be able to move to be able to diffuse. Individual molecules move about randomly, but overall net movement of a gas occurs from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration. A is incorrect because active transport requires protein molecules embedded within a membrane using energy released via respiration to move molecules deliberately into the cell (usually against a concentration gradient). C is incorrect because respiration as a chemical process produces the waste gas carbon dioxide, but the reaction isn’t responsible for the movement of the gas. D is incorrect because photosynthesis is a chemical process that requires carbon dioxide, and although a plant cell photosynthesising lowers the concentration of carbon dioxide inside the cell, it doesn’t cause the movement of carbon dioxide out of the cell.

questions.stem: Which of the structures below is best adapted for diffusion?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (ileum) because: The ileum is part of the small intestine where most food absorption occurs. The wall of the ileum is heavily folded; these finger-like folds are called villi (singular villus) which are externally covered by highly folded cells called microvilli. B and C are incorrect because the bronchioles and atria are not adapted for diffusion at all due to their thick walls. D is incorrect because even though a capillary is adapted for diffusion, it is not the best adapted from the listed structures. The ileum will collectively have a larger surface area for diffusion compared to one capillary.

questions.stem: Which statement is false?
options: A. Fatty acids are a type of lipid
C. A triglyceride consists of three fatty acids and one glycerol molecule
D. Amino acids each have a side group (R) that distinguishes them from other amino acids
questions.explanation: The false statement is A (Fatty acids are a type of lipid) because: Fatty acids are part of a lipid molecule, so cannot be a type of lipid. All the other statements about biological molecules are true.

In 1985 the fullerenes were discovered. They are solid forms of the element carbon. The structure of the C60 fullerene is given below.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/09/fullerene.png)i) In the C60 fullerene, how many other carbon atoms is each carbon atom bonded to?

 [1]
questions.explanation: i) In C 60 fullerene, each carbon is bonded to: 3 (other carbons); [1 mark] ii) In one molecule of fullerene there are: 70 (carbon atoms); [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] Looking at the diagram you can see that each carbon (circled) has 3 bonds  Although you aren't expected to be familiar with the structure of fullerene you should be used to seeing similar diagrams for the structure of diamond and graphite To figure out how many carbon atoms there are for part ii) carbon has an atomic mass of 12 Therefore 840 / 12 = 70

questions.stem:
Which of the following options is the best explanation for the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
Chlorophyll...
options: A. transfers light energy from the Sun because it has magnesium ions
B. transfers chemical potential energy from sunlight into organic molecules which can be used to synthesise carbohydrates such as glucose
C. transfers light energy from the Sun into chemical energy in inorganic molecules which can be used for growth
D. transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates) because: chlorophyll absorbs light energy (from the Sun or artificial light sources) light energy is used to drive a reaction between water and carbon dioxide, producing glucose (a carbohydrate) glucose can be converted into other carbohydrates, such as sucrose, starch and cellulose A is incorrect because chlorophyll molecules do contain magnesium ions, but this doesn’t outline its role in photosynthesis. B is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs light energy, not chemical potential energy, to drive the synthesis of organic molecules such as glucose (light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy stored in the bonds of glucose molecules). C is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs energy from sunlight to drive reactions between inorganic molecules (carbon dioxide and water) to produce glucose (an organic molecule). Glucose can then be converted into other molecules (such as amino acids) which are used in growth.

questions.stem:
An experiment is set up with four test tubes as shown in the diagram below. 
All four test tubes are left in sunlight for 6 hours. 
Which test tube would contain the least amount of dissolved carbon dioxide after 6 hours?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/tv02bT3k_picture2.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The test tube contains pondweed, which in the presence of light can photosynthesise . As a result, carbon dioxide levels in the water will decrease A carbon dioxide diffusion gradient is set up between the water and the leaves  as photosynthesis occurs, resulting in diffusion of carbon dioxide into the leaf for photosynthesis A is incorrect because there is nothing in the test tube photosynthesising or respiring, so the concentration of carbon dioxide in the water will not change. B is incorrect because although the pondweed in the test tube will be photosynthesising and therefore decreasing the carbon dioxide concentration of the water, the snail will be respiring and so releasing carbon dioxide. There will be more carbon dioxide than in test tube C . D is incorrect because the test tube contains a snail which will be respiring and therefore releasing carbon dioxide into the water, increasing the overall amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the function of vitamin D in a human?
options: A. Vitamin D forms an essential part of collagen protein which is the main component of skin, hair and nails.
B. Vitamin D is needed for strong bones and teeth and a deficiency may lead to osteoporosis later in life.
C. Vitamin D assists with the absorption of calcium and is therefore needed to build strong bones and teeth.
D. Vitamin D is an important component of haemoglobin which is needed for the transport of oxygen to the cells.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Vitamin D assists with the absorption of calcium and is therefore needed to build strong bones and teeth.) because: Vitamin D facilitates the absorption of calcium into bones and teeth, which is required to provide strength to these parts. Without sufficient vitamin D intake, a child may develop rickets where the bones develop poorly. A is incorrect because vitamin C is needed to make collagen, not vitamin D. B is incorrect because even though vitamin D is needed for strong bones and teeth, a deficiency will not lead to osteoporosis later in life. That is a characteristic of a calcium deficiency. D is incorrect because iron is an important component of haemoglobin and therefore plays a role in the transport of oxygen in the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of physical digestion?
options: A. Breaking food up into smaller pieces by chewing it.
B. Starch being broken down into glucose molecules.
C. Food being churned when the muscles in the stomach lining contracts.
D. Bile breaking large fat droplets up into smaller ones during emulsification.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Starch being broken down into glucose molecules.) because: The digestion of starch involves enzymes that break large insoluble starch molecules up into smaller soluble glucose molecules. Whenever enzymes are involved then it is an example of chemical digestion, not physical digestion. A , B and D are incorrect because these are all examples of physical digestion where large food particles are mechanically broken down into smaller particles. This is done to increase the surface area on which the digestive enzymes can work during chemical digestion to change large insoluble molecules into smaller soluble ones.

questions.stem:
Hydrogen chloride gas is strong-smelling, denser than air and soluble in water. A sample of hydrogen chloride gas can be prepared by adding concentrated sulfuric acid to sodium chloride. Study the diagram of the apparatus used.

questions.explanation: The correct labels in the boxes are: Top box = sulfuric acid; [1 mark] Bottom box = sodium chloride; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] The question tells you that the chemicals being reacted together are sodium chloride and sulfuric acid Sodium chloride is a solid, and therefore the bottom box Sulfuric acid is a liquid, and therefore the top box

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows how the rate of photosynthesis is affected by different conditions.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/6-q5-limiting-factors.png)What of the following correctly identifies the limiting factor for photosynthesis at the three points on the graph?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| A | light intensity | light intensity | carbon dioxide concentration |
| B | temperature | temperature | light intensity |
| C | light intensity | temperature | carbon dioxide concentration |
| D | light intensity | carbon dioxide concentration | temperature |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: At 1, the rate of photosynthesis has yet to level off (neither temperature nor concentration of carbon dioxide are limiting in this experiment) so light intensity is still the limiting factor At 2, the rate of photosynthesis is no longer increasing even though the light intensity is still increasing , so some other factor is limiting (in the table, we can see the temperature for experiment 2 is 20℃, so the temperature is the limiting factor) At 3, the rate of photosynthesis is no longer increasing even though the light intensity is still increasing, so some other factor is limiting (in the table, we can see the carbon dioxide concentration is lower than other experiments, so carbon dioxide concentration is the limiting factor) A is incorrect because temperature is the limiting factor for experiment 2, not light intensity. B is incorrect because light intensity is the limiting factor in experiment 1, not temperature. D is incorrect because temperature is the limiting factor for experiment 2, and carbon  dioxide is the limiting factor for experiment 3.

questions.stem:
The human body has a number of barriers to prevent infection by pathogens some of which are listed below.
• Skin

• Mucus

• Hairs in the nose

• Antibodies

• Stomach acid

Which of these are examples of mechanical barriers?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. (1 and 3) because: The skin and hairs in the nose forms a physical barrier that makes it more difficult for pathogens to enter the body. B and C are incorrect because mucus (2) is an example of a chemical barrier while antibodies (4) are produced by lymphocytes in response to foreign antigens entering the body, they do not act as a barrier. D is incorrect because stomach acid (5) is another example of a chemical barrier, not a mechanical one.
