questions.stem: What is a pathogen?
options: B. A phagocyte that engulfs bacteria
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. (A disease-causing organism) because: A pathogen is a microorganism that infects another organism where it replicates / multiplies and causes disease. A is incorrect because a transmissible disease is caused by a pathogen that can spread from one organism to another (e.g. Covid-19 is a transmissible disease caused by the pathogenic SARS-CoV-2 virus). B is incorrect because phagocytes are part of the immune system responsible for destroying pathogens that have entered the body. D is incorrect because not all bacteria (or microorganisms for that matter) are pathogenic. The human digestive system and skin, contains huge numbers of beneficial bacteria that help prevent infection (by competing with pathogens for resources).

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Magnetic field lines always go from the north pole to the south pole This eliminates options B and C which have the wrong direction for the magnetic field arrows The strength of the magnetic field is shown by the spacing of the magnetic field lines If the magnetic field lines are close together then the magnetic field will be stronger The field lines in option D are closer than A , so D has the stronger magnetic field

questions.stem: Which of the following organs are responsible for removing excretory products from the blood?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (kidneys and lungs) because: The kidneys remove urea, excess salts and water from the blood. The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the blood due to the concentration gradient set up between the air in the lungs and the carbon dioxide in the blood. This is maintained by breathing. A is incorrect because the bladder is not responsible for removing excretory products from the blood , it removes it from the body. C is incorrect because the liver is responsible for producing many of the excretory products, but it is not directly responsible for the excretion of these products. D is incorrect because neither the bladder nor liver will remove excretory products from the blood for excretion as mentioned above.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are reasons for the evolution of reflex arcs in the mammalian nervous system?
• To prevent harm or damage to an organism.

• To provide a rapid response to dangerous situations.

• To allow a degree of choice to an organism about response.

• To allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (1 and 2 are correct) because: Statement 1 (to prevent harm or damage to an organism) is correct because an automatic, rapid response to a dangerous stimulus cuts the reaction time and allows less damage to be sustained before a response takes place Statement 2 (to provide a rapid response to dangerous situations) is correct, linked to the explanation for Statement 1 Statement 3 (to allow a degree of choice to an organism about response) is incorrect because reflexes are involuntary - they take place with no choice of conscious thought. Statement 4 (to allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated) is incorrect because a dangerous stimulus cannot be ignored, nor can one be eliminated; that would be outside an organism's ability to control events!

questions.stem:
One magnesium atom reacts with two chlorine atoms to form the ionic compound, MgCl2.
Which row shows the correct electron change taking place for chlorine and the correct formula of the ion formed?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | electron change | formula of ion formed |
| A | electron lost | Cl - |
| B | electron gained | Cl 2- |
| C | electron gained | Cl - |
| D | electron lost | Cl 2- |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Non-metals , such as chlorine, gain electrons when forming ionic compounds Chlorine is in Group VII , so it needs to gain one electron to reach a stable noble gas electron configuration Therefore, the answer is Cl - A and D are incorrect because magnesium is the element that will lose electrons to form an ionic bond with chlorine B is incorrect because chlorine cannot acquire a 2- charge because it just needs one electron to have a full outer shell. Magnesium loses two electrons to become Mg 2+ . Each chlorine atom gains one electron to become Cl - . Chlorine (atom) is not the same as chloride (ion) . This mix-up is very common in exams and it can lead you to lose easy marks. Always double check the names

questions.stem:
Three statements about the electrolysis of molten lead (II) bromide are listed.
• A green gas is produced at the negative electrode.

• Lead ions will gain electrons at the cathode.

• The electrodes for the electrolysis must be from an inert material, such as graphite.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Statement 1 is incorrect During the electrolysis, bromine gas is produced at the anode ( positive electrode ) Bromine gas is red-brown A green gas refers to chlorine Statement 2 is correct At the cathode ( negative electrode ), lead ions (Pb 2+ ) from the the molten lead bromide will gain two electrons When lead is formed a shiny grey liquid will be produced at the electrode Statement 3 is correct The electrodes must be inert materials, such as graphite, so they do not react during the electrolysis Use the PANIC mnemonic to remember which electrode is the positive and which is the negative: Positive (is) Anode Negative Is Cathode

questions.stem:
Penicillin is an antibiotic that prevents bacteria growing by stopping them from forming cell walls.
Why does penicillin not affect viruses?
options: A. Viruses do not have cell walls.
B. Viruses do not contain cytoplasm.
C. Viruses become resistant to penicillin.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Viruses are technically not living cells, this means that they are not affected by antibiotics. Viruses do not have cell walls or carry out cellular functions. Antibiotics work by disrupting cell chemical reactions or the production of cell walls. B is incorrect because viruses do not contain cytoplasm, and antibiotics don’t affect cytoplasm. C is incorrect because penicillin does not work on viruses. D is incorrect because this is correct as viruses use the host cell to reproduce rapidly. It is not relevant to why penicillin will not work on viruses, however.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows the female reproductive system.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/image-7.png)After ejaculation, which pathway will the male gamete take to fuse with the egg?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. (Vagina →  cervix   → uterus  → oviduct) because: Ejaculation takes place in the vagina; from there sperm travels through the cervix, into the uterus and then to the oviduct where (if it has been released) an egg can be fertilised. B and D are incorrect because they would both be correct paths of an egg that was not fertilised by a sperm cell. C is incorrect because the sperm will need to go through the cervix before it can enter the uterus.

questions.stem:
An iron tray is electroplated with pure silver to improve its appearance. The diagram shows the electrochemical cell with labels X, Y and Z.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/02/32554-paper-1-q13-image-1.png)Which row correctly identifies X, Y, and the electrolyte Z?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Electrode X (at the negative terminal) | Electrode Y (at the positive terminal) | Electrolyte Z |
| A | Pure silver | Iron tray | Silver nitrate |
| B | Pure silver | Iron tray | Iron (II) chloride |
| C | Iron tray | Pure silver | Silver nitrate |
| D | Iron tray | Pure silver | Silver chloride |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Electrode X (Cathode): This is connected to the negative terminal In electroplating, the object to be coated (the iron tray) must be the cathode so that positive metal ions are attracted to it Electrode Y (Anode): This is connected to the positive terminal The anode must be made of the pure metal you are using for the coating (silver) As the reaction proceeds, the silver anode dissolves to replace the silver ions in the solution Electrolyte Z: This must be a soluble salt of the plating metal Silver nitrate is the standard choice Silver chloride ( Choice D ) is incorrect because it is insoluble and will not conduct electricity in this setup

questions.stem:
Males and females have a unique set of chromosomes. 
What is the correct combination of male and female chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (males XY, females XX) because: The male sex chromosomes are inherited as an X and a Y chromosomes - the X from the mother and the Y from the father, giving a male the chromosomes XY. A female inherits an X from the mother and another X from the father, giving the chromosomes XX as a female.

questions.stem:
The graph below shows the growth of the human population globally since 1630.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/-1RXSz0K_image-2-1.png)Which of the following options represents the longest time period taken for the population of humans to double?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (200 years) because: Between 1630 and 1830 the population increased from 500 million to 1000 million. This is the longest time period represented on the graph for the population to double. After 1830 there was rapid growth of the human population, the time for the population to double was significantly less.

questions.stem:
Albinism is a condition where the pigment melanin does not get produced in the skin, hair and eyes. This is an inherited condition that is caused by a recessive allele.
If both parents have albinism what are the chances of the offspring being an albino child?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (100%) because: If both parents have the condition then they will both have the same genotype : homozygous recessive Both parents only have (two) copies of the recessive allele; therefore the gametes formed by meiosis in each parent will always contain a recessive allele, therefore the only possible genotype for any offspring from these parents will be homozygous recessive Note - in genetics it is key to know your definitions! Gene - section of the chromosome that codes for a particular characteristic Allele - alternative version of a gene Genotype -  the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present Phenotype - the observable features (physical characteristics) of an organism Homozygous - having two identical alleles for the same gene Heterozygous - has two different alleles for a particular gene

questions.stem: What is a mutation?
options: A. A process used in genetic engineering.
B. A type of continuous variation.
C. A condition caused by a dominant allele.
D. A change in a gene.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (a change in a gene) because: The definition of a mutation is the change in the base sequence of DNA (which is a more detailed way of saying a change in a gene) This is how we get different versions of the same genes known as alleles Mutations are the basis of genetic variation A is incorrect because genetic engineering is a process that involves inserting a gene into an organism (from another) B is incorrect because continuous variation is a type of variation that has a range of phenotypes often due to both genetic and environmental factors. C is incorrect because a dominant allele is a version of a gene that will always be expressed in the phenotype of an organism.

questions.stem:
The image shows a food web. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/lG-mZtON_image-5.png)Which organism, from the food web, feeds on the greatest variety of organisms?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (crabs) because: Crabs feed on mussels, lugworms and limpets. This gives them the largest range of food sources (3 in all) in this food web. This would mean that they have the greatest chance of survival if one of their food sources decreased in number. A is incorrect because whelks only have one source of food, mussels. C is incorrect because limpets only have one source of food, sea lettuce. D is incorrect because mussels only have one source of food, small invertebrates.

questions.stem: Which of these statements correctly describes genetic engineering?
options: A. Only breeding from crop plants that are resistant to pests.
B. Altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides.
C. Using yeast to produce ethanol.
D. Production of insulin in the pancreas.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides) because: Genetic engineering is the process of altering DNA to include new genes or sequences of DNA. This will give the modified organism new characteristics that may increase yield or increase resistance to chemicals. A is incorrect because this process describes selective breeding .  Selective breeding is the use of organisms with a particular characteristic in breeding so that the offspring have the trait that you desire. C is incorrect because this process describes fermentation . This is a natural process that has been exploited for centuries to produce bread and beer. D is incorrect because this is a natural process that occurs normally in healthy individuals.

questions.stem:
The table shows the change in temperature of four different reactions W, X, Y and Z.


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | initial  temperature /  °C | final  temperature /  °C |
| W | 10 | 20 |
| X | 23 | 25 |
| Y | 15 | 13 |
| Z | 22 | 12 |
Which row  is correct?
options: A. W is the most exothermic reaction.
B. W and X are endothermic reactions.
C. Z is the most exothermic reaction.
D. Y and Z are exothermic reactions.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A There is an increase in temperature in exothermic reactions, while there is a decrease in temperature in endothermic reactions Work out the change in temperature for each reaction Temperature change for W Temperature change for X Temperature change for Y Temperature change for Z W has the largest positive temperature increase ( +10 °C ), so it releases the most amount of energy to the surroundings Therefore, W is the most exothermic reaction B is incorrect because both W and X increase in temperature, so they are exothermic, not endothermic C is incorrect because Z has a temperature decrease (−10°C), so it is endothermic D is incorrect because both Y and Z decrease in temperature, so they are endothermic, not exothermic

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct example of a population?
options: A. All the animals in a forest.
B. All the goldfish in a pond.
C. All the species of animals in Europe.
D. All the people born in Scotland over a 150-year period.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: The definition of a population is 'the same species living in the same habitat at the same time'. A is incorrect because this answer refers to ‘all the animals’, it is highly unlikely all of the animals in a forest belong to the same species, so this is not a definition of a population. C is incorrect because this refers to more than one species so is not the definition of population. D is incorrect because while this refers to a number of organisms of the same species this is not at the same time as over 150 years, some of the people will have died and other will have been born.

questions.stem:
Water is important for living organisms as many substances are able to dissolve in it.
Give two examples of the importance of water as a solvent in living organisms.
questions.explanation: The importance of water as a solvent in living organisms includes... Any two of the following: Dissolved substances can be easily transported around organisms OR a named example e.g. xylem transporting water and mineral ions / phloem transporting sucrose and amino acids / blood transporting dissolved food molecules; [1 mark] Digested food molecules in the alimentary canal dissolve in water to be absorbed into the blood (for transport to cells); [1 mark] Toxic substances/urea / substances in excess can dissolve in water to be (easily) excreted in urine; [1 mark] Ensures that metabolic reactions can occur (in solution) within cells; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] Make sure to familiarise yourself with the importance of water as a solvent in living organisms as this is a question you may come across in an exam paper.

questions.stem:
Fig. 1 shows sections of two flowers, K and L, from the same species.

• protect the bud of the flower

questions.explanation: (i) An ovule and a petal on flower L can be identified as follows:  The most common error here is to label the ovary rather than the ovule; be sure to know the difference between the two. (ii) The names of the following flower parts are as follows: Produce ovules = carpel / ovary; [1 mark] Protect the bud on the flower = sepal; [1 mark] The most common error here is to say that the petal protects the bud; the petal's job is to attract insect pollinators. [Total: 4 marks]

questions.stem:
The oil palm is a tree that grows in tropical areas, whose oil has many uses in cooking, food preparation and as a detergent. It is also used in the manufacture of biofuels.
Fig. 1 shows the annual production of palm oil in Colombia (South America) since 2010.

Show your working and give your answer in thousands of metric tonnes per year.
questions.explanation: The mean increase in palm oil production per year for the three year period 2014 to 2017 is calculated as: Difference = (1 625 - 1 100) = 525 (000 metric tonnes); [1 mark] Mean increase = 525 ÷ 3 = 175 (000 metric tonnes); [1 mark] Full marks awarded for the correct answer in the absence of other calculations [Total: 2 marks]  The most common error in the question of this kind is to add up palm oil production for all 3 years and divide by 3, giving a value for mean production rather than mean increase. Avoid another common error, which is to subtract the value for 2014 from that for 2017 but then not to divide by 3. Take care to read the graph accurately, in particularly the axes.

Gaining oxygen is oxidation B and C are incorrect because  ZnSO 4 and Cu are products of the reaction. (ZnSO 4 ) is a product of oxidation. C (Cu) is the product of reduction.

B. A solution prepared with YO 3 will turn blue if drops of thymolphthalein are added
C. A solution prepared with X 2 O will have a pH lower than 7
D. A solution prepared with X 2 O  will turn blue litmus paper to red
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A X is on the left of the Periodic Table, so it's a metal X is in Group I where all the elements have a valency of I Therefore, it will form metal oxides of the general formula X 2 O , such as Na 2 O or K 2 O When a metal oxide is dissolved in water form a basic solution (pH >7) Y is on the right of the Periodic Table, so it's a non-metal Y can react with oxygen to form non-metal oxides When a non-metal oxide is dissolved in water, it forms an an acidic solution (pH < 7) Therefore, YO 3  is an acidic oxide B is incorrect because YO 3 is an acidic oxide, acidic solutions are colourless with thymolphthalein; while basic solutions are blue C is incorrect because X is a metal, so X 2 O forms a basic oxide . When mixed with water, the solution will have a pH above 7 , not below D is incorrect because X 2 O is a basic oxide. The solution prepared would turn red litmus paper to blue , not blue litmus to red

questions.stem:
Which of the following descriptions are correctly matched to the different stages of food breakdown?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | absorption | assimilation | egestion |
| A | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| B | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| C | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| D | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Absorption is the movement of soluble food molecules and ions through the intestinal wall into the blood to be transported to the cells. Once it reaches the cells these food molecules and ions will cross the cell membrane during assimilation in order to become part of the cell. Any food that hasn't been digested or absorbed will move along the alimentary canal and leave the body through the anus during egestion . A is incorrect because egestion does not involve excretion. The waste products that leave the body during the process of excretion comes from metabolic reactions that occur within cells . Waste products that leave the body during egestion was created outside cells . C is incorrect because the description of absorption and assimilation has been switched around. D is incorrect because all three descriptions is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

questions.stem:
Adaptive features are defined as the inherited features of an organism that increase its fitness.
State what is meant by fitness in this context.
questions.explanation: In this context, fitness means: (The probability that an organism will) survive AND reproduce; [1 mark] [Total: 1 mark] Just mentioning 'survival' won't be enough to gain the mark on this question. This is because the organisms of a species may well be able to survive, but unless they can reproduce , then the species is effectively extinct; it will only take until the end of those individuals' natural lives and there won't be any more individuals to keep the species going. This question covers core knowledge taken from an extended only paper 4 question.

questions.stem: Which name can be given to a group of organisms that have similar morphological features and can reproduce successfully to produce fertile offspring?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (species) because: Members of the same species usually look similar or share similar features, and crucially, can reproduce to produce offspring that can in turn go on to produce fertile offspring themselves. A is incorrect because a kingdom is an extremely large group containing different phyla. For example, animals make up one kingdom, plants make up another. B is incorrect because a genus is a group containing several different species with similar characteristics and evolutionary history. C is incorrect because a family is a taxonomic classification between order and genus; a family contains many different genera.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A ( F. americana ) because: The leaf shown is not in one piece, the start of the question states ‘the diagram shows a leaf’ which means a single leaf. Therefore this leaf is in more than one piece. The leaf edge is smooth.

questions.stem: Which of the following depicts the correct order of stages in the formation of a blood clot?
options: A. soluble fibrin → insoluble fibrinogen → blood clot
B. soluble fibrinogen → insoluble fibrin → blood clot
C. insoluble fibrin → soluble fibrinogen → blood clot
D. insoluble fibrinogen → soluble fibrin→ blood clot
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (soluble fibrinogen → insoluble fibrin → blood clot) because: When a blood vessel is broken/ damaged , a series of reactions occur within the blood plasma This results in an enzyme becoming activated which converts soluble  fibrinogen (present in the blood plasma) into insoluble  fibrin Strands of insoluble fibrin trap red blood in a mesh -like structure which forms a clot over the damaged area

questions.stem: Which of the following terms would be correct to describe a leaf, a root and stem?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (organ) because: All three structures in the question are organs. An organ is a group of two or more tissues working together to carry out a particular function. A is incorrect because each of the leaves, stems and roots are made up of thousands of different cells all working together. B is incorrect because the leaf is made from palisade & spongy mesophyll tissue, epidermal tissue and vascular tissue functioning together to allow a plant to photosynthesise. The roots and stem are made from vascular (transport) tissue which work together to transport substances around the plant. D is incorrect because together plants have two organ systems. The shoot organ system in a plant is made from leaves, stems, buds, fruits and flowers. The root organ system of most plants are all the parts that are underground.

questions.stem:
Eukaryotic cells contain mitochondria (a mitochondrion is shown below).


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/mitochondrion-mitochondria-structure-mcq-1.png)Which diagram below correctly shows the position of mitochondria in a plant cell?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/1-2--image-3--cells.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Mitochondria are usually slightly smaller than chloroplasts and are found within the cytoplasm. Mitochondria have a highly folded internal membrane, whereas chloroplasts look like they contain stacks of pancakes (sometimes!). B is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the cell wall; in fact, no organelles are found within the cell wall. C is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the vacuole. D is incorrect because this cell is an animal cell. You can tell this because of the absence of a cell wall and vacuole.

questions.stem:
A number of red blood cells were immersed in pure water before being observed under a microscope. There was a dramatic change in their appearance. 
Which row of the table below correctly describes what happened to the red blood cells?


|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | direction of water movement | from higher to lower solute concentration | from higher to lower water potential | effect |
| A | in | ✓ | X | cells burst |
| B | in | X | ✓ | cells burst |
| C | out | ✓ | X | cells shrink |
| D | out | ✓ | ✓ | cells shrink |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Pure water has a solute concentration of zero and has the highest possible water potential Water will therefore move into red blood cells by osmosis when they are placed in pure water Water moves from low to high solute concentration and from high to  low water potential through a partially permeable membrane This will cause the cells to swell and eventually burst

questions.stem:
A student prepares pure hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals from copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid.
Which row shows the correct order of steps for this preparation?
options: A. add excess copper(II) oxide → filter → evaporate filtrate to point of crystallisation → cool
B. add excess copper(II) oxide → evaporate mixture to point of crystallisation → filter → cool
C. add excess copper(II) oxide → filter → heat filtrate until dry → cool
D. add excess copper(II) oxide → evaporate mixture until dry → cool → filter
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A This option shows the steps in order for preparing hydrated crystals of copper (II) sulphate Add excess copper(II) oxide to ensure all sulfuric acid reacts Filter to remove unreacted (excess) copper(II) oxide Evaporate the filtrate to the point of crystallisation (do not dry it because otherwise it will become anhydrous copper (II) sulphate) Cool so hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals form B & D are incorrect because excess copper(II) oxide (a solid) is still present in the mixture, so it needs to be removed before heating. Therefore, it must be the second step C is incorrect because heating until dry removes water of crystallisation, so hydrated crystals cannot form

questions.stem:
The effect of pH on the rate of reaction of three different enzymes is shown in the graph below.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/5-q11-graph-ph.png)What does the graph show?
options: A. Each enzyme works best over a narrow temperature range.
B. Most enzymes work best around a neutral pH.
C. Enzymes work better in acidic conditions.
D. Each enzyme works best at a different pH.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (Each enzyme works best at a different pH) because: For enzyme 1, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 1.5, making this its optimum pH. For enzyme 2, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 7, making this its optimum pH. And for enzyme 3, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 14, making this its optimum pH. A is incorrect because the graph gives no information about temperature. B is incorrect because only enzyme 2 works best in neutral conditions. C is incorrect because only enzyme 1 works best in acidic conditions.

questions.stem:
Three statements about metals are listed.

• Metals react with acids to form salt and water.

• Copper is used in electrical wires because of its malleable and a good electricity conductor

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Statement 1 is incorrect Aluminium is used for aircraft due to its low density, not high density, even though it has good resistance Statement 2 is incorrect Metals react with acids to form salt and hydrogen, not water Statement 3 is correct Copper is malleable and a good conductor of electricity These properties allow copper to be used in electrical wiring Therefore, only statement 3 is correct

questions.stem:
Students were discussing how to remember the difference between two groups of cells, ‘many, minute and motile’ or ‘few, fat and fixed’.
What group of cells were they referring to?
options: C. Red and white blood cells
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. (Male and female gametes) because: ‘Many, minute and motile’ refers to sperm cells. They are produced in very large numbers and are much smaller than the ovum (the egg) - they are much less energy intensive to produce which is why more of them can be made. They also have a tail to swim to the ovum ‘Few, fat and fixed’ refers to an ovum (egg cell). Generally, only one egg is released each month in the menstrual cycle . They are much larger than sperm cells and are unable to move independently, instead, they rely on the ciliated cells in the oviduct to waft them through to the uterus A common misconception here is that these statements are referring to animal and plant cells, students often think of animal cells being smaller and motile and plant cells being large and fixed.

questions.stem:
The pH of an enzyme controlled reaction is decreased by a pH of 2. 
How does this affect the rate of the reaction?
options: A. It has no effect on the rate.
B. It always decreases the rate.
C. It always increases the rate.
D. It may increase or decrease the rate .
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (It may increase or decrease the rate) because: Whether the rate of enzyme activity increases or decreases depends on what the optimum pH for the enzyme is. In mammals, it would depend if the enzyme acts inside cells, or if it were a digestive enzyme If the increase in pH takes the pH away from the optimum in either direction, then the rate will slow down If the increase in pH moves the pH towards the optimum, then the rate will increase The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly state how changing the pH will affect the rate of reaction.

questions.stem:
A student ate a meal which contained a type of biomolecule, X.
The digestion of biomolecule X started in the mouth, and finished in the duodenum.
What is the product of the digestion of biomolecule X?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Glucose) because: Starch , a large biomolecule, is made from many molecules of glucose molecules bonded together. Salivary  amylase , an enzyme produced by the salivary glands, acts on starch and breaks it down into maltose (a disaccharide). Amylase is also produced by the pancreas , to help digest any remaining starch in the small intestine. Maltose is broken down by the enzyme maltase (which is found in the lining of the small intestine), producing glucose molecules. A and B are incorrect because amino acids are the product of protein digestion, which begins in the stomach, not the mouth. D is incorrect because starch was the starting molecule in this process (starch is a polymer of glucose molecules).

questions.stem:
W, X, Y and Z are metals. 
A student investigates the reactivity of these elements with dilute hydrochloric acid. The table shows the observations at room temperature.


|  |  |
|---|---|
| metal | observation |
| W | Slow reaction |
| X | Violent reaction |
| Y | Very slow reaction |
| Z | No reaction |
Which row correctly identifies W, X, Y and Z?


|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | W | X | Y | Z |
| A | iron | potassium | silver | aluminium |
| B | iron | potassium | aluminium | silver |
| C | aluminium | potassium | iron | silver |
| D | aluminium | potassium | silver | iron |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Considering the reactivity series: K > Al > Fe > H > Ag A metal above hydrogen reacts with hydrochloric acid, and the higher it is, the faster the reaction Potassium reacts very violently with hydrochloric acid because it is at the top of the reactivity series, so X must be potassium . Silver does not react with hydrochloric acid at all because it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so Z must be silver Aluminium and iron are both above hydrogen, so they do react with hydrochloric acid, but aluminium is more reactive than iron. This means aluminium reacts faster than iron. Therefore, W (slow reaction) is aluminium and Y (very slow reaction) is iron A is incorrect because silver would not show a very slow reaction, it does not react at all B is incorrect because aluminium reacts faster than iron, not slower D is incorrect because silver should not react with acid at all; iron does react, so "no reaction" for iron is wrong

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows four different types of human teeth. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/7-q13-teeth.png)Which teeth would be used to grind and chew food?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (1 and 2) because: 1 is a premolar tooth and 2 is a molar tooth. Premolars and molars have larger , flatter surfaces with ridges at the edges for chewing and grinding up food. B is incorrect because 3 is an incisor , which is chisel shaped for biting and cutting. C is incorrect because 1 (premolar) is also responsible for chewing and grinding of food. D is incorrect because 3 is an incisor , which is for biting and cutting while 4 is a canine , which is pointed for tearing, holding and biting.

questions.stem:
A student collected some of the solution from the phloem in the stem of a plant. 
Which of the following would be present in the liquid?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Amino acids would be the only substance from the options given to move through the phloem (as well as sucrose). A is incorrect because glucose is never transported through the phloem; however, sucrose (a disaccharide that contains one glucose molecule) is transported through the phloem. B and D are incorrect because starch and cellulose are large biomolecules that are insoluble in water, therefore they cannot be moved around the plant.

questions.stem:
Water from a reservoir contains insoluble solids and harmful microbes. The water must be treated to make it safe for the domestic water supply.
Which row shows the correct order of the stages used to treat the water?
options: A. filtration of big insoluble particles → filtration of small insoluble particles → sedimentation → chlorination
B. filtration of big insoluble particles  → sedimentation → chlorination → filtration of small insoluble particles
C. filtration of big insoluble particles → sedimentation → filtration of small insoluble particles →  chlorination
D. filtration of big insoluble particles →   chlorination → sedimentation → filtration of small insoluble particles
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Water from reservoir can contain big insoluble particles, big insoluble particles and microbes Filtration of big insoluble particles is done first to remove large solids such as leaves or rocks This will prevent damaging or blockage in later stages of the treatment Sedimentation allows smaller suspended solids to settle under gravity because they are denser than water This is done before the filtration of small particles to make the filtration of small particles more effective If the fine filtration were done first, the filter can block quickly, reducing the efficiency Once the particles settle down by the action of gravity, filtration of small insoluble particles is performed This removes remaining fine particles that did not settle in the sedimentation Chlorination is carried out last to kill harmful microorganisms Doing this earlier would be ineffective because particles can protect microbes from chlorine Therefore, the correct order is filtration of big insoluble particles → sedimentation → filtration of small insoluble particles →  chlorination A is incorrect because sedimentation is placed after filtration of small particles, but particles must settle before fine filtration is effective B is incorrect because chlorination is carried out before final filtration, which can remove chlorine and reduce disinfection effectiveness D is incorrect because chlorination is done too early and insoluble solids would reduce its ability to kill microbes

questions.stem:
The data in the graph shows the effect of an antibiotic on the population of bacteria in the blood.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/aaI_~vWY_image-1.png)What can be concluded from the data in the graph?
options: A. Antibiotics take 10 days to kill all bacteria.
B. Antibiotics cause a reduction in division of bacteria.
C. Antibiotics are effective against viral and bacterial infections.
D. Before the start of the antibiotic treatment the bacterial population was increasing.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The bacterial population is increasing before the patient starts to take antibiotics. This can be seen in the graph. A is incorrect because from the graph the bacteria population has decreased to 0 by 6.5 days after starting the treatment with antibiotics. B is incorrect because you can’t see how the antibiotic works on the bacteria from the graph. C is incorrect because antibiotics are not effective against viruses - the graph only shows the effect on bacterial populations.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases can be transmitted by contact with contaminated surfaces?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (Salmonella and athletes foot) because: Both these diseases are transmitted when a person comes into contact with a surface that contains these pathogens. A is incorrect because malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. B is incorrect because typhoid is transmitted by the consumption of water or food contaminated with the faeces of people infected with typhoid. C is incorrect because influenza spreads by inhaling droplets in the air carrying the virus while dengue fever is spread by the bite of a specific species of mosquito ( Aedes aegypti ).

questions.stem:
Passive and active immunity have which of the following features in common?
• They are always long-term.

• They always involve the activity of memory cells.

• They involve antibodies.

• They can be acquired by vaccination.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (3 only) because: Both active and passive immunity involve antibodies being present to help the immune system (particularly phagocytes) fight an infectious pathogen causing disease In active immunity, the antibodies are acquired by having memory cells present in the body (as a result of prior infection with the pathogen or vaccination) which can make them, whereas in passive immunity the antibodies are acquired directly from another person either through an infusion of blood plasma,  or passed from mother to baby via breast milk A is incorrect because long-term effects and the activity of memory cells only apply in cases of active immunity. C is incorrect because memory cells are not involved in passive immunity. D is incorrect because only active immunity is developed by vaccination.

Four different stages in one heartbeat are shown in the diagram below.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/9-q13-heart-cycle.png)Which of the following depicts a correct order of stages?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (X → Z → W → Y) because: Stage X – blood enters the atria Stage Z – the walls of the atria contract and blood moves into the ventricles Stage W – the walls of the ventricles contract and blood is pushed up through the valves into the arteries Stage Y – the arteries carry blood away from the heart and more blood is carried towards the heart in the veins

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows a cross-section through an alveolus and a capillary.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/11--image-6-alveolus-and-capillary.png)Why does oxygen move from P to Q?
options: A. The concentration of carbon dioxide is lower in the alveolus than in the blood.
B. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than in the air in the capillary.
C. Oxygen must replace carbon dioxide.
D. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus) because: Blood is deoxygenated when it enters the lung capillaries, therefore there is an oxygen concentration gradient between P and Q. There is a higher  concentration of oxygen in the air in the alveolus than in the  blood , leading to diffusion of oxygen into the blood. A is incorrect because the movement of oxygen is not affected by the concentration gradient for carbon dioxide B is incorrect because there is no air in the capillary; the air is in the alveolus. C is incorrect because the movement of each gas (carbon dioxide and oxygen) is dependent on the concentration gradient of each individual gas, not on the concentration of the other gas.

questions.stem:
Three statements about propane and propanol are listed below.
• Propane and propanol belong to the same homologous series

• Propanol is a compound that contains three carbon atoms 

• Propane is an unsaturated hydrocarbon

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Statement 1 is incorrect because propane is an alkane , while propanol is an alcohol , so they belong to different homologous series Propane (C 3 H 8 ) is an alkane, meaning it contains only single C–C bonds with enough C-H bonds to complete four bonds per carbon Propanol (C 3 H 7 OH) is an alcohol because it contains the –OH functional group Substances in the same homologous series must have the same functional group, so propane and propanol are not in the same homologous series Statement 2 is correct because propanol has the prefix prop- , which means it contains three carbon atoms in the main carbon chain Statement 3 is incorrect because propane is a saturated hydrocarbon, not unsaturated A hydrocarbon is unsaturated only if it contains a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C) Propane contains only single bonds because it is an alkane, so it is a saturated hydrocarbon Therefore, only statement 2 is correct

questions.stem: Which of the following substances would be reabsorbed by the kidneys?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (salts and glucose) because: The kidneys reabsorb all the glucose that enters the tubules (by active transport in selective reabsorption) and some salts, depending on the concentration of salts in the blood and how much water needs to be reabsorbed. Urea is not reabsorbed back into the bloodstream from the kidney tubules, and glycogen would not be present in the filtrate in the first place (it is a relatively large molecule and isn’t usually present in the blood).

questions.stem:
Penicillin is an antibiotic that prevents bacteria growing by stopping them from forming cell walls.
Why does penicillin not affect viruses?
options: A. Viruses do not have cell walls.
B. Viruses do not contain cytoplasm.
C. Viruses become resistant to penicillin.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Viruses are technically not living cells, this means that they are not affected by antibiotics. Viruses do not have cell walls or carry out cellular functions. Antibiotics work by disrupting cell chemical reactions or the production of cell walls. B is incorrect because viruses do not contain cytoplasm, and antibiotics don’t affect cytoplasm. C is incorrect because penicillin does not work on viruses. D is incorrect because this is correct as viruses use the host cell to reproduce rapidly. It is not relevant to why penicillin will not work on viruses, however.

questions.stem:
During birth the following processes happen:
• Breaking of the amniotic sac

• Contraction of the muscles in the uterine wall

• Cutting of the umbilical cord

In which order do these processes usually occur?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (2 → 1 → 3) because: Birth begins when the muscles in the wall of the uterus start contracting . This is the start of labour At first the contractions of the muscles stretch the cervix. This is the point that the amniotic sac breaks After a few hours, when the cervix is wide enough the head of the baby will pass through and the contractions will push the baby out through the vagina Once the baby is born it will start to breathe for itself and no longer need to get its oxygen from the placenta via the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord is cut just above the point it joins the baby (forming the belly button)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements would not be a correct example of negative feedback?
options: A. An increase in core body temperature when cold.
C. The release of a neurotransmitter at a synapse.
D. The control of blood glucose levels.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The release of a neurotransmitter at a synapse is not an example of negative feedback. Negative feedback mechanisms are the responses that occur in the body when a factor/system moves away from the normal range in which it should fall. A is incorrect because maintenance of a core body temperature within a narrow range is a key example of negative feedback. B is incorrect because vasoconstriction (constriction of arterioles in the skin) is part of a negative feedback response to a decrease in body temperature and is an action to reduce heat loss. D is incorrect because the hormones insulin and glucagon act to maintain blood glucose levels within a narrow range, another key example of negative feedback.

questions.stem: Which organ is involved in the metabolic breakdown of oral medication?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (liver) because: The liver is the primary site for drug metabolism. A is incorrect because although the stomach is involved in the digestion of some oral medications it does not fully metabolise the drug. C and D are incorrect because the brain and kidneys are not the primary sites of drug metabolism.

questions.stem: The glucose molecules formed during photosynthesis have which form of energy stored within them?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Chemical) because: When glucose is made in photosynthesis, light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy in the chemical (covalent) bonds that hold the atoms in a glucose molecule together. A is incorrect because light energy is essential to drive the reactions of photosynthesis (reacting carbon dioxide and water together to form glucose). B is incorrect because photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction. Heat energy is released when an exothermic reaction occurs. D is incorrect because mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy in an object used to do work (a machine), not the stored energy found in glucose molecules.

questions.stem:
The statements below are about different hormones in the human body.
• Produced by the pancreas.

• Causes the voice to deepen at puberty.

• Causes an egg to mature in the menstrual cycle.

• Promotes the development of stronger muscles.

Which of these statements are correct for testosterone?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (2 and 4) because: Testosterone is the male hormone that causes secondary sexual characteristics during puberty . These include the development of stronger muscles and the voice to deepen. A is incorrect because while it does cause the voice to deepen, testosterone is not produced by the pancreas (it’s produced in the testes). C is incorrect because while it does promote the development of stronger muscles and is primarily thought of as a male hormone, women do produce small amounts of testosterone but it is not involved in the control of egg maturation in the ovaries. D is incorrect because even though this is a correct statement, it is not the only correct statement (the question is asking you for all the statements).

questions.stem:
There are a number of hormones that control fertility in women.
Which one of these maintains the lining during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (Progesterone) because: Progesterone is produced by the corpus luteum after ovulation. This maintains the lining of the uterus until the placenta can be developed and continue the production of progesterone until birth If no fertilisation occurs, the corpus luteum breaks down which leads to a fall in progesterone so that the lining of the uterus is no longer maintained and is lost (a period) A is incorrect because oestrogen stimulates the thickening of the uterus lining in the menstrual cycle. C is incorrect because FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary. D is incorrect because testosterone is a male sex hormone and has no role in the menstrual cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct definition for a sustainable resource?
options: A. A resource that can be replaced.
B. A resource that is running out.
C. Making sure that needs are met for future generations.
D. A resource that can be replenished as quickly as it is used.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (a resource that can be replenished as quickly as it is used) because: A sustainable resource is a resource that can be replaced (almost) as quickly as it is used. This means that it will not run out. An example of this would be planting a tree to replace one that is chopped down. A is incorrect because this statement only refers to resource replacement and not that it can be replaced as quickly as it is used. B is incorrect because this statement only refers to resources, and does not take into account the needs of the future populations. C is incorrect because sustainability is about protecting both the environment and resources for now and the future.

questions.stem:
Albinism is a condition where the pigment melanin does not get produced in the skin, hair and eyes. This is an inherited condition that is caused by a recessive allele.
If both parents have albinism what are the chances of the offspring being an albino child?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (100%) because: If both parents have the condition then they will both have the same genotype : homozygous recessive Both parents only have (two) copies of the recessive allele; therefore the gametes formed by meiosis in each parent will always contain a recessive allele, therefore the only possible genotype for any offspring from these parents will be homozygous recessive Note - in genetics it is key to know your definitions! Gene - section of the chromosome that codes for a particular characteristic Allele - alternative version of a gene Genotype -  the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present Phenotype - the observable features (physical characteristics) of an organism Homozygous - having two identical alleles for the same gene Heterozygous - has two different alleles for a particular gene

questions.stem:
The graph below shows the growth of the human population globally since 1630.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/-1RXSz0K_image-2-1.png)Which of the following options represents the longest time period taken for the population of humans to double?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (200 years) because: Between 1630 and 1830 the population increased from 500 million to 1000 million. This is the longest time period represented on the graph for the population to double. After 1830 there was rapid growth of the human population, the time for the population to double was significantly less.

questions.stem: Which of these statements correctly describes genetic engineering?
options: A. Only breeding from crop plants that are resistant to pests.
B. Altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides.
C. Using yeast to produce ethanol.
D. Production of insulin in the pancreas.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides) because: Genetic engineering is the process of altering DNA to include new genes or sequences of DNA. This will give the modified organism new characteristics that may increase yield or increase resistance to chemicals. A is incorrect because this process describes selective breeding .  Selective breeding is the use of organisms with a particular characteristic in breeding so that the offspring have the trait that you desire. C is incorrect because this process describes fermentation . This is a natural process that has been exploited for centuries to produce bread and beer. D is incorrect because this is a natural process that occurs normally in healthy individuals.

questions.stem:
The following statements refer to conservation techniques.
• Artificial insemination will decrease the need for male and female organisms to be present in the same area

• The offspring produced during artificial insemination will have less genetic variation than their parents

• In vitro fertilisation will produce large numbers of offspring without the need for gametes to fuse

• These techniques will increase the resilience of a species and decrease their risk of extinction

Which of these statements are false?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (2 and 3 only) because: Artificial insemination is a technique whereby the genetic material carried by the gametes combine and is therefore used to maintain or increase the genetic variation within a species, which makes statement 2 false. In vitro fertilisation involves the fusion of gametes outside the body (usually in a petri dish), so statement 3 is not correct. A , C and D are all incorrect because statements 1 and 4 are true regarding conservation techniques.

Fig. 1 shows a photomicrograph of some red blood cells.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/10/061032-oct-2018-paper-3-q8a-rbcs---sq.png)Fig. 1

[1]
(ii)
State two ways in which a red blood cell is adapted to its function.
[2]
questions.explanation: (i) The function of a red blood cell is: (To) transport oxygen; [1 mark] (ii) Ways in which a red blood cell is adapted to its function are: Any two from the following: Contains haemoglobin; [1 mark] Biconcave (disc shape) / large surface area to volume ratio; [1 mark] No nucleus / (named) organelle; [1 mark] [Total: 3 marks]

questions.stem: Compare natural selection with artificial selection.
questions.explanation: A comparison of natural selection with artificial selection is... Natural selection occurs naturally due to selection pressures within the environment whereas artificial selection is carried out by humans (selecting organisms with the most suitable characteristics); [1 mark] Natural selection results in populations with features/characteristics better adapted to the environment whereas artificial selection results in populations (more) useful to humans; [1 mark] Natural selection takes many generations / a long time to occur whereas artificial selection takes fewer generations / less time to occur; [1 mark] [Total: 3 marks]

questions.stem:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a condition that commonly occurs in women of reproductive age. It is characterised by hormonal imbalances that affect the menstrual cycle of women with this condition.
Fig. 1 compares the levels of FSH and LH in a normal menstrual cycle with the levels seen in the cycle of a woman with PCOS.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/hormone-level.png)Fig. 1
Use the information in Fig. 1 to explain the effect that PCOS would have on the ovaries of a woman.
questions.explanation: The effect that PCOS would have on the ovaries of a woman would include... Any three of the following: Low FSH levels SO an egg will not mature; [1 mark] Low FSH SO oestrogen will not be released; [1 mark] No oestrogen SO LH will not be released; [1 mark] Low LH / no LH increase SO no ovulation / no egg will be released (from ovary); [1 mark] Where capitalised SO is present the statements on both sides of SO are required for a mark to be awarded. [Total: 3 marks] Note that this is an explain question, so each effect on the ovaries needs to be linked to its hormonal cause for a mark to be awarded.

questions.stem:
The stomach produces gastric juice which contains hydrochloric acid.
Explain the importance of hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is important in the stomach because... It kills bacteria in food because the low pH denatures their enzymes; [1 mark] This means they cannot carry out any cell reactions to maintain life; [1 mark] It ensures that the pH (in the stomach) is at an optimum for the working of pepsin; [1 mark] [Total: 3 marks]

questions.stem:
More than 40 years ago, botanists studied the leaves of broad bean plants and discovered that guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata. They found that stomata were open when the guard cells were turgid.
Table 1 shows some of their measurements.
Table 1


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | closed stomata | open stomata |
| ion concentration in guard cells /pmol | 0.3 | 2.5 |
| guard cell volume/μm 3 | 4000.0 | 6500.0 |
| turgor pressure in the guard cells /MPa | 2.0 | 4.8 |
| width of stomatal opening/μm | 0.0 | 8.0 |
(i)
Ions move into guard cells by active transport.
Describe how the ions move into the guard cells.
[2]
(ii)
Describe and explain how the change in ion concentration causes the guard cell volume to change.
Use the information in Table 1 in your answer.
[6]
(iii)
The botanists left the broad bean plants unattended for three days. During this time the broad bean plants wilted. 
Suggest two environmental factors that can cause plants to wilt.
[2]
questions.explanation: (i) Ions move into guard cells as follows: Any two from the following: (Ions) move against the concentration gradient; [1 mark] (Through) proteins (in the cell membrane) ; [1 mark] (Which) uses/requires energy; [1 mark] From respiration; [1 mark] (ii) A description and explanation of how a change in the ion concentration causes the guard cells to change volume includes: Any six from the following: Description A high(er) ion concentration results in large(r) (guard cell) volume (or reverse argument of this) ; [1 mark] A high(er) ion concentration causes low(er) water potential ( or reverse argument of this) ; [1 mark] Accept a comparative data quote (from the table) with units to support any description; [1 mark] Explanation (A high ion concentration causes) water to move into (guard) cells; [1 mark] (This happens) across a partially permeable membrane; [1 mark] By osmosis ; [1 mark] A large cell volume correlates with high turgor pressure ( or reverse argument of this) ; [1 mark] This is because cell water / membrane / cytoplasm / vacuole, pushes more on the cell wall; [1 mark] (iii) Two environmental factors that cause plants to wilt are: Any two from the following: Lack of water; [1 mark] High temperature; [1 mark] Low humidity / dry air; [1 mark] Wind; [1 mark] Accept any other valid point referring to water loss from the stomata ; [1 mark] [Total: 10 marks] For part (iii), make sure you qualify responses with high/low rather than just writing about the process.  For example, " high temperature" will get you a mark, but just "temperature" alone will not.

questions.stem:
Petroleum is separated into fractions by fractional distillation.
Which statement about the properties of the fractions is correct?
options: A. The boiling point of the fractions decreases as the number of carbon atoms in the molecules increases.
B. Fractions containing smaller molecules are collected at the bottom of the column where the temperature is highest.
C. The viscosity of the fractions increases as the chain length increases because the intermolecular forces become stronger.
D. Fractions with longer carbon chains are used as refinery gas because they are more volatile.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Crude oil (petroleum) is a mixture of hydrocarbons with different chain lengths In fractional distillation , crude oil is heated so that most of it vaporises The vapours enter a fractionating column , which is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top Hydrocarbons with high boiling points (long-chain molecules) condense low down in the column Hydrocarbons with low boiling points (short-chain molecules) rise higher before condensing As chain length increases, hydrocarbons have stronger intermolecular forces Stronger intermolecular forces mean higher boiling points , higher viscosity , and lower volatility This explains why fractions with longer carbon chains are more viscous liquids Therefore, the viscosity of the fractions increases as chain length increases, so C is correct A is incorrect because fractions with more carbon atoms have higher boiling points, not lower. This is because larger molecules have strong intermolecular forces of attraction B is incorrect because fractions with small molecules have low boiling points and rise to the top of the fractionating column D is incorrect because refinery gases contain short-chain hydrocarbons, which are more volatile than long-chain hydrocarbons

questions.stem:
Fig. 1 shows a pyramid of biomass and part of the carbon cycle.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/10/cie-igcse-2018-s1-oct-p4-q1a-carbon-cycle.png)Fig. 1
(i)
State the principal source of energy required for trophic level D of the pyramid of biomass in Fig. 1. 
[1]
(ii)
State the letter that represents the primary consumers in Fig. 1.
[1]
(iii)
State how carbon is transferred from producers to primary consumers.
[1]
(iv)
Explain why trophic level A is smaller than trophic level B in the pyramid of biomass in Fig. 1.
[3]
questions.explanation: (i) The principle source of energy required for trophic level D is: Sun / light; [1 mark] (ii) The letter that represents the primary consumers is: C ; [1 mark] (iii) The carbon is transferred from producers to primary consumers by: Ingestion / feeding; [1 mark] (iv) Trophic level A is smaller than trophic level B because: Any three from the following: Energy is lost (from the food chain as it is transferred from one trophic level to the next) / energy decreases up the trophic levels / energy transfer is inefficient; [1 mark] Only 10% of the energy from each trophic level is transferred to the next OR about 90% of the energy from each trophic level is not transferred to the next; [1 mark] Energy is lost as heat / in respiration / in (named) metabolic processes / movement; [1 mark] Not all organisms (in one trophic level) are eaten / not all parts of the organisms are eaten; [1 mark] Not all nutrients in the organisms are eaten / digested / absorbed; [1 mark] Some energy is lost in excretion / urine / faeces / egestion; [1 mark] Some energy is transferred to decomposers; [1 mark] [Total: 6 marks] It is important to remember as many examples as possible of how energy is lost between trophic levels. This is quite a common question that gets repeated many times in exams. This question covers core knowledge but is taken from an extended paper 4 question.

questions.stem:
CGRP is a protein found in the human brain. High levels of CGRP has been linked to the occurrence of migraines in sufferers. A possible treatment under investigation involves injecting mice with human CGRP.
Explain how the immune system of mice would respond to the CGRP injection.
questions.explanation: The immune system of mice would respond in the following ways to the CGRP injection... Antigens on CGRP proteins would be recognised as foreign (by mice lymphocytes); [1 mark] Lymphocytes would produce antibodies against CGRP; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] Remember that the immune response would occur in response to the presence of any foreign antigen, even if that antigen does not form part of a pathogen. Human CGRP proteins would trigger a similar immune response in mice than an infection with a pathogen would.

questions.stem: Which class of vertebrate typically gives birth to live young?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (mammals) because: Mammals are generally the only group of vertebrates to give birth to live young. B, C and D are all incorrect because all other vertebrate classes tend to lay eggs.

questions.stem:
Four statements about large biological molecules are given below:
• Proteins are made from a number of different amino acids.

• Both glycogen and starch are made from simple sugar base units.

• Fats are made from glycerol and fatty acids.

• Oils are made from glycerol only. 

Which of the four statements above is/are false?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The question asks which of the statements given is false . Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true. Statement 4 is false because oils (like fats, a type of lipid) are made from glycerol and fatty acids. Around 20 different amino acids are used to build protein molecules in almost all living cells. The basic structure of each amino acid is largely the same, with one variable region differing to produce a variety of amino acids. Glycogen and starch, as well as cellulose, are all polymers of glucose.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows part of an organism (ciliated epithelium). 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/50314_1-2--image-1--ciliated-cell.png)What term would correctly describe the level of organisation of the structure in the diagram above?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (cell) because: The image shows a ciliated epithelial cell. These cells can be found lining the trachea and parts of the lungs. Cells are the basic functional units of all living organisms on Earth. B is incorrect because organelle is a term used to describe subcellular structures within cells, such as mitochondria and chloroplasts. C is incorrect because an organ is formed from two or more tissues working together. Tissues are made from groups of similar cells. D is incorrect because an organ system is made from organs working together to perform a particular function.

questions.stem:
X, Y and Z are organic compounds.
Some properties of these compounds are listed.
• Y and Z decolourise bromine water, while X does not.

• X and Z has the same number of carbons. Y has one carbon atom more in the chain.

• X is manufactured by the hydration of Z with steam.

Which row identifies correctly X, Y and Z?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | X | Y | Z |
| A | ethanol | propene | ethene |
| B | ethanol | butene | ethene |
| C | ethene | propene | ethanol |
| D | ethene | butene | ethanol |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The bromine water test is used to distinguish between alkenes and other organic compounds Substances that decolourise bromine water are unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes) This is because the bromine diatomic (Br 2 ) can react via an addition reaction across C=C double bond, turning the orange bromine water into colourless Since Y and Z can decoulourise bromine water, Y and Z must be alkenes X does not decolourise bromine water, so X is not an alkene X and Z have the same number of carbon atoms Y has one more carbon atom than X and Z By checking the rows of the table, if Z is ethene (2 carbons), then Y must be propene (3 carbons) If Z is ethene then X must start with the prefix eth- X is manufactured by the hydration of Z with steam Hydration is the process of adding water (steam) to the C=C double bond One hydrogen of water will bond to one carbon, while the OH group will bond to the other carbon The hydration of ethene produces ethanol Therefore Z = ethene and X = ethanol Putting it all together: X = ethanol Y = propene Z = ethene B & D is incorrect because Y is not butene. Butene has two more carbons than ethene, not one C is incorrect Z is not ethanol. Ethanol is not an unsaturated hydrocarbon and it does not decolourise bromine water

questions.stem:
Three statements about the role of water in mammals are given below:
• Water forms a major part of the cytoplasm, allowing substances to dissolve and participate in metabolic reactions within the cell

• Substances, such as urea and excess salts, are able to dissolve in water making them easier to remove from the body in urine

• Allows substances to be transported around the body in the blood

Which of the statements above are true?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (All of the statements) because: Water is known as the universal solvent for living organisms as a very large number of substances are able to dissolve in it. Those substances that are not able to dissolve in water are usually packaged in substances that can. Water is the main constituent of the cytoplasm - remember this is the jelly-like solution that is enclosed within the cell membrane The kidneys are responsible for filtering the blood and removing urea and excess salts by forming urine. Water plays a large role in this function Blood plasma is the yellowish liquid that holds the blood cells in suspension; it is mainly water in which proteins, hormones, antibodies, soluble food molecules and ions (amongst other substances) dissolve to be transported around the body

questions.stem: A decrease in which of the following factors would normally cause the transpiration rate to increase?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The less humid (drier) the atmosphere, the higher the diffusion gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside (through the stomatal pore). A is incorrect because a decrease in stomatal density means less transpiration (as the leaves have fewer stomata). B is incorrect because a reduction in light intensity causes stomata to close, reducing the rate of transpiration. C is incorrect because a reduction in temperature means the water vapour molecules move more slowly, so they would diffuse out of the stomata at a lower rate.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows a palisade mesophyll cell found in the leaves of plants.
In which region of the cell would starch be stored? 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/eeEIuXLc_picture4.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: It represents the chloroplasts which are the organelles where photosynthesis occurs. They contain chlorophyll which absorb light energy. A is incorrect because this is the nucleus where genetic information is stored. B is incorrect because this is the vacuole, which contains a solution of sugars and salts and helps the cell maintain its shape. C is incorrect because this is the cell wall which contains the polymer cellulose which provides structural support to the cell.

questions.stem: What is a feature of all catalysts?
options: A. They are made from protein
B. They are not changed by the reaction
C. They are broken down in the reaction
D. They are altered by the rate of the reaction
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (They are not changed by the reaction) because: A feature of all catalysts is that they remain unchanged at the end of a reaction, and can go on to catalyse subsequent reactions. A is incorrect because although enzymes, as biological catalysts, are made from proteins, other catalysts not found in living organisms are not made of proteins (many metals can act as catalysts in certain chemical reactions for example). C and D are incorrect because catalysts are not changed by the chemical reactions they speed up.

questions.stem:
A student reacts aqueous silver nitrate with aqueous sodium chloride. A white precipitate of silver chloride is formed in a solution of sodium nitrate. The reaction mixture is filtered to separate the precipitate.
Which row identifies the residue and the filtrate?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | residue | filtrate |
| A | silver chloride | aqueous sodium nitrate |
| B | aqueous sodium nitrate | silver chloride |
| C | silver chloride | pure water |
| D | silver nitrate | aqueous sodium chloride |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Silver nitrate reacts with sodium chloride to form silver chloride, which is insoluble and appears as a white precipitate Insoluble solids are trapped on the filter paper during filtration and form the residue The remaining liquid that passes through the filter paper is the filtrate Aqueous sodium nitrate is a soluble side product from the mixture The filtrate contains aqueous sodium nitrate, which stays dissolved in water Therefore, the residue is silver chloride and filtrate is aqueous sodium nitrate B is incorrect because aqueous sodium nitrate is soluble and cannot be the residue, because it will go through the filter paper C is incorrect because the filtrate is not pure water because sodium nitrate is dissolved in it. The filtration process does not remove the soluble salt from the mixture D is incorrect because silver nitrate and sodium chloride are the reactants, not the separated products

questions.stem: Which of the following terms would be correct to describe a leaf, a root and stem?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (organ) because: All three structures in the question are organs. An organ is a group of two or more tissues working together to carry out a particular function. A is incorrect because each of the leaves, stems and roots are made up of thousands of different cells all working together. B is incorrect because the leaf is made from palisade & spongy mesophyll tissue, epidermal tissue and vascular tissue functioning together to allow a plant to photosynthesise. The roots and stem are made from vascular (transport) tissue which work together to transport substances around the plant. D is incorrect because together plants have two organ systems. The shoot organ system in a plant is made from leaves, stems, buds, fruits and flowers. The root organ system of most plants are all the parts that are underground.

questions.stem:
The image below shows two molecules before and after chemical digestion by enzymes in the alimentary canal. 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/01/4--image-2---molecules.png)Which letter(s) identify the product(s) of complete starch digestion?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: The product of complete starch digestion is glucose, a simple sugar, as shown by H. A is incorrect because G represents glycerol and F represents fatty acid chains; these are the products of lipid (fat and oil) digestion. C is incorrect because E represents maltose molecules. Maltose is a disaccharide made from two molecules of glucose chemically bonded together. Maltose is the product of starch digestion by amylase. D is incorrect because E is maltose and H is glucose. Only glucose is the final product of complete starch digestion.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is an effect of a cholera infection?
• Loss of salts from the blood

• Loss of water from the blood

• Blockage of the small intestine

• Persistent diarrhoea
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. (1, 2 and 4) because: Blockage of the small intestine (3) is the only effect listed above not caused by a cholera infection.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows a potted plant and the same plant 48 hours later.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/8-q1-wilting.png)What has caused the plant’s appearance to change?
options: A. Water loss by translocation is greater than water uptake.
B. Water evaporating from the leaves by translocation.
C. Water loss by transpiration is greater than water uptake.
D. Water loss from the leaves by osmosis.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: After 48 hours the leaves have wilted , you can see them drooping in the image Wilting is a sign that a plant has insufficient water – it has lost more water by transpiration than it has taken up and therefore water has moved out of cells, causing them to become flaccid A & B are incorrect because translocation is the term used to describe the movement of sucrose and amino acids in the phloem. D is incorrect because water loss occurs by evaporation of water from mesophyll cells inside the leaf and then diffusion of this water vapour through the stomata. questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the effect of root hairs on absorption?
options: A. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water and ions by osmosis.
B. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
C. Increase the surface area, maximising the uptake of water by osmosis and ions by diffusion.
D. Provide a surface area, increasing the rate of absorption of water and ions by active transport.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Root hairs are extensions of the cytoplasm of root cells, increasing the surface area to maximise the absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport. A is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport. Osmosis only applies to the movement of water. C Is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport, not diffusion. D Is incorrect because there is no indication that surface area is increased in this explanation, and osmosis should be mentioned in relation to the movement of water.
