A is incorrect because the stomach (2) only produces proteases for protein digestion. C is incorrect because the liver (3) produces bile which aids lipid digestion (by emulsifying lipids to increase their surface area) but it does not produce lipases. D is incorrect because the mouth (1) contains salivary glands which secrete salivary  amylase to digest carbohydrates. No lipases are made here.

questions.stem:
Ear length in rabbits is determined by a single gene with two alleles.
• The long ears allele is dominant and is represented by E

• The short ears allele is recessive and is represented by e

A male rabbit that is heterozygous for ear length mates with a female rabbit with short ears.
What is the probability that any offspring will have long ears?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. To determine the probability that any offspring will have long ears: Determine the genotypes of both parents: the heterozygous male has genotype Ee the female has short ears, which is the recessive phenotype, so she must be homozygous ee Set up a Punnett square: E e e Ee ee e Ee ee Count the offspring with long ears: 2 out of 4 offspring have genotype Ee and will therefore have long ears Express as a probability: =  = 50 %

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about antibiotics is correct?
options: A. antibiotics can be used to treat HIV
B. antibiotic resistance in humans reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics
C. antibiotics can only treat bacterial infections
D. antibiotics are an effective method of preventing the spread of STIs
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Antibiotics are drugs that are used to treat bacterial infections, but do not affect viruses A is incorrect as HIV is a viral infection and antibiotics do not affect viruses. B is incorrect as antibiotic resistance develops in bacteria, not in humans. D is incorrect as antibiotics treat bacterial infections and are not an effective method of controlling the spread of STIs.

questions.stem:
An image of a cell is 24 mm long. The actual cell length is 6 μm.
What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The cell is magnified 4000 times To calculate magnification: Convert the units so that they match There are 1000 μm in 1 mm 24 x 100 = 24 000 μm Use the formula: magnification = image size ÷ actual size = 24 000 ÷ 6 = 4000 Always check that your units match before you begin calculating. If the image size is given in millimetres and the actual size is given in micrometres, convert the image size to micrometres first (multiply by 1000) before doing anything else. Carrying out unit conversions at the start of your working reduces the risk of forgetting to convert at all, which is one of the most common sources of error in magnification questions.

questions.stem: What is the role of water in digestion?
options: A. It increases the surface area of food for enzyme action.
B. It allows soluble food molecules to dissolve so they can be absorbed.
C. It turns insoluble food molecules into soluble molecules.
D. It provides energy for active transport.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Water acts as a solvent, so substances can dissolve in it. This allows digested substances to be transported and absorbed A is incorrect because increasing the surface area of food is the role of physical digestion (for example chewing), not water. C  is incorrect because large insoluble food molecules are made into small soluble molecules by chemical digestion carried out by enzymes, not water. D is incorrect because water does not provide the energy for active transport.

questions.stem:
A potato tissue sample has an initial mass of 5.0 g. 
It is immersed in an unknown solution.  
Its mass after 1 hour is 4.2 g. 
Which statement is correct?
options: A. The solution had a lower water potential than the plant tissue.
B. The solution had a higher water potential than the plant tissue.
C. The plant tissue had no cell membrane.
D. The solution was distilled water.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The tissue lost mass , so water left the cells by osmosis. This means the surrounding solution had a lower water potential than the plant tissue B is incorrect because if the solution had a higher water potential, water would enter and mass would increase. C is incorrect because osmosis only occurs through partially permeable membranes, which plant cells do have. D i s incorrect because distilled water has a high water potential, meaning water would enter and mass would increase. Don't mix up water potential  with the concentration of the solute. Osmosis is defined as the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane .

questions.stem:

questions.stem: How does physical digestion help chemical digestion?
options: A. It changes large insoluble molecules into small soluble molecules.
B. It increases the surface area of food.
C. It provides the acidic conditions needed.
D. It absorbs digested nutrients directly into the blood.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Physical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which increases the surface area available for enzymes A is incorrect because changing large insoluble molecules into small soluble molecules is chemical digestion, not physical digestion. C is incorrect because acidic conditions are provided by hydrochloric acid in the stomach, not by physical digestion. D is incorrect because physical digestion does not move nutrients into the blood, and absorption happens after digestion.

|---|
| A | amylase | fats |
| B | maltase | starch |
| C | pepsin | starch |
| D | trypsin | protein |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Trypsin is a protease , so it breaks down protein A is incorrect because amylase breaks down starch, not fats. B is incorrect because maltase breaks down maltose to glucose, not starch. C is incorrect because pepsin is another protease that breaks down protein, not starch. While pepsin breaks down proteins in the acidic conditions of the stomach, trypsin continues to break down proteins in the alkaline conditions of the small intestine.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the pathway of water through a plant?
options: A. xylem → root hair cell → root cortex cell → mesophyll
B. root hair cell → root cortex cell → xylem → mesophyll
C. root cortex cell → mesophyll → xylem → root hair cell
D. root hair cell → xylem → root cortex cell → mesophyll
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Water moves through the plant in this order: root hair cells → root cortex cells → xylem → mesophyll cells Root hair cells absorb water from the soil because they are in direct contact and have a large surface area. The water then passes through the root cortex cells to reach the centre of the root Next, the water enters the xylem , which carries water up through the root and stem towards the leaves Finally, in the leaf water moves from the xylem into the mesophyll cells , where it can evaporate during transpiration and is also used in photosynthesis

questions.stem:

How does the density of the unknown liquid compare with the density of water?
options: A. Its density is greater than the density of water
B. Its density is less than the density of water
C. Its density is the same as the density of water
D. With the information given, it is impossible to tell.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Density = 200 / 230 = 0.87 g/cm 3 This is less than 1.0 g/cm 3 A is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water. C is incorrect as the density is less than the density of water. D is incorrect as it is possible to tell what the density is.

questions.stem: How does blood exit the heart?
options: A. through arteries from the atria
B. through arteries from the ventricles
C. through veins from the atria
D. through veins from the ventricles
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Blood leaves the heart in arteries , and it is pumped out from the ventricles The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta , and the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery A is incorrect because blood does not leave the heart from the atria. C is incorrect because veins carry blood towards the heart, not away from it. D is incorrect because although blood leaves from the ventricles, it does not leave through veins.

questions.stem:
The following are statements about blood.
• Red blood cells transport oxygen.

• Plasma transports hormones.

• Platelets destroy pathogens.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Statement 1 is correct because red blood cells transport oxygen . They contain haemoglobin , a protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and carries it to body tissues. Statement 2 is correct because plasma transports hormones and other dissolved substances around the body. These include nutrients such as glucose, waste products such as urea, carbon dioxide and ions. Statement 3 is incorrect because destroying pathogens is mainly the role of white blood cells . Platelets are involved in blood clotting , helping to form a clot to prevent blood loss when a blood vessel is damaged.

questions.stem:
Varicella zoster virus  (VZV) causes chickenpox.
The graph shows the concentration of antibodies in the blood of a patient after vaccination against VZV.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/03/57617-vaccination.png)What most likely happened at point X to cause the increase in antibody concentration?
options: A. infection with a different pathogen
B. the vaccine took time to stimulate lymphocytes
C. antibodies produced earlier were released into the blood
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The first small rise shows the primary immune response after vaccination , when antibodies are produced slowly and memory cells are formed When the person is infected with VZV at X , these memory cells recognise the antigen and respond rapidly, producing large amounts of antibodies and causing the large second increase A is incorrect because infection with a different pathogen would trigger a new primary immune response, which would be slower and smaller. B is incorrect because the vaccine already stimulated lymphocytes to produce antibodies, shown by the first peak on the graph. C is incorrect because antibodies are not stored and later released.

questions.stem: What do the external intercostal muscles do during inhalation?
options: B. pull ribs upwards and outwards

questions.stem: Why does breathing rate increase during exercise?
options: A. oxygen concentration in blood increases
B. oxygen concentration in blood decreases
C. carbon dioxide concentration in blood increases
D. carbon dioxide concentration in blood decreases
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. During exercise, muscle cells carry out respiration at a higher rate , producing more carbon dioxide as a waste product The increased carbon dioxide concentration in the blood is detected by the brain , which stimulates an increase in breathing rate and depth to remove the excess carbon dioxide A is incorrect because oxygen concentration does not increase during exercise. B is incorrect because although oxygen concentration in the blood may decrease slightly during exercise, breathing rate is mainly controlled by increases in carbon dioxide concentration detected by the brain. D is incorrect because because carbon dioxide concentration does not decrease during exercise.

questions.stem: What is the sequence of a reflex arc?
options: A. receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
B. receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
C. sensory neurone→ relay neurone → receptor → motor neurone → effector
D. sensory neurone → receptor → relay neurone → effector → motor neurone
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. A reflex arc follows a fixed sequence: A receptor detects a stimulus (for example heat or pain) and generates a nerve impulse The impulse travels along a sensory neurone to the central nervous system (usually the spinal cord) The impulse passes across a synapse to a relay neurone within the spinal cord The relay neurone passes the impulse across another synapse to a motor neurone The motor neurone carries the impulse to an effector (a muscles or gland), which produces the response

questions.stem: Which muscle action causes the pupil to become smaller in bright light?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. In bright light, the pupil reflex reduces the amount of light entering the eye. The circular muscles of the iris contract , which makes the pupil smaller (constricts) and therefore reduces the amount of light reaching the retina B is incorrect because when the radial muscles contract, the pupil becomes larger (dilates), which happens in dim light to allow more light into the eye. C is incorrect because when the circular muscles relax, the radial muscles contract as described above. D is incorrect because the ciliary muscles control the shape of the lens, helping focus on near or distant objects; they do not control pupil size.

questions.stem:
The table shows features of four body control systems.
Which row is the nervous system?


| ['', 'Response speed', 'Carried by', 'Duration of effect'] |
|---|
| A | fast | neurones | short |
| B | slow | blood | long |
| C | slow | neurones | long |
| D | fast | blood | long |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Nervous control involves electrical impulses travelling along neurones , so responses are very fast and usually short-lived B is incorrect because signals carried in the blood describe hormonal control, not nervous control. C is incorrect because nervous signals do travel along neurones, but they are fast, not slow. D is incorrect because signals carried in the blood describe hormonal control, not nervous control.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows a plant shoot.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/03/29897-auxin.png)What substance is X?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Auxin is a plant growth hormone produced in the shoot tip. When light shines from one side, auxin becomes unevenly distributed , moving to the shaded side of the shoot Auxin stimulates cell elongation , so cells on the shaded side grow longer This causes the shoot to bend towards the light , which is the phototropic response A is incorrect because glucose is used in respiration and growth, but it does not control the bending of the shoot. B is incorrect because chlorophyll is the green pigment used for photosynthesis; it absorbs light but does not control growth direction. C is incorrect because cellulose forms the cell walls of plant cells and provides support; it does not control plant growth responses.

questions.stem:
A new antibiotic is introduced. Initially it is very effective at killing a bacterial pathogen. After many years, the antibiotic becomes much less effective.
Which process explains this change?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Natural selection occurs when bacteria with mutations that make them resistant to an antibiotic survive treatment These resistant bacteria reproduce and pass the resistance genes to their offspring Over time, the proportion of resistant bacteria increases , so the antibiotic becomes less effective B is incorrect because bacteria do not have immune systems. C is is incorrect because behavioural adaptation refers to changes in animal behaviour that improve survival, such as migration or hunting strategies. D is incorrect because toxin production refers to bacteria producing harmful chemicals that damage host tissues, not antibiotics.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows a flower.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/03/31387-flower.png)Which row correctly identifies the functions of X, Y and Z?


| ['', 'Function of X', 'Function of Y', 'Function of Z'] |
|---|
| A | produces pollen grains | receives pollen grains | contains ovules |
| B | produces pollen grains | receives pollen grains | produces pollen |
| C | receives pollen grains | produces pollen grains | contains pollen |
| D | produces pollen grains | contains ovules | receives pollen |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The anther ( X ) is part of the stamen and its function is to produce pollen grains , which contain the male gametes The stigma ( Y ) is the top of the carpel and its role is to receive pollen grains during pollination . It is often sticky to help trap pollen The ovary ( Z ) is located at the base of the carpel and contains ovules , which hold the female gametes . After fertilisation, the ovules develop into seeds

questions.stem:
The graph shows the levels of four hormones in the blood during a 28-day menstrual cycle.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/03/29035-menstrual-cycle.png)What is hormone X?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Luteinising hormone (LH) shows a sharp surge just before day 14 , which triggers ovulation , causing the ovary to release an egg This sudden peak in LH is known as the LH surge A is incorrect because FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) increases earlier in the cycle and stimulates the development of follicles in the ovary. C is incorrect because oestrogen gradually increases during the first half of the cycle as the follicle develops. D is incorrect because progesterone rises after ovulation and helps maintain the lining of the uterus in preparation for possible pregnancy.

questions.stem:
Red–green colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome.
A carrier female (XᴺXᶜ) and a normal male (XᴺY) have children.
What proportion of their sons will be colour blind?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Determine parent genotypes: Carrier female: XᴺXᶜ Normal male: XᴺY Complete Punnett square: Xᴺ Y Xᴺ XᴺXᴺ (daughter, normal) XᴺY (son, normal) Xᶜ XᴺXᶜ (daughter, carrier) XᶜY (son, colour blind) For sons only, look at the Y column (because sons get Y from the father): XᴺY (normal) XᶜY (colour blind) So 1 out of 2 sons ( 1/2 ) are colour blind A is incorrect because one possible son genotype (XᶜY) results in colour blindness. B is incorrect because 1/4 refers to the proportion of all children, not specifically to sons. D is incorrect because only sons that inherit Xᶜ from the mother are colour blind. If a question asks only about “sons” or “daughters”, only consider the relevant row or column of the Punnett square. A helpful strategy is to identify and highlight the sons or daughters in the Punnett square before doing any calculations. This makes it much easier to avoid errors.

questions.stem:
A desert plant has thick leaves and a waxy cuticle.
Scientists make three statements.
• These features reduce water loss.

• These features are inherited characteristics.

• These features developed because the plant needed them.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Statement 1 is correct because thick leaves and a waxy cuticle are adaptive features that reduce water loss . These features help desert plants survive in dry environments by reducing evaporation from the leaf surface. Statement 2 is correct because these features are inherited characteristics . Adaptive features are controlled by genes and can be passed from parent plants to their offspring. Statement 3 is incorrect because adaptations do not develop because organisms need them . Instead, they arise through natural selection over many generations. Plants that already had traits such as thicker leaves or a waxy cuticle survived better in dry conditions and passed these alleles to their offspring.

questions.stem: Which organism is a producer?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. A producer is an organism that makes its own organic nutrients , usually by photosynthesis using energy from sunlight Grass is a plant, so it acts as a producer at the first trophic level of a food chain, converting light energy into chemical energy stored in organic molecules B is incorrect because a rabbit is a primary consumer, obtaining energy by feeding on plants. C is incorrect because a hawk is a carnivore and a higher-level consumer, obtaining energy by eating other animals. D is incorrect because fungi are decomposers, obtaining energy by breaking down dead organic material.

questions.stem:
The sequence shows the events that occurs in a lake after fertiliser runoff enters the water.
fertiliser runoff → algal bloom → X → dissolved oxygen decreases → fish die
What is process X?
options: D. increased nitrate absorption by plants
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. When fertilisers containing nitrates and other nutrients enter a lake, they cause an algal bloom (rapid growth of algae) When many algae die as part of their natural life cycle, decomposers break down the dead organic material During this process, decomposers carry out aerobic respiration , which uses large amounts of dissolved oxygen in the water This increase in respiration by decomposers causes the dissolved oxygen concentration to decrease , which can lead to the death of aquatic organisms that require oxygen B is incorrect because increased photosynthesis would produce oxygen, not cause oxygen levels to decrease. C is incorrect because fish feeding does not cause a large decrease in oxygen. D is incorrect because nitrate absorption by plants occurs earlier in the process.

questions.stem:
Fig. 4.1 shows a blue whale, a marine mammal that has a heart weighing up to 600 kg.

questions.explanation:
• The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body while the right ventricle only pumps blood to the lungs  OR  the left ventricle pumps blood further than the right ventricle  [1 mark]
 • The left ventricle needs to generate higher pressure / must contract with more force  [1 mark]
 Make sure you connect the destination of the blood (whole body vs. lungs) to the requirement for a thicker wall. Avoid vague statements such as "it needs more muscle" without explaining why.

questions.stem:
A volunteer participated in a study looking at the pupil reflex. Fig. 5.1 shows the change in the volunteer's pupil diameter when a high-intensity light is switched on after 0.5 seconds.
  Fig. 5.1
 Calculate the rate of pupil constriction between 0.5 seconds and 2.5 seconds.
 Show your working and provide the correct units.
questions.explanation:
To calculate the rate of pupil constriction between 0.5 seconds and 2.5 seconds:
 • Determine the time that has passed, i.e. the change in the Y axis:
 = 2.5 - 0.5
 = 2 seconds
 • Determine the change in pupil diameter, i.e. the change in the X-axis:
  = 8 - 2
 = 6 mm
 • Determine the change in pupil diameter per second:
 • Divide the change in diameter by the number of seconds
 = 6 ÷ 2
 =  3 mm/s
 Award marks as follows:
 • 2 (seconds)  AND  6 (mm)  [1 mark]
 • 3  [1 mark]
 • mm/s  OR  mm s -1  [1 mark]
 Award full marks for the correct answer and units in the absence of other calculations.

questions.stem:
Alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) is a protein that protects the lungs from damage. A deficiency in this protein is a genetic condition determined by a single gene.
 Fig. 6.1 shows the inheritance of this condition in a family.
  Fig. 6.1
 Using evidence from Fig. 6.1:
 (i) Explain whether the allele for AAT deficiency is dominant or recessive.
 [2]
 (ii) Determine the probability of individuals 5 and 6 having a second child who is a carrier.
 [1]
questions.explanation:
(i) The allele is:
 • Recessive  [1 mark]
 • Two unaffected parents / 5 and 6 have an affected child  [1 mark]
 (ii) The  probability of individuals 5 and 6 having a second child who is a carrier is:
 • 50%  OR  0.5  OR  1/2  [1 mark]
 Where two parents with the same phenotype produce a child with a different one, this indicates that the parents are heterozygous and the condition is recessive.

questions.stem:
The diagram below shows a cross-section through an alveolus and a capillary.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/11--image-6-alveolus-and-capillary.png)Why does oxygen move from P to Q?
options: A. The concentration of carbon dioxide is lower in the alveolus than in the blood.
B. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than in the air in the capillary.
C. Oxygen must replace carbon dioxide.
D. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. (The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus) because: Blood is deoxygenated when it enters the lung capillaries, therefore there is an oxygen concentration gradient between P and Q. There is a higher  concentration of oxygen in the air in the alveolus than in the  blood , leading to diffusion of oxygen into the blood. A is incorrect because the movement of oxygen is not affected by the concentration gradient for carbon dioxide B is incorrect because there is no air in the capillary; the air is in the alveolus. C is incorrect because the movement of each gas (carbon dioxide and oxygen) is dependent on the concentration gradient of each individual gas, not on the concentration of the other gas.

questions.explanation: (i) The rabbit population at year 0 is: 400 [1 mark] (ii) The fox population at year 10 is: 40 [1 mark] When reading values from a graph, make sure you read the correct axis. Here, the rabbit population is typically shown on one axis and the fox population on another. Take care to identify which line represents which organism before reading off the value.

questions.explanation: Answer B is correct because:  On a distance-time graph, constant speed is shown by a non-horizontal straight line This shows that the distance travelled per unit time is increasing at a steady rate Therefore, the only correct graph is graph B A is incorrect as A horizontal line shows that distance is not changing over time, therefore the object is stationary C is incorrect as An upward curved line shows that the distance travelled over time is increasing. The object is speeding up or accelerating D is incorrect as A curve like this shows that the distance travelled over time is decreasing. The object is slowing down or decelerating

questions.stem:
A group of students set up an experiment to investigate growth responses in plants. 
In one of the experiments, they placed a plant shoot in a box with a small window allowing light to fall on one side of the shoot only.
Which of the following options correctly describes and explains what happened in the student’s experiment?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | response | cause | effect |
| A | positive phototropism | more auxin on side of shoot exposed to light | slower growth on shaded side of shoot |
| B | positive phototropism | more auxin on shaded side of shoot | slower growth on side of shoot exposed to light |
| C | negative gravitropism | even distribution of auxins | equal rates of growth |
| D | positive phototropism | less auxin on shaded side of shoot | faster growth on side of shoot exposed to light |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: We can divide the shoot into two halves; the side in the light and the side in the shade. Auxins accumulate on the shaded side of a shoot strongly exposed to light from one direction (in this case through the window of a box) In the shoots, auxin promotes cell growth and elongation; if the shaded side has more auxin than the side exposed to the light then it will grow at a faster rate and the shoot exhibits positive phototropism, growing towards the light source A is incorrect because auxin would accumulate on the shaded side (as auxins diffuse away from light) and the shaded side would grow at a faster rate. C is incorrect because although shoots do show negative gravitropism, this factor does not impact the shoots growth response to light. Auxins are strongly affected by light so would not be evenly distributed and there would not therefore be even growth. D is incorrect because there would be more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot and faster growth in this region, not the region exposed to light.

questions.stem: Which energy source relies on radiation from the Sun?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Plants form the basis for fossil fuels Plants grow using radiation from the Sun Geothermal energy relies on the heat produced in the Earth's core and radioactive elements in the crust. Nuclear power relies on the energy released by radioactive  materials Tidal power comes (mostly) from the gravitational attraction to the Moon. Some of this is influenced by the Sun, but not by its radiation .

questions.stem: Which of the following energy transfers is most efficient?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The most efficient energy transfer is the one that produces the greatest percentage of useful energy output , which is the same as saying the lowest percentage of wasted energy output Answer D has a wasted energy output of 25% Therefore, it has a useful energy output of 75% Answer D has the greatest percentage of useful energy output Therefore, it is the most efficient energy transfer

questions.stem:
A small metal block is suspended under the surface of a beaker of water by a string. 
The metal block experiences a pressure exerted by the liquid.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/q2-medium-mcq-1-9-pressure-cie-igcse-physics.png) What would increase the pressure exerted on the metal block?
options: A. increasing the surface area of the stone
B. using a liquid with a lower density
C. increasing the mass of the metal block
D. lowering the metal block deeper into the liquid
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Lowering the block deeper into the liquid would increase the pressure A is incorrect as surface area has no effect on pressure in a fluid. B is incorrect as lowering the density would reduce the pressure. C is incorrect as mass of the block has no effect on the pressure in a fluid.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct word equation for aerobic respiration in plants?
options: A. glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
B. carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
C. glucose + water → carbon dioxide + oxygen
D. glucose + carbon dioxide → water + oxygen
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (glucose + oxygen →  carbon dioxide + water) because: Plants, like all living organisms, respire to release energy (not shown in the above equations), therefore the process of aerobic respiration is the same in plants as it is in other organisms Plants also photosynthesise, but only when conditions allow it to (such as when light is available and the temperature is appropriate) B is incorrect because this is the equation for photosynthesis in plants. Photosynthesis is not the reverse reaction of respiration, although the reactants and products are the opposite way around in each reaction. C and D are incorrect because the reactants and products have been mixed up.

questions.stem:
A car tyre is inflated with air.
As the car drives, the temperature of the tyre increases, which also causes the temperature of the air inside the tyre to increase. This increases the pressure of the air inside the tyre.
Which of the following is a correct explanation as to why?
options: A. The mass of air inside the tyre has increased.
B. The area of the tyre has decreased, thus increasing the pressure.
C. The air molecules collide with each other less frequently.
D. The average kinetic energy of the air molecules has increased.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy (KE) per molecule. If the temperature increases , then so does the average KE per molecule. If the particles have more KE , they move with a greater velocity . This causes them to hit the walls of the tyre at a greater speed, and to exert more force when they bounce off. This increased force increases the pressure in the tyre. A is incorrect as the tyre has not been pumped up, so no more air has been added. Therefore the mass cannot have increased. B is incorrect as the tyre has a (very nearly) fixed volume therefore the area with which air molecules can collide could not have changed. C is incorrect as if anything, the molecules will collide with each other more frequently, but it is collisions with the wall of the tyre that increase the pressure.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C  because  diffraction is the name given to the spreading out of waves as they pass through a gap, as shown in the diagram below.  A is incorrect as reflection is what happens when waves bounce off a boundary. B is incorrect as refraction is what happens when waves change speed and (usually) direction when they cross a boundary. D is incorrect as dispersion is the spreading out of the different colours of (usually) light when they are passed through a prism.

questions.stem:
A lit match is placed above a thermometer.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/q3-medium-mcq-2-3-thermal-processes-cie-igcse-physics.png)Which row in the table shows how the thermal energy from the lit match reaches the thermometer?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Convection | Conduction | Radiation |
| A | yes | yes | yes |
| B | yes | yes | no |
| C | no | yes | yes |
| D | no | no | yes |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Air is a terrible thermal conductor. Convection only transfers heat in an upwards direction, and the thermometer is being held beneath the match. Infrared radiation is emitted equally in all directions, so this is the only one that can reach the match. Always look for a direction when dealing with convection questions. Convection always transfers heat upwards .

questions.stem: What is the definition of the word amplitude?
options: A. The number of complete waves that pass a point per second.
B. The distance from the peak of one wave to the peak of an adjacent wave.
C. The distance from the equilibrium position of a peak plus the same distance from a trough.
D. The maximum distance from the equilibrium position of any point on a wave.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Amplitude is shown on the diagram, as is wavelength. Amplitude is the maximum distance from the equilibrium position of any point on a wave.  A is incorrect as this is the definition of frequency. B is incorrect as this is the definition of wavelength. C is incorrect as this is the standard error made by students when defining amplitude.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D  because images in a plane mirror are always reflected left to right but not top to bottom. This diagram shows the actual clock:

questions.stem: Which description of the liver below is correct?
options: A. The liver is a cell, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system.
B. The liver is an organ, containing several systems, which forms part of the digestive tissue
C. The liver is an organ, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system.
D. The liver is a cell, containing several systems, which forms part of the digestive system.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (The liver is an organ, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system) because: The liver is an organ composed of several different tissue types. It plays a vital role in digestion by producing bile which neutralises acidic gastric juice from the stomach. An organ is a structure made up of a group of tissues working together to perform a specific function A tissue is a group of cells with similar structures working together to perform a shared function An organ  system is a group of organs with related functions working together to perform body functions The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly define what the liver is.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is a reason yeast is used to make bread?
Yeast is used to make bread because...
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (it produces carbon dioxide) because: Yeast produces carbon dioxide and ethanol (alcohol) during fermentation, and it is bubbles of carbon dioxide gas that makes the bread rise as it gets trapped in the dough. A is incorrect because while yeast fermentation does result in the production of ethanol , it is the production of the carbon dioxide that makes the bread rise. B is incorrect because lactic acid is a product of anaerobic respiration in animals and some bacteria. D is incorrect because fermentation is anaerobic , meaning that it doesn’t require oxygen, and as a type of respiration does not produce oxygen. The process that produces oxygen is photosynthesis in plants and algae.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of electromagnetic radiation has the highest speed in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: all types of electromagnetic radiation travel at the same speed in a vacuum. That speed is the speed of light: 3 x 10 8 m/s.

What happens to the wavelength of the wave?

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: The wave equation  applies here. Rearrange  : If v doubles, and f stays the same: is twice as big as  , the original wavelength. The other answers are incorrect because they do not get the algebra correct.

questions.stem: Which of the lists of metals below contains only metals which are non-ferrous?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: A ferrous metal contains iron , a non-ferrous metal does not. Aluminium and copper are elements, so they cannot contain iron. Brass is an alloy of copper and tin, which does not contain iron. A is incorrect as iron is ferrous, and steel is an alloy of iron. B is incorrect as steel is an alloy of iron, which is ferrous. D is incorrect as iron is ferrous.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows a toaster that has been wired up.
Three fuses have been connected to the toaster, but only one or two have been connected correctly.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/q6-medium-mcq-4-3-electrical-circuits-cie-igcse-physics.png)Which of the fuses has been positioned correctly?
options: A. Fuse X and fuse Y
D. Fuse X and fuse Z
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: A fuse must be connected in series with the live wire. Only fuse X is in the correct position. A is incorrect as fuse Y is in series with the neutral wire. It is in the wrong position. C is incorrect as fuse Z is connected in parallel with the heating element. This is really badly in the wrong position, would cause a short circuit, and would blow fuse Z as soon as the circuit was switched on. D is incorrect as X is in the correct position but Z is badly positioned, in parallel with the heating element. It would cause a short circuit, and would blow fuse Z as soon as the circuit was switched on

questions.stem:
This is the circuit symbol for which component?

questions.stem:
The graph below shows the results of an investigation into how the rate of respiration of an organism is affected by changing the temperature.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/02/12--image-2-respiration-rat.png)Which of the following statements would explain the difference between the rate of respiration at 10 °C and that at 30 °C?
options: A. Enzyme activity is higher at 30 °C because more frequent collisions are occurring than at 10 °C.
B. Enzyme activity at 30 °C is lower because the bonds holding an enzyme together are altered at higher temperatures.
C. Enzyme activity is at its optimum at 30 °C, meaning the rate is at its highest.
D. Enzyme activity is lower at 10 °C because the enzymes are denatured and therefore unable to bind to their substrates.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (enzyme activity is higher at 30 °C because more frequent collisions are occurring than at 10 °C) because: Increasing the temperature of an enzyme to its optimum increases the rate of the chemical reaction it catalyses as enzymes and substrates will have more kinetic energy and therefore will collide successfully more often. B is incorrect because the graph shows the rate of the enzyme’s activity increasing up to 40°C, so the bonds holding the structure together cannot have been altered. C is incorrect because the optimum for the enzyme is somewhere between 30°C and 50°C. D is incorrect because enzymes are denatured at temperatures above their optimum, not at low temperatures.

questions.stem:
When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, an e.m.f. is induced in the wire.
Which of the following devices uses this effect?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, the induced e.m.f. can be used to drive a current The combination of current and voltage can deliver electrical power to devices ( P = IV ), which causes them to work This is the process used by a generator to produce electricity A is incorrect as an electric motor works using the reverse effect: when a current is passed through a wire in a magnetic field, it experiences a force. C is incorrect as a photon accelerator is a fictitious device, popularised on a children’s TV show in the early 90s called “Bucky O’Hare”. One might argue that a light bulb accelerates photons. D is incorrect as a transformer uses the induction effect, but does not use a moving wire, it uses an alternating magnetic field to create the same effect.

questions.stem:
After electricity is generated at a power station, the voltage is increased significantly for transmission across the country via the national grid.
What is the advantage of transmitting electricity at very high voltages?
options: A. It makes the electricity flow more quickly.
B. It increases the efficiency of the electricity transfer.
D. It is safer to transmit electricity at high voltage.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Since P = IV , when the voltage increases, the current decreases This is because the electrical power must be the same before and after transforming, otherwise, you create or destroy energy, which is not possible The lower the current, the less power is dissipated as heat in the power lines If less power is wasted, the transmission is more efficient A is incorrect as electricity does not flow more or less quickly due to the voltage. C is incorrect as power cannot be created or destroyed due to the conservation of energy. If the voltage goes up, the current comes down to compensate, since P = IV. options: A. The number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
B. The number of protons is equal to the number of neutrons.
C. The number of electrons, protons and neutrons are all different.
D. The number of electrons is equal to the number of neutrons.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Protons have a charge of +1. Electrons have a charge of -1. For an atom to be neutral , the positive charges and negative charges must be equal . Therefore the number of protons must be the same as the number of electrons. B and D are incorrect as neutrons have no charge so do not affect the overall charge of the atom. C is incorrect as atoms can have different numbers of neutrons and still be neutral.

questions.stem:
Fruit flies can have orange or red eyes.
If two orange flies are crossed, all of the offspring will have orange eyes.
If two red eyed fruit flies are crossed, the offspring have either orange or red eyes.
What can be concluded from these observations?
options: A. The allele for orange eyes is dominant.
B. Crossing an orange-eyed fly with a red-eyed fly will give a 1:1 ratio.
C. The allele for red eyes is dominant.
D. We could determine which allele is dominant only if we did further crosses that produced a 3:1 ratio.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (The allele for red eyes is dominant) because: Dominant characteristics will show even if a recessive allele is present in the genotype (for example in an heterozygous individual) Organisms that are orange-eyed must be recessive as when crossed offspring always have orange-eyes In order for there to be a mixture of red and orange-eyed individuals the red-eyed flies must have been heterozygous If R  = red eyes and r = orange eyes then the Punnett square for two orange-eyed individuals would be: r r r rr rr r rr rr The cross for red-eyed flies would be: R r R RR Rr r Rr rr A is incorrect because if the allele for orange eyes was dominant, then the results of the two red-eyed fly cross would be all red eyes and in this case the red eyes trait would be recessive (rr) B is incorrect because the 1:1 ratio would depend on the genotype of the red-eyed fly in the cross and can’t be concluded from the information given. D is incorrect because we do not need to do a cross to find the 3:1 ratio just to find out which of the alleles are dominant.

C. The car is accelerating because its velocity is changing
D. The car is not accelerating, but its velocity is changing.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because This is a circular motion question . Velocity is defined as the speed in a given direction, if either the speed or the direction change, then the velocity changes. Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity . questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Compare the mass and velocity of each rollercoaster: The first rollercoaster has mass m and velocity v The second rollercoaster has mass ½ m and velocity 4 v Momentum = mass x velocity, or p = m x v The momentum of the first rollercoaster is p = m x v = mv The momentum of the second rollercoaster is p = (½ m ) x (4 v ) = 2 mv Therefore, the momentum of the second rollercoaster will be twice that of the first rollercoaster's momentum

This is because water has left the cells and they have become flaccid, providing less support to the overall structure of the leaf. If a cell does not contain enough water there is no pressure pushing outwards against the cell wall and the cells will all shrink a little. A is incorrect because a decrease in light intensity would just reduce the rate of photosynthesis, not cause the plant to wilt. B is incorrect because an increase in humidity would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water. D is incorrect because a decrease in wind speed would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water.

questions.stem:
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a mobile phone battery is 3.7 V. 
What does this mean?
options: A. 3.7 J is the maximum energy the battery can provide in 1.0 s.
B. 3.7 J is the total energy the battery can provide before it has to be recharged.
C. 3.7 J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a charge of 1.0 C around a complete circuit.
D. 3.7 J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a current of 1.0 A around a complete circuit.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The e.m.f. is defined as the electrical work done by a source in moving a unit charge around a complete circuit If the battery has an e.m.f. of 3.7 V, that means it takes 3.7 J to move 1.0 C of charge around a circuit A is incorrect as this describes the power (energy transferred per second) B is incorrect as this describes the total energy in the battery’s chemical energy store D is incorrect as e.m.f. is the energy required to move charge, not current

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a use of ultrasound?
options: A. Scanning a fetus during pregnancy
B. Non-destructive testing of materials such as to find leaks in copper pipes
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Broken bones are imaged using x-rays The other options are all key uses of ultrasound waves

questions.stem: Which statement about a permanent bar magnet is incorrect?
options: A. The S-pole attracts the N-pole of another magnet
B. The S-pole repels the S-pole of another magnet
C. It cannot repel a non-magnetic material
D. It is made from a soft magnetic material (such as soft iron)
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is D because: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field This means it never loses its magnetism Most permanent magnets are made from 'hard' iron, nickel, or cobalt A soft magnetic material, such as soft iron, will only be magnetic whilst there is a current around it (such as in an electromagnet) Once the current is switched off, it is demagnetised (loses its magnetism) This means it wouldn't work as a permanent magnet A is correct as opposite poles attract, so an S-pole will attract the N-pole of another magnet B is correct as like poles repel, so an S-pole will repel the S-pole of another magnet C is correct as permanent magnets can only attract or repel other magnetic materials, so it is true that they cannot repel non-magnetic materials

questions.stem:
A PVC (plastic) rod is rubbed with a nylon cloth. This process causes electrons to be transferred between the rod and the cloth, causing both objects to become charged.
Which row gives the correct nature of the charges on both the cloth and the rod, and the effect the objects have on each other after becoming charged?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Charges on rod and cloth | Effect |
| A | the same | repel |
| B | the same | attract |
| C | opposite | repel |
| D | opposite | attract |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: When the rod is rubbed with the cloth, electrons are transferred between them If electrons move from the cloth, the cloth becomes positive If electrons move to the rod, the rod becomes negative This means the two objects have opposite charges Opposite charges attract A and B are incorrect as the charges will be opposite. C is incorrect as opposite charges will attract, not repel.

questions.stem: In which of the following situations would no resultant force be required?
options: A. A motorbike travelling round a bend at a constant speed.
B. A rocket accelerating straight upwards into space.
C. A ship sailing at a constant speed across the ocean.
D. A Formula One car accelerating off the starting grid.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Objects which travel at a constant speed in a straight line need no resultant force. All the other objects are either changing speed, or direction, both of which require a resultant force. A is incorrect as the motorbike is changing direction when going round a bend, this requires a resultant force. B is incorrect as the rocket is accelerating, this requires a resultant force. D is incorrect as the car is accelerating, this requires a resultant force.

questions.stem:
When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, an e.m.f. is induced in the wire.
Which of the following devices uses this effect?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: When a wire is moved through a magnetic field, the induced e.m.f. can be used to drive a current The combination of current and voltage can deliver electrical power to devices ( P = IV ), which causes them to work This is the process used by a generator to produce electricity A is incorrect as an electric motor works using the reverse effect: when a current is passed through a wire in a magnetic field, it experiences a force. C is incorrect as a photon accelerator is a fictitious device, popularised on a children’s TV show in the early 90s called “Bucky O’Hare”. One might argue that a light bulb accelerates photons. D is incorrect as a transformer uses the induction effect, but does not use a moving wire, it uses an alternating magnetic field to create the same effect.

questions.stem:
After electricity is generated at a power station, the voltage is increased significantly for transmission across the country via the national grid.
What is the advantage of transmitting electricity at very high voltages?
options: A. It makes the electricity flow more quickly.
B. It increases the efficiency of the electricity transfer.
D. It is safer to transmit electricity at high voltage.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Since P = IV , when the voltage increases, the current decreases This is because the electrical power must be the same before and after transforming, otherwise, you create or destroy energy, which is not possible The lower the current, the less power is dissipated as heat in the power lines If less power is wasted, the transmission is more efficient A is incorrect as electricity does not flow more or less quickly due to the voltage. C is incorrect as power cannot be created or destroyed due to the conservation of energy. If the voltage goes up, the current comes down to compensate, since P = IV. D is incorrect as high voltage transmission is much less safe than low voltage transmission, but the rewards are worth the risk.

questions.stem: Which device uses a split ring commutator?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: a d.c. motor uses a split ring commutator to reverse the direction of the current through the coil every half turn, and, therefore, to keep it spinning in the same direction. a.c. generators use slip rings, transformers have no moving parts, and relays use no rings at all.

questions.stem:
A nucleus of uranium ( ) is unstable and decays by emitting an α-particle. 
Which equation correctly describes this process?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A : An α -particle consists of two protons and two neutrons. When a nuclide emits an α -particle, the nuclide loses two protons and two neutrons. This means the proton number reduces by two and the nucleon number reduces by four. Nuclear equations must be balanced , which means the sum of the nucleon numbers on the left of the equation must equal the sum on the right. The same goes for the proton numbers. Since the proton number has changed, this means that it is a different element. B is incorrect as in this answer the numbers are correct, but since the proton number has changed then this element is no longer uranium (U). C is incorrect as this equation does not describe the decay. Uranium is the nuclide which decays into α -particle and another nuclide. Therefore, the α -particle should be on the right hand side. You should also notice that this equation is not balanced. D is incorrect as this equation is not balanced, the total proton number on the left hand side is 92, and on the right hand side is 88+2=90. Therefore this cannot be correct.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because the number of neutrons is found by subtracting the number of protons (13) from the total atomic mass (27). A is incorrect as this is the proton number. This tells us the number of protons in the nucleus of an aluminium atom. B is incorrect as this is the nucleon number. This tells us the number of protons plus the number of neutrons in the nucleus of an aluminium atom . D is incorrect as this number does not represent the number of neutrons. We never add the proton number to the nucleon/mass number.

questions.stem:
During vigorous exercise, such as cycling uphill, lactic acid builds up in the muscles.
How is this lactic acid removed during recovery?
options: A. excretion of lactic acid by the kidneys
B. anaerobic respiration of lactic acid in the muscles
C. aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver
D. excretion of lactic acid by the lungs
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver) because: Lactic acid builds up in skeletal muscle cells during vigorous exercise It is mainly excreted into the blood, and when the blood passes through the liver lactic acid is taken up by liver cells where it reacts with oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water (and releasing energy) As lactic acid is therefore being broken down with oxygen (and energy is being released), this is an example of aerobic respiration A is incorrect because the kidneys can also break down lactic acid (using oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water) but they do not excrete lactic acid. B is incorrect because anaerobic respiration in the muscles produces lactic acid. D is incorrect because lactic acid is not excreted by the lungs (the carbon dioxide produced in aerobic respiration is).

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: We are looking for the corkscrew with the greatest moment. In D , both forces are acting in an anticlockwise direction about the pivot. Both forces are the maximum distance away from the pivot (in the centre), which means the moment will be the maximum. A is incorrect as the forces act in opposite directions (the topmost F is in the clockwise direction, the bottommost F is in the anticlockwise moment), so they cancel each other out. B is incorrect as one of the forces is only halfway along the corkscrew handle and although both forces act in the anticlockwise direction about the pivot, because one of the moments is only halfway along the corkscrew, the combined moment in B is less than combined moments in corkscrew D . questions.stem:
The image below shows a simple reflex arc.

|  |  |
|---|---|
|  | first  →  last |
| A | Z   →    X   →    Y |
| B | X   →   Y    →   Z |
| C | Y  →     X   →    Z |
| D | Z   →    Y   →    X |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Receptor cells are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that is then sent along a sensory neurone (Z) to the coordinator (the brain or spinal cord) The impulse is then passed to a relay neurone (X) which is a short neurone found inside the coordinator and connects sensory neurones to motor neurones The impulse is then passed on to a motor neurone (Y) which connects to an effector, in this case a muscle, stimulating it to contract and bring about a response B is incorrect because a reflex action cannot start with the relay neurone (X). C is incorrect because the order of neurones is back-to-front from effector (muscle) to receptor, only effectors can carry out a response when signalled by an impulse from a motor neurone (Y) which requires impulses originating from the receptor. D is incorrect because impulses pass along neurones in sequential order, an impulse cannot jump from a sensory neurone to a motor neurone.

A student is timing the rate of cooling of a beaker of water. On a repeat run of the investigation, the student forgets to zero the stopwatch.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Cooling time = end time − start time Firstly, consider the minutes 23 − 11 = 12 minutes Then consider the seconds 27 − 19 = 8 seconds Cooling time = 12 minutes and 8 seconds It is important to work out the minutes and the seconds separately, because if the number of seconds at the end time is greater than the number of seconds at the start time, you will need to adjust the number of minutes. Remember that there are only 60 seconds in a minute, so time calculations can't be done easily with decimals. Another method, would be to convert everything into seconds, do the calculation, and convert the answer into minutes.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: As the temperature of air molecules increases, they move more quickly, and tend to be further apart, on average. This makes the air less dense. Less dense substances float on more dense substances. A is incorrect as the molecules themselves remain exactly the same size and shape. They absolutely do not expand. This is a very common misconception among students. C is incorrect as the air molecules do not contract, either. questions.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of natural selection?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (selection by humans) because: Within populations there will always be variation Natural selection is the ‘favouring’ of a characteristic giving an individual a survival advantage over others: individuals with these characteristics are better adapted to the environment (remember the environment determines what is ‘favoured’ or ‘selected’) and therefore these individuals are more likely to survive and reproduce Variation increases the capability of a population to survive and cope with environmental change Artificial selection is carried out by humans selecting specific traits and deciding which individuals in a population (of livestock animals or plant crops) are able to breed. This is not a feature of natural selection All the other answers are incorrect because they are features of natural selection: Production of a large number of offspring will mean that there will be a larger range of phenotypes from the inheritance of random mutations in sexually reproducing organisms Competition for resources means that only the best suited to the environment are likely to survive Variation in the population means that there are a wide variety of genotypes and therefore phenotypes; making the population as a whole better able to adapt to changes in the environment

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because North poles will repel North poles of other permanent magnets. B is incorrect as soft magnetic materials lose their magnetism quickly. A permanent magnet would not be permanent if it were made from a soft magnetic material. C is incorrect as magnetic materials become magnets when placed in a magnetic field. questions.stem:
A student wants to investigate the effect of air resistance on the swing of a pendulum.
Plan an experiment which will enable him to investigate how air resistance changes the way in which a pendulum swings.
The apparatus available includes:
a light wooden rod, approximately 80cm long with a hole at one end, through which a nail will fit
a piece of modelling clay to act as a pendulum bob, as shown in Fig. 4.1
a sheet of thick card which will provide the air resistance when the pendulum swings.
In your plan, you should:
• list any additional apparatus needed

• explain briefly how you would carry out the experiment including exactly which measurements should be taken

• state the key variables that you would control

• draw a table, or tables, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use your readings to reach a conclusion.

You may add to Fig. 4.1 or draw an additional diagram if it helps to explain your plan.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/11/p4-4.PNG)
questions.explanation: To investigate the effect of air resistance on the swing of a pendulum. State the additional apparatus: Any one from: Stop watch; [1 mark] Meter rule; [1 mark] Protractor; [1 mark] State a suitable method: Any one from: Affix / secure / glue the card to the pendulum bob in order to provide air resistance; [1 mark] Allow the pendulum to swing; [1 mark] Measure the time taken OR the distance moved by the pendulum bob OR the angle the pendulum passes through; [1 mark] Describe a way to obtain multiple results for comparison: Repeat (the experiment) for a different value of the independent variable, the area of the card;  [1 mark] List the control variables: Any one from: Length of the pendulum; [1 mark] Angle of release; [1 mark] Mass of the bob; [1 mark] Draw a suitable table: Area of the card/cm 2 Time period / s Repeat 1 Repeat 2 Average OR Area of the card/cm 2 Distance moved by bob/cm Repeat 1 Repeat 2 Average OR Area of the card/cm 2 Angle subtended by bob/cm Repeat 1 Repeat 2 Average Suitable table with clear headings and units; [1 mark] Discuss how to analyse the results: Compare the readings to see if a change in air resistance produces change in dependent variable e.g. see if a change in the area of card changes the time period of oscillation; [1 mark] OR Plot a graph of the independent variable (x-axis) vs the dependent variable (y-axis) to see if there is a relationship; [1 mark] Give a final additional point: Any one from: Time 10 oscillations / swings (and calculate the period of one swing); [1 mark] Use a small angle of swing; [1 mark] Take at least 5 sets of data (5 values of the independent variable used); [1 mark] Repeat each measurement and take an average; [1 mark] Adjust the mass of the pendulum to compensate for changing the mass of card when area is removed, ensuring bob mass remains constant; [1 mark] Repeat with different length of pendulum / mass of bob; [1 mark] Measure the length to the centre of bob / centre of gravity of pendulum; [1 mark] Use a fiducial aid e.g. a marker for the midpoint of the swing; [1 mark]  An example of an answer which would score 7 marks is: The student should attach a known area of the card to the bob using glue [1 mark] . They should use a stopwatch [1 mark] to record the time period of 10 oscillations of the pendulum [1 mark] and calculate the time period for one swing. The experiment should be repeated with a smaller area of card [1 mark] . The length of the pendulum should be constant throughout the experiment [1 mark] . The results should be recorded in the following table [1 mark for a correct table] Area of the card/cm 2 Time period / s Repeat 1 Repeat 2 Average The readings should be compared to see if a change in the area of card changes the time period of oscillation [1 mark]  [Total: 7 marks] The example above shows the kind of short descriptions which easily score full marks in the exam. The most common mistakes with the investigation question are; Saying what the result will be, rather than how to draw the conclusion; Forgetting that only one variable can change per investigation, and changing all of them; Showing repeat readings or the range in the table, but not mentioning them in the description (it seems unfair, but this won't get you the mark); Wasting time by inventing data for the table. If you find yourself doing one of these - stop !

questions.stem:
A chemical test is carried out on a flax seed as follows:

options: B. iodine solution test for starch
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. The emulsion test is used to detect lipids in a sample As the test tube contains a milky/cloudy emulsion, the flaxseeds must contain lipids which are soluble in ethanol A is incorrect because a positive result of the Biuret test for proteins is a colour change from blue to lilac, not formation of a cloudy emulsion. C is incorrect because, while the test described does involve ethanol, it is called the emulsion test (not the ethanol test) and it detects lipids broadly, not oils specifically.

questions.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in remote controls?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Remote controls contain an infrared LED at the front. This is used to send coded signals to the TV that cannot be seen by the human eye. It is possible, with certain mobile phone cameras, to see this infrared LED flashing when a button is pressed on a remote control. Give it a go. It won’t work with Apple phones as they include an IR filter over the lens of their cameras. A is incorrect as microwaves are used for mobile phone and satellite communication, and for cooking in microwave ovens. B is incorrect as visible light is used to see things. C is incorrect as ultraviolet radiation is used to kill bacteria, to make security features in secure documents and banknotes glow and to make people’s clothes and teeth glow at nightclubs. Oh, it also gives you a suntan and causes skin cancer.

questions.stem: When light passes from a denser material into a less dense material

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: When light passes from a denser medium into a less dense medium It speeds up It bends away from the normal

That would make D microwaves. A is incorrect as this would be X-rays. B is incorrect as this would be ultraviolet light. C is incorrect as this would be visible light.

questions.stem: Which of the following describe prevention methods for rickets?
options: A. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of protein, adequate intake of iron.
B. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of calcium, avoid exposure to sunlight
C. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of calcium, exposure to sunlight
D. foods that are high in vitamin D, vitamin A supplementation, adequate intake of fibre
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Rickets is a deficiency condition, caused by a lack of vitamin D, that is characterised by soft, weak bones Vitamin D supplementation ensures adequate vitamin D levels Sunlight can stimulate the body to naturally produce vitamin D Calcium is an essential mineral for bones and teeth A is incorrect as protein and iron do not prevent rickets. B is incorrect as sunlight exposure stimulates the body to produce vitamin D, so it should not be avoided. D is incorrect as vitamin A and fibre do not prevent rickets.

questions.stem: What is the correct unit of charge?

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: All the bulbs are connected in parallel , and so will have the same potential difference across them. The rating of 10 W is not needed for the question. A is incorrect as some of the bulbs are in series with each other. This means that the potential difference will split between them, reducing their power output, and making them dimmer. B and C are incorrect as some of the bulbs are in series with each other. This means that the potential difference will split between them, reducing their power output, and making them dimmer.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about the current in ammeters X, Y and Z is correct?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/q6-hard-mcq-4-3-electrical-circuits-cie-igcse-physics.png)
options: A. The current through X equals the current through Y + the current through Z.
B. The current through X is equal to the current through Z.
C. The current through X is equal to the current through Y.
D. The current through Y is greater than the current through Z.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Observe that the two resistors are connected in parallel For resistors connected in parallel, the current before the resistors (X) is the sum of the current in each resistor In other words, the current at Y cannot be greater than or equal to the current at X or Z It should be clear that the current before and after the resistors must be the same A is incorrect as X is equal to Z, so it cannot equal Y + Z C is incorrect as the current splits as it enters the junction between the two resistors, therefore, some current must go to the lower resistor, meaning current X cannot equal current Y. D is incorrect as the current through Y adds to the current through the bottom resistor, and gives current Z. Therefore Z cannot equal Y.

questions.stem:
A student considers how changing the diameter and length of a wire affects its resistance.
Which row shows the changes that could be made to the length and diameter of the wire to decrease its resistance?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Change to length | Change to diameter |
| A | increase | increase |
| B | increase | decrease |
| C | decrease | increase |
| D | decrease | decrease |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The resistance of a wire is directly  proportional to its length Therefore, a shorter wire would give a lower resistance The resistance of a wire is inversely  proportional to its diameter Therefore, a larger diameter wire would give a lower resistance A is incorrect as increasing the length would increase the resistance of the wire. B is incorrect as both of these factors would increase the resistance of the wire. D is incorrect as decreasing the diameter would increase the resistance of the wire.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: In a simple a.c. generator a coil rotates between magnetic poles (or a magnet rotates around a coil) This causes the voltage to rise, then fall, then to rise in the opposite direction, then fall, and to repeat in this manner This produces a graph with a sine or cosine curve, which is shown by graph B A & C are incorrect as the voltage is never negative in these graphs. An a.c. generator makes the voltage negative every half cycle. D is incorrect as this graph shows d.c. (direct current)

questions.stem:
A potometer is used to measure the rate of transpiration. The table below shows the results.


|  |  |
|---|---|
| Distance travelled by bubble (mm) | Time (mins) |
| 0 | 0 |
| 17 | 30 |
| 29 | 60 |
| 35 | 90 |
| 44 | 120 |
| 51 | 150 |
Calculate the rate of transpiration between 30 and 120 minutes.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. To calculate the rate of transpiration:  Calculate the distance travelled by the bubble between 120 min and 30 min: = 44 - 17 = 27 mm Calculate the time that passes between 120 and 30 mins: = 120 - 30 = 90 min Calculate the rate of transpiration: = 27 ÷ 90 = 0.3 mm / min A is incorrect as it corresponds to dividing 44 mm by 120 mins, i.e. it is the rate of transpiration between 0 and 120 mins, not between 30 and 120 mins. C is incorrect as this is what you get if you divide time by distance (90 ÷ 27) rather than distance by time. D is incorrect as this is the correct calculation but the wrong unit. Always remember to calculate the change in distance and the change in time rather than using the raw values from the table. Ensure that you include the correct units in your final answer.

questions.stem: Which statement about α-particles is correct?
options: A. α- particles consist of two protons and two electrons.
B. α- particles are the most penetrating type of radiation.
C. α- particles are a type of electromagnetic radiation.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: α -particles have a positive charge of +2 and an atomic mass of 4 This makes them heavier and more charged than other types of radiation For this reason, they are more likely to interact with matter, causing ionisation A is incorrect as α -particles consist of two protons and two neutrons. This means they have an overall charge of +2. They don’t contain any electrons. B is incorrect as γ -rays are the most penetrating. C is incorrect as γ -rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: When a nuclide decays by β emission, a neutron decays into a proton plus a β -particle. This is shown in the diagram below. When this occurs, the proton number increases by 1 but the nucleon number doesn’t change. A is incorrect as an α -particle is two protons and two neutrons. If strontium decayed by emitting this particle, the nucleon number would reduce by four and the proton number would reduce by two. B is incorrect as if a nuclide emitted a neutron, the nucleon number would decrease by one but the proton number would stay the same. C is incorrect as γ -rays are not particles. If a nuclide emits a γ -ray, the proton and neutron number remain the same.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the process of transpiration is correct?
options: A. water moves upwards from the roots

C. water evaporates directly from the stomata

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves, which occurs by diffusion through the stomata A is incorrect as this does not describe transpiration, which is the loss of water vapour from leaves. The movement of water upwards from the roots is known as the transpiration stream. B is incorrect as increasing wind speed increases the rate of transpiration. C is incorrect as water evaporates from the surfaces of the mesophyll cells, not directly from the stomata.

questions.stem:
Below are statements about methods of controlling the spread of disease.
• Boiling drinking water reduces the risk of transmitting waterborne pathogens

• Disinfecting surfaces reduces the risk of transmitting pathogens via direct contact

• Collecting food waste in sealed bins reduces the likelihood of animals spreading pathogens

• Treating sewage before releasing it into rivers prevents the direct transmission of pathogens between individuals

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Statement 1 is correct: boiling drinking water kills pathogens, reducing the risk of waterborne transmission Statement 3 is correct: collecting food waste in sealed bins prevents animals from accessing waste and spreading pathogens Statement 2 is incorrect as disinfecting surfaces reduces indirect transmission via contaminated surfaces, not direct transmission between individuals. Statement 4 is incorrect as sewage treatment prevents indirect transmission via contaminated water, not direct transmission between individuals.

questions.stem:
Below are statements about the features of gas exchange surfaces in humans.
• Gas exchange surfaces have a large surface area to maximise the rate of diffusion

• Gas exchange surfaces have a thick surface to prevent damage from the constant movement of air

• Gas exchange surfaces have a good blood supply to remove gases that have diffused across the surface

• Gas exchange surfaces are well ventilated to increase the concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Statement 1 is correct: a large surface area increases the rate of diffusion of gases across the gas exchange surface Statement 3 is correct: a good blood supply removes oxygen from the lung capillaries after it has diffused into the blood, maintaining the concentration gradient for further diffusion Statement 2 is incorrect as gas exchange surfaces are thin, not thick in order to maximise the rate of diffusion. Statement 4 is incorrect as good ventilation maintains a high concentration of oxygen and a low concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli, not a high concentration of carbon dioxide.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: If two materials are made from the same material, their density must be the same. questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about excretion in humans?
options: A. carbon dioxide, excess water and ions are excreted by the lungs
B. urea and excess water are excreted by the kidneys
C. urea is transported from the kidneys to the bladder via the urethra
D. the bladder connects the kidneys to the urethra
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The kidneys excrete urea and excess water from the body Ions are also excreted by the kidneys, but their omission does not make this statement incorrect A is incorrect as, although carbon dioxide and some water vapour are excreted through the lungs, ions are not — they are excreted by the kidneys. C is incorrect as urea leaves the kidneys in the urine, which is transported to the bladder via the ureters. The urethra connects the bladder to the exterior. D is incorrect as the bladder does not connect the kidneys to anything. The kidneys are connected to the bladder via the ureters, and the bladder is connected to the exterior via the urethra.

questions.stem:

This is the smallest amount of work in the table. A is incorrect as 20 x 20 = 400 J B is incorrect as 40 x 10 = 400 J C is incorrect as 50 x 6.0 = 300 J

| C | decreases | increases |
