questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: The average kinetic energy of the molecules in a substance is proportional to the temperature of the substance. So as the temperature in the bottle rises, the average kinetic energy per molecule will also increase. Since  KE =  , increasing the kinetic energy also increases the speed of the air molecules. Pressure against the inside walls of the container is caused by the air molecules colliding with the walls. The faster the molecules are moving, the greater the force they apply when they collide with the container. As the volume of the container remains constant, the area over which this force is exerted remains constant. Remember Since the air molecules are moving faster, they exert more pressure on the walls of the container. The other answers have one or both of the statements incorrect, for the reasons outlined above.

questions.stem: A person touches a pin. Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events in the resulting reflex arc?
options: A. pin → receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
B. pin → receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
C. pin → receptor → relay neurone → sensory neurone → motor neurone → effector
D. pin → effector → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → receptor
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. When a finger touches a pin, touch receptors detect the stimulus and a nerve impulse is sent along the sensory neurone to the relay neurone in the spinal cord The relay neurone passes the impulse to the motor neurone, which carries it to the effector, causing the arm muscles to contract and withdraw the finger B is incorrect as the impulse travels along the sensory neurone first, not the motor neurone. Motor neurones carry impulses away from the CNS to the effector. A helpful way to remember this is that sensory neurones connect to sense organs, such as the skin. C is incorrect as the impulse travels along the sensory neurone before reaching the relay neurone, not the other way round. D is incorrect as the sequence begins at the receptor, not the effector. Receptors detect stimuli at the start of the reflex arc, whereas effectors, such as muscles, produce the response at the end.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a metal experiencing thermal expansion?
options: A. The size of the metal atoms increases
B. The space between the metal atoms increases
C. The metal atoms change state
D. The metal atoms gain enough energy to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction holding them in place
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Expansion happens because the atoms gain energy and move faster Therefore, the space between the atoms increases It is a common misconception that the size of the atoms / molecules / particles increases with expansion. This is not true! As the particles move more and more with the gain in energy, the space between the particles increases. This is true for a solid, a liquid, and a gas.

questions.stem: What is the unit of wave speed?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Wave speed is a measure of how much distance a wave crosses per second. The units are, therefore, of distance / time, or metres / seconds, metres per second. A is incorrect as this is the unit of frequency. B is incorrect as this is the unit of wavelength, and sometimes amplitude as well. C is incorrect as this is the unit of time period.

questions.stem:
Water waves travel from deeper water to more shallow water. This causes them to refract.
Which wave property always remains the same when refraction occurs?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Every wavefront that hits the boundary has to leave the boundary. Since frequency is defined as the number of waves (or wavefronts) that pass a point per second, this has to be the same on both sides of the boundary. Anything else can change. A is incorrect as wavelength changes when a wave refracts. C is incorrect as amplitude can change when a wave refracts, especially if the water's depth changes. D is incorrect as by definition, speed changes when a wave refracts.

questions.stem:
A palisade mesophyll cell is found near the upper surface of a leaf and contains many chloroplasts.
Why is this an effective adaptation?
options: A. It reduces water loss by closing stomata.
B. It allows the cell to absorb more light for photosynthesis.
C. It increases the surface area for gas exchange.
D. It allows the cell to respire at a higher rate.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. A palisade mesophyll cell is packed with many chloroplasts and is found near the upper surface of the leaf, where light intensity is highest This means it can absorb more light energy for photosynthesis A is incorrect because palisade mesophyll cells do not close stomata; that is the role of guard cells. C is incorrect because the palisade mesophyll layer does not have a notably large surface area. Increasing surface area for gas exchange is mainly the role of the spongy mesophyll, which has large air spaces that allow gases to diffuse through the leaf. D is incorrect because although the cell does respire, the key adaptation described here is for photosynthesis, not increased respiration.

questions.stem: Why are enzymes said to be specific?
options: A. Each enzyme can only work at one temperature.
B. Each enzyme has an active site with a complementary shape to a particular substrate.

A student investigates the effect of the colour of the surface of a metal container on the rate of loss of heat from the container. She knows that black surfaces are better radiators of thermal energy than white surfaces and wants to investigate the effect of other colours.

She can also use other apparatus and materials that are usually available in a school laboratory.

You should:

• explain briefly how you would carry out the investigation

• state the key variables to be kept constant

• draw a table, or tables, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use your readings to reach a conclusion.
questions.explanation:
To investigate the effect of surface colour on rate of heat loss: Draw a labelled diagram to show how to set up the equipment:  Thermometer shown in the container; [1 mark] Briefly outline the method: Put hot water in container AND record starting temperature AND temperature at regular intervals; [1 mark] 
 OR Put hot water in container AND record starting temperature AND temperature after a named amount of time; [1 mark] Specify the range: Repeat with at least three colours; [1 mark] Identify the control variables and state at least two: Same starting temperature of the water; [1 mark] 
 OR 
 Same room temperature; [1 mark] Use of a lid; [1 mark] 
 OR Three (or more) named colours; [1 mark] 
 OR Same thickness of paint; [1 mark] Draw a table showing columns and units:  Correctly labelled columns for all variables AND  units; [1 mark] Explain how to draw a conclusion from the results: Greatest loss of temperature is best radiator OR  least loss of temperature is worst radiator / best insulator: [1 mark] An example of an answer which would score 7 marks is:  [diagram with thermometers in containers: 1 mark] The student should take the black and white containers and place them on the bench at the same time (same room temperature). [1 mark] Then they take three identical containers but choosing three colours, for example yellow, red and green. [1 mark] Make sure that the thickness of paint [1 mark] and material of the container are the same. The student adds a measured volume of boiling water to each container, and decides a starting temperature for the experiment, say 90 °C. Put a thermometer into each container and watch the temperature until it drops to 90 °C. Use a lid to stop heat loss. Start the stopwatch and time for 5 minutes. After five minutes record the new temperature. [1 mark] Finally empty the water out (taking care with hot water - wear safety glasses) and repeat the whole experiment two more times. Record the results in the table and plot a graph. The paint colour with the higest drop in temperature is the best radiator of heat. [1 mark]  [table with correct columns and units ; 1 mark] The example above shows the kind of short descriptions which easily score full marks in the exam. An alternative method would be to take the temperature every minute and this would also score full marks. The most common mistakes with the investigation question are; Saying what the result will be, rather than how to draw the conclusion; Forgetting that only one variable can change, and changing all of them; Showing repeat readings or the range in the table, but not mentioning them in the description (it seems unfair, but this won't get you the mark); Wasting time by inventing data for the table. questions.stem: Which statement best describes a metal experiencing thermal expansion?
options: A. The size of the metal atoms increases
B. The space between the metal atoms increases
C. The metal atoms change state
D. The metal atoms gain enough energy to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction holding them in place
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Expansion happens because the atoms gain energy and move faster Therefore, the space between the atoms increases It is a common misconception that the size of the atoms / molecules / particles increases with expansion. This is not true! As the particles move more and more with the gain in energy, the space between the particles increases. This is true for a solid, a liquid, and a gas.

B. Y boils sooner than X.
C. X has a lower specific heat capacity than Y.
D. Y has a higher boiling point than X.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1℃.  If energy is supplied at the same rate to equal masses of liquid, then the one with the lower specific heat capacity will show the greater temperature change, as it requires less energy to increase its temperature by 1℃ This means that the substance with the steeper gradient on the graph will have the lower specific heat capacity. Therefore X has a lower specific heat capacity than Y. A is incorrect as we have no information about the melting point of either substance. B is incorrect as X actually boils sooner than Y. D is incorrect as X has the higher boiling point.

questions.stem:
Copper(II) sulfate can be prepared by reacting solid copper(II) carbonate with hot sulfuric acid. The copper(II) carbonate is always added in excess.
Why is the solid reactant added in excess?
options: A. To ensure all of the acid reacts.
B. To make the reaction go faster.
C. To ensure all of the solid reactant has reacted.
D. To increase the product yield.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Copper(II) carbonate reacts with sulfuric acid to produce copper(II) sulfate: CuCO 3 + H 2 SO 4 → CuSO 4 + H 2 O + CO 2 Copper(II) sulfate is soluble and is separated from the mixture by evaporation . If there is any acid remaining in the solution it would become dangerously concentrated during this phase of the preparation. For this reason the carbonate is added in excess to make sure that all of the acid has reacted. B and D are incorrect as the rate of reaction and yield are not dependent on there being an excess of only one of the reactants. C is incorrect as any unreacted copper(II) carbonate is removed by filtration .

questions.stem: When gametes are produced, cells undergo division by
options: A. mitosis to produce genetically identical cells.
B. mitosis to produce genetically different cells.
C. meiosis to produce genetically identical cells.
D. meiosis to produce genetically different cells.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Meiosis is the type of cell division that produces gametes (sperm and egg cells) During meiosis, the chromosome number is halved from diploid to haploid , and the resulting cells are genetically different from each other This genetic variation is important for sexual reproduction If the question mentions growth , repair or asexual reproduction , the process is mitosis . Mitosis produces genetically identical cells and keeps the chromosome number the same. If the question mentions gametes or sexual reproduction , the process is meiosis . Meiosis produces haploid gametes that are genetically different , with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

D. Student Y reaches the top of the stairs first because they transfer more energy to their gravitational potential store than student X.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B As the students climb the stairs, they do work against gravity The work done by each student is equal to the energy transferred to the gravitational potential store, which depends on their weight the vertical height climbed Since both students climb the same vertical height, the student with the smaller weight (student Y) does less work Power is defined as the rate of doing work:  For the same average power, a smaller amount of work done results in a shorter time to reach the top of the stairs A is incorrect as student X does more work and will therefore take more time to reach the top given the same power output. C is incorrect because time depends on both power and the amount of work to be done; since the work values are different, the times cannot be the same. questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Sound is a longitudinal wave that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth along the same line, i.e. parallel to the direction of wave travel B is incorrect as longitudinal waves have vibrations parallel to the direction of wave travel, not at right angles. This means that any change in wave speed must be accompanied by a proportional change in wavelength. A useful way to remember this is: when waves slow down, they 'bunch up', resulting in a shorter wavelength.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: This random motion of smoke particles is called Brownian motion . questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Charging by friction involves the transfer of electrons, which are negatively charged particles When a rod becomes negatively charged, it has gained an excess of electrons from the cloth Electrostatic forces follow the rule that opposite charges attract and like charges repel A negatively charged rod will be attracted to an object with a positive charge B is incorrect as unlike charges attract each other, they do not repel C is incorrect because losing electrons would leave the rod with an overall positive charge D is incorrect as losing electrons results in a positive charge, which would be repelled by another positive object but attracted to a negative one Remember the key principles of electrostatics: electrons are the particles that move during charging by friction, and opposite charges attract whilst like charges repel. If an object gains electrons, it becomes negatively charged; if it loses electrons, it becomes positively charged. Many students confuse which way electrons transfer — always think about which material ends up with the excess electrons.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A In nuclide notation  : the top number  is the nucleon (mass) number the bottom number  is the proton (atomic) number Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same proton number but different nucleon numbers Both P and Q have a proton number of 6, which identifies them as the same element Since their nucleon numbers are different (12 and 14), they are isotopes of each other B is incorrect as both atoms have a proton number of 6. C is incorrect because the number of neutrons is calculated as nucleon number − proton number (  ). D is incorrect as 6 is the proton number of P; its nucleon number is 12.

| B | Earth orbits the Sun | Earth rotates on its axis |
| C | Earth rotates on its axis | Earth orbits the Sun |
| D | Earth rotates on its axis | Earth rotates on its axis |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C The Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours This rotation causes the side of the Earth facing the Sun to change, creating the cycle of day and night The Earth orbits the Sun once approximately every 365 days This orbital motion, combined with the tilt of the Earth's axis, causes the periodic cycle of the seasons A is incorrect as the orbit around the Sun is too slow to cause the daily cycle of day and night. questions.stem:

• The Sun is a star of medium size.

• The Sun consists mostly of nitrogen and oxygen.

• The Sun is located inside the Milky Way galaxy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C The Sun is a medium-sized star Therefore, statement 1 is correct The Sun consists mostly of hydrogen and helium, not nitrogen and oxygen Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect The Sun is one of billions of stars that make up the Milky Way galaxy Therefore, statement 3 is correct Remember that the Sun is composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, not nitrogen and oxygen. Many students confuse the composition of the Sun with that of Earth's atmosphere. Also, keep in mind that the Sun is located within the Milky Way galaxy, not outside it.

questions.stem:
Astronomers observe light from distant galaxies and find that the wavelength has increased. This effect is called redshift.
What is the main conclusion from these observations?
options: A. The galaxies are moving away from the Earth and the Universe is expanding.
B. The galaxies are moving towards the Earth and the Universe is contracting.
C. The galaxies are stationary and the speed of light is changing.
D. The Earth is at the exact centre of the Universe.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Redshift occurs when the light observed from an object has a longer wavelength than the light originally emitted This increase in wavelength happens because the source of the light is moving away from the observer Observations of redshift from almost all distant galaxies show that they are moving away from us This provides evidence that the Universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang Theory B is incorrect because moving towards the Earth would cause a decrease in wavelength (blueshift). C is incorrect as the speed of light in a vacuum is a constant and the galaxies are known to be in motion. D is incorrect as the expansion of the Universe happens in all directions and does not imply that the Earth is in a special central position. Remember that redshift indicates objects moving away (wavelength increases), whilst blueshift indicates objects moving towards us (wavelength decreases). The observation that almost all galaxies show redshift is key evidence for the expanding Universe and the Big Bang Theory. Be careful not to confuse the expansion of the Universe with the Earth being at the centre — the expansion occurs uniformly in all directions from any point in space.

questions.stem:
A student investigates how the material of a surface affects the height to which a ball bounces.
The following apparatus is available to the student:
• a selection of balls of similar size

• a clamp, stand, and boss

• samples of different surface materials (e.g., wood, carpet, rubber, tile)

Plan an experiment to investigate how the surface material affects the bounce height of the ball.
In your plan:
• list any additional apparatus needed

• explain briefly how you would carry out the investigation

• state the key variables to keep constant

• draw a table, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use your readings to reach a conclusion.

You may draw a diagram if it helps your explanation.
questions.explanation: Apparatus Use a metre ruler to measure bounce height and a set square to ensure the metre rule is vertical. Method Set up the metre rule vertically using the stand and clamp Place the first surface material (e.g., wood) on the bench at the base of the ruler Hold the ball at a fixed drop height (e.g., 50.0 cm) and release it Observe the maximum height reached by the ball on its first bounce and record it in the table Repeat the drop from the same height at least two more times for this surface and calculate an average bounce height Repeat the entire procedure for at least four other different surface materials Control variables The variables to be controlled are the drop height of the ball and the type of ball used (i.e. use the same ball each time). Table surface material bounce height 1 / cm bounce height 2 / cm bounce height 3 / cm average bounce height / cm Conclusion Compare the average bounce heights for each material by plotting a bar chart with surface material on the x-axis and average bounce height on the y-axis. The tallest bar shows which surface results in the highest bounce. The plan is marked out of 7, with one mark awarded for each of the following points: Apparatus Metre rule [1 mark] Method Valid procedure, e.g. dropping the ball from a fixed point and measuring the bounce height using the ruler [1 mark] Repeat the experiment for at least 3 different surface materials [1 mark] Control variable Drop height [1 mark] Table Table with columns for surface material and bounce height with appropriate units [1 mark] Conclusion/analysis of the data Compare readings in the table to see if different surfaces produce a change in the dependent variable (average height) OR Plot a bar chart of material vs bounce height [1 mark] Additional points Any one from: Method to ensure the metre ruler is vertical / perpendicular to the bench, e.g. use of a set square Method to measure the bounce height more accurately, e.g. use of a video camera / slow-motion phone camera Take at least 5 sets of data Repeat each measurement and take the average Use the same ball / diameter / mass of ball each time [1 mark] In your table headings, always use the format 'Quantity / unit'. If you write "Height (cm)" or just "Height", you may lose the mark. Never just say "repeat the experiment." You must say what you are repeating (e.g., "Repeat for 5 different materials") and why (e.g., "Repeat three times for each material to find an average"). If the apparatus list doesn't include something essential for a fair test, add it! For example, a "fiducial marker" (a pointer) is a great answer for anything involving scales or oscillators. The conclusion mark is usually the easiest mark. If the independent variable is "categories" (like materials), suggest a bar chart . If the independent variable is "numerical" (like length or temperature), suggest a line graph .

questions.stem:
A student wants to find the volume of a small, irregularly shaped stone.
Which pieces of apparatus should the student use?
options: A. a balance and a ruler
B. a measuring cylinder and a balance
C. a measuring cylinder and water
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C An irregularly shaped solid cannot have its volume calculated using length measurements, so a ruler alone is not sufficient The volume of an irregularly shaped solid can be found by the displacement method: The stone is lowered into a measuring cylinder containing a known volume of water The rise in water level equals the volume of the stone This requires a measuring cylinder (to measure the water level before and after) and water (as the displacement liquid) A is incorrect because a balance measures mass, not volume, and a ruler can only measure the volume of a regularly shaped solid (e.g. a cuboid). B is incorrect because a balance is not needed to find volume by displacement. A balance would be needed to find mass (and then density), but the question only asks about volume. D is incorrect because a ruler cannot measure the volume of water displaced by an irregularly shaped object. A measuring cylinder is needed to read the water level accurately.

questions.stem: Which statement about a permanent bar magnet is incorrect?
options: A. The S-pole attracts the N-pole of another magnet
B. The S-pole repels the S-pole of another magnet
C. It cannot repel a non-magnetic material
D. It is made from a soft magnetic material (such as soft iron)
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is D because: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field This means it never loses its magnetism Most permanent magnets are made from 'hard' iron, nickel, or cobalt A soft magnetic material, such as soft iron, will only be magnetic whilst there is a current around it (such as in an electromagnet) Once the current is switched off, it is demagnetised (loses its magnetism) This means it wouldn't work as a permanent magnet A is correct as opposite poles attract, so an S-pole will attract the N-pole of another magnet B is correct as like poles repel, so an S-pole will repel the S-pole of another magnet C is correct as permanent magnets can only attract or repel other magnetic materials, so it is true that they cannot repel non-magnetic materials

D is incorrect because the spring constant is not a point on the graph. The spring constant is found from the gradient of the straight-line section (force per unit extension).

questions.stem:
An oven is wired into somebody’s kitchen. The oven is protected by a fuse, and functions normally, but the owner notices that the wires that connect the oven to the mains electricity supply get quite hot.
What could be done to reduce the temperature of the wires?
options: A. Add a circuit breaker to the circuit.
B. Put thicker insulation on the wires.
C. Replace the wires with thicker diameter wires.
D. Replace the wires with thinner diameter wires.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The problem here is that the wires used to connect the oven are not rated for the amount of current the oven uses. This is an easy mistake to make, as ovens use more current than normal electrical devices. Thicker diameter wires are required, since thicker wires have a smaller resistance, and therefore dissipate less heat when current flows through them. Remember:  gives the power dissipated by a component which has resistance. A is incorrect as this would have no effect, as the oven is operating properly. B is incorrect as thicker insulation might cause the wires to feel cooler, but they would still be just as hot. They would actually be less able to dissipate the heat they are generating, and are in greater danger of causing a fire. D is incorrect as thinner wires would exacerbate the problem. They have a higher resistance, and would dissipate more heat, becoming even hotter.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Tidal energy comes from the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun on the oceans, not solar radiation B is incorrect because wind is caused by differential solar heating. questions.stem:
A balloon is filled with air and tied closed. The balloon is placed in a refrigerator.
What happens to the average speed of the air molecules and the pressure of the air inside the balloon as the temperature decreases?


| ['', 'average speed of air molecules', 'pressure of air'] |
|---|
| A | stays the same | decreases |
| B | decreases | stays the same |
| C | increases | increases |
| D | decreases | decreases |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules When the temperature decreases, the average kinetic energy decreases, so the average speed of the molecules decreases Slower molecules hit the walls of the balloon less frequently and with less force This means the pressure decreases A is incorrect because the average speed of the molecules is directly related to the temperature. If the temperature decreases, the average speed must also decrease. B is incorrect because the pressure does not stay the same. Slower molecules exert less force on the walls of the balloon, so the pressure decreases. C is incorrect because both the average speed and the pressure decrease when the temperature decreases, not increase.

questions.stem:
A plastic rod is rubbed with a cloth. The rod becomes negatively charged.
What has happened during the charging process?
options: A. Protons have been transferred from the rod to the cloth.
B. Electrons have been transferred from the rod to the cloth.
C. Protons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod.
D. Electrons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D When two materials are rubbed together, electrons are transferred from one material to the other Only electrons can be transferred because they are on the outer shells of atoms and can be removed by friction Protons cannot be transferred because they are fixed in the nucleus of the atom The rod becomes negatively charged, which means it has gained electrons Therefore, electrons have been transferred from the cloth to the rod A is incorrect because protons cannot be removed from the nucleus by friction. Charging by friction always involves the transfer of electrons. B is incorrect because if electrons moved from the rod to the cloth, the rod would lose negative charge and become positively charged, not negatively charged. C is incorrect because protons are located in the nucleus of the atom and cannot be transferred by rubbing.

questions.stem:
A liquid evaporates from an open dish.
Which change would increase the rate of evaporation?
options: B. covering the dish with a lid
C. decreasing the surface area of the liquid
D. blowing air across the surface of the liquid
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Evaporation occurs when molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to escape as a gas Blowing air across the surface removes the vapour molecules from above the liquid, preventing them from returning to the liquid and allowing more molecules to escape This increases the rate of evaporation A is incorrect because cooling the liquid reduces the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Fewer molecules will have enough energy to escape from the surface, so the rate of evaporation decreases. B is incorrect because covering the dish traps the vapour above the liquid. The vapour becomes saturated and molecules return to the liquid at the same rate as they leave, so the net rate of evaporation decreases. C is incorrect because decreasing the surface area reduces the number of molecules at the surface that can escape. A larger surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

questions.stem:
Water waves in a ripple tank travel from a region of deep water into a region of shallow water.
Which row correctly describes what happens to the speed and the wavelength of the water waves?


| ['', 'speed', 'wavelength'] |
|---|
| A | increases | decreases |
| B | increases | increases |
| C | decreases | decreases |
| D | decreases | increases |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C When water waves enter a shallower region, the increased interaction with the bottom of the tank causes the waves to travel more slowly The frequency of a wave is determined solely by its source and does not change when the wave enters a different depth According to the wave equation  , if the speed  decreases while the frequency  remains constant, the wavelength  must also decrease A is incorrect because waves travel more slowly in shallow water, not more quickly. B is incorrect as both the speed and the wavelength decrease when moving from deep to shallow water. D is incorrect because wavelength decreases when waves slow down at a constant frequency. Remember that frequency is determined by the source and remains constant when waves travel between different media. This means that any change in wave speed must be accompanied by a proportional change in wavelength. A useful way to remember this is: when waves slow down, they 'bunch up', resulting in a shorter wavelength.

questions.stem: What creates the periodic nature of the seasons?
options: A. The tilting of the Earth's axis
B. The orbiting of the Earth around the Sun
C. The combination of the orbiting of the Earth around the Sun and the Earth's tilting axis
D. The change in temperature of the Sun
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The tilting of the Earth's axis means that certain hemispheres (halves) of the Earth tilt towards the Sun for one half of the year, and away from the Sun from the other half When the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, this is spring and summer When it is tilted away from the Sun, this is autumn and winter The orbiting of the Earth around the Sun means that different sides of the Earth face the Sun at different parts of the year, every 365 days Therefore, the combination of both creates the seasons The tilting of the Earth's axis and its orbit around the Sun is why when it is winter in Europe (in the northern hemisphere), it is summer in Australia (in the southern hemisphere). Whilst Europe is facing away from the Sun during that time, this means Australia is facing towards the Sun, because of the tilt.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a fuse in a mains electrical circuit?
options: A. to reduce the current flowing through the appliance
B. to increase the resistance of the circuit so the appliance works safely
C. to break the circuit if the current becomes too large
D. to prevent the voltage from becoming too high
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C A fuse is a safety device that protects the circuit and the appliance It contains a thin wire that melts when the current exceeds the rated value When the wire melts, the circuit is broken (the current stops flowing) This prevents overheating and reduces the risk of fire Note that in a mains circuit, the fuse is always placed in the live wire A is incorrect because a fuse does not reduce the current. It either allows the current to flow normally or breaks the circuit completely. It does not limit or regulate the current. B is incorrect because the purpose of a fuse is not to increase resistance. A fuse has a very low resistance during normal operation so that it does not affect the circuit. D is incorrect because a fuse responds to excessive current, not voltage. It does not control or limit the voltage in a circuit.

C is incorrect because the number of neutrons is calculated as nucleon number − proton number (  ). D is incorrect as 6 is the proton number of P; its nucleon number is 12.

questions.stem:
A comet is at the point in its orbit where it is furthest from the Sun.
Which row is correct?


| ['', 'orbital speed', 'energy in gravitational potential store'] |
|---|
| A | at its maximum | at its maximum |
| B | at its maximum | at its minimum |
| C | at its minimum | at its maximum |
| D | at its minimum | at its minimum |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Comets travel in highly elliptical orbits around the Sun As a comet moves further away from the Sun, the distance between them increases, which means energy is transferred to its gravitational potential store Therefore, at the point furthest from the Sun, the energy in the gravitational potential store is at its maximum The total energy of the comet remains constant throughout its orbit Due to the principle of conservation of energy, an increase in gravitational potential energy results in a decrease in kinetic energy When the gravitational potential energy is at its maximum, the kinetic energy is at its minimum Since kinetic energy depends on speed, a minimum kinetic energy means the orbital speed of the comet is also at its minimum A is incorrect as it assumes the orbital speed is at its maximum when the comet is furthest from the Sun B is incorrect because the comet has its minimum orbital speed and maximum gravitational potential energy at this point, not the other way around D is incorrect as the energy in the gravitational potential store is at its maximum, not its minimum, when the comet is furthest away A great way to remember this is to apply the principle of conservation of energy. When a comet approaches the Sun, it "falls" towards it, losing gravitational potential energy and gaining kinetic energy, causing it to speed up. As it moves away, it travels "uphill" against the Sun's gravity, losing kinetic energy and gaining gravitational potential energy, causing it to slow down.

questions.stem:
The light from distant galaxies is observed to be redshifted.
Which statement correctly explains this observation?
options: A. Distant galaxies are hotter than nearby galaxies.
B. Distant galaxies are moving away from us, stretching the wavelength of the light.
C. Light loses energy as it travels through space, decreasing its frequency.
D. The Universe is contracting, compressing the wavelength of the light.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B Redshift is the increase in the observed wavelength (decrease in frequency) of light from distant galaxies It occurs because the galaxies are moving away from us — the expansion of the Universe stretches the wavelength of the light The faster a galaxy moves away, the greater the redshift This is evidence that the Universe is expanding A is incorrect because the colour shift is not caused by temperature. Redshift is a Doppler-type effect caused by the relative motion of the galaxy away from the observer. C is incorrect because light does not lose energy as it travels through the vacuum of space. The frequency of light remains constant unless the source is moving relative to the observer. D is incorrect because red-shift indicates that wavelengths are being stretched (increased), not compressed. If the Universe were contracting, we would observe blueshift (shorter wavelengths), not redshift.

questions.stem:
A student investigates how the material of a surface affects the height to which a ball bounces.
The following apparatus is available to the student:
• a selection of balls of similar size

• a clamp, stand, and boss

• samples of different surface materials (e.g., wood, carpet, rubber, tile)

Plan an experiment to investigate how the surface material affects the bounce height of the ball.
In your plan:
• list any additional apparatus needed

• explain briefly how you would carry out the investigation

• state the key variables to keep constant

• draw a table, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use your readings to reach a conclusion.

You may draw a diagram if it helps your explanation.
questions.explanation: Apparatus Use a metre ruler to measure bounce height and a set square to ensure the metre rule is vertical. Method Set up the metre rule vertically using the stand and clamp Place the first surface material (e.g., wood) on the bench at the base of the ruler Hold the ball at a fixed drop height (e.g., 50.0 cm) and release it Observe the maximum height reached by the ball on its first bounce and record it in the table Repeat the drop from the same height at least two more times for this surface and calculate an average bounce height Repeat the entire procedure for at least four other different surface materials Control variables The variables to be controlled are the drop height of the ball and the type of ball used (i.e. use the same ball each time). Table surface material bounce height 1 / cm bounce height 2 / cm bounce height 3 / cm average bounce height / cm Conclusion Compare the average bounce heights for each material by plotting a bar chart with surface material on the x-axis and average bounce height on the y-axis. The tallest bar shows which surface results in the highest bounce. The plan is marked out of 7, with one mark awarded for each of the following points: Apparatus Metre rule [1 mark] Method Valid procedure, e.g. dropping the ball from a fixed point and measuring the bounce height using the ruler [1 mark] Repeat the experiment for at least 3 different surface materials [1 mark] Control variable Drop height [1 mark] Table Table with columns for surface material and bounce height with appropriate units [1 mark] Conclusion/analysis of the data Compare readings in the table to see if different surfaces produce a change in the dependent variable (average height) OR Plot a bar chart of material vs bounce height [1 mark] Additional points Any one from: Method to ensure the metre ruler is vertical / perpendicular to the bench, e.g. use of a set square Method to measure the bounce height more accurately, e.g. use of a video camera / slow-motion phone camera Take at least 5 sets of data Repeat each measurement and take the average Use the same ball / diameter / mass of ball each time [1 mark] In your table headings, always use the format 'Quantity / unit'. If you write "Height (cm)" or just "Height", you may lose the mark. Never just say "repeat the experiment." You must say what you are repeating (e.g., "Repeat for 5 different materials") and why (e.g., "Repeat three times for each material to find an average"). If the apparatus list doesn't include something essential for a fair test, add it! For example, a "fiducial marker" (a pointer) is a great answer for anything involving scales or oscillators. The conclusion mark is usually the easiest mark. If the independent variable is "categories" (like materials), suggest a bar chart . If the independent variable is "numerical" (like length or temperature), suggest a line graph .

questions.stem:

questions.stem: Which statement about the Alkali metals is correct?
options: A. Potassium is more dense than lithium.
B. Lithium has a higher density than sodium.
C. Potassium is less reactive than sodium.
D. The melting point of sodium is higher than lithium.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The atomic number of the elements increases and their properties change as you move down Group I. Melting and boiling points and hardness decrease while their density increases . They become more  reactive due to increasing distance between the outermost  electrons and the nucleus, making it easier for the metals to lose their outer shell electron. Potassium is below lithium in Group I so its density is higher than that of lithium. B is incorrect as lithium is less dense than sodium as it is higher up in the group. C is incorrect as potassium is below sodium in Group I and is thus more  reactive . D is incorrect as sodium has a lower melting point than lithium since it is lower down the group.

questions.stem:
A rectangular coil is dropped between a pair of opposite magnetic poles, as shown.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/02/58341-coil-em-induction-question.png)In which position is the magnitude of the induced e.m.f. in the coil the greatest?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2026/02/16886-coil-em-induction-answer-option.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C An e.m.f. is induced in the coil only when its horizontal wires are cutting through the magnetic field lines The magnitude of the induced e.m.f. depends on the speed at which the magnetic field lines are being cut As the coil falls, it accelerates due to gravity, meaning its speed increases at each successive position In position C , the top wire of the coil is cutting the field lines while the coil is moving at a higher speed than it was in position A A is incorrect because although an e.m.f. is induced, the coil is moving more slowly than at position C . B is incorrect because when the entire coil is within a uniform magnetic field, the e.m.f. induced in the top wire cancels out the e.m.f. induced in the bottom wire, so, the induced e.m.f. is momentarily zero. D is incorrect because the coil has completely left the magnetic field and no field lines are being cut; therefore, the induced e.m.f. is zero. Remember that an e.m.f. is only induced when there is a change in the magnetic flux through the coil. When the coil is entirely within a uniform field, there is no change in flux, so no e.m.f. is induced. Also consider that a falling object accelerates, so the coil moves faster at lower positions, which affects the rate of cutting field lines.

questions.stem:
A ball is dropped from a height above the ground.
Which transfer between energy stores takes place as the ball falls towards the ground?
options: A. chemical energy to kinetic energy
B. gravitational potential energy to elastic energy
C. kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy
D. gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D As the ball falls, it loses height, and therefore the energy in its gravitational potential store decreases The ball speeds up, so the energy in its kinetic store increases Therefore, the main transfer between energy stores is: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy A is incorrect because chemical energy is not involved in a falling ball. Chemical energy is stored in fuels, food and batteries. B is incorrect because elastic energy is only relevant if the ball deforms (e.g. on impact with the ground), not during free fall through air. C is incorrect because this describes the energy transfer for the opposite motion, i.e. a ball being thrown upwards into the air.

questions.stem:

options: A. They contain carbon and hydrogen atoms.
C. They have the same functional group.
D. They react differently from each other.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: A homologous series is a family of chemicals with similar properties that share the same general formula and which have the same functional group . Each atom in the series has an oxygen atom with a double bond to a carbon. This is a series called aldehydes. This is not a group that you need to be able to draw or recall, but you must be able to look at a structure and see the pattern in a series and recognise it as a functional group. A is incorrect as this would be the definition of a hydrocarbon B is incorrect as the molecules shown have saturated carbon-carbon bonds, but this does not make a homologous series. D is incorrect as a homologous series will have similar chemical properties.

questions.stem:
Background radiation is the radiation that is always present in the environment around us.
Which list contains only natural sources of background radiation?
options: A. cosmic rays, radon gas, medical X-rays
B. cosmic rays, radon gas, rocks and buildings
C. food and drink, nuclear power stations, cosmic rays
D. mobile phones, radon gas, rocks and buildings
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B Background radiation comes from both natural and man-made sources Natural sources include cosmic rays radon gas radioactive elements found naturally in rocks, buildings, and even food and drink Man-made sources include medical procedures (like X-rays) and nuclear power generation A is incorrect as medical X-rays are a man-made source of radiation C is incorrect as nuclear power stations are a man-made source of radiation D is incorrect as mobile phones do not emit ionising nuclear radiation and are not a source of background radiation Remember that background radiation has both natural and man-made sources. Be careful not to confuse non-ionising radiation (e.g. from mobile phones) with ionising nuclear radiation — mobile phones are not a source of background radiation.

questions.stem:
A student is investigating the work required to pull a box containing some masses up a sloping wooden board. Fig. 4.1 shows the board and the box.
  Plan an experiment to investigate how the work required to pull the box up the slope depends on the mass of the box and its contents.
  Work done is calculated using the equation:
work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force.
The following apparatus is available to the students:
a wooden board a box with a length of string attached a selection of masses that fit in the box a metre rule an electronic balance.
In your plan, you should:
• list any other apparatus that you would use

• explain briefly how you would carry out the investigation, including the measurements you would take

• state the key variables that you would control

• draw a suitable table, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use the results to reach a conclusion.

 You may add to the diagram if it helps your explanation.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/11/p2-4.PNG)
questions.explanation: To investigate how the work required to pull the box up the slope depends on the mass of the box and its contents: List any other apparatus that you would use: Forcemeter / newtonmeter OR Pully and weights; [1 mark] Outline the method: Pull the box up the slope and measure the force and the distance moved; [1 mark] Repeat with different masses in the box; [1 mark] List the control variables: The angle of the slope / height of the blocks; [1 mark] The distanced moved up the slope; [1 mark] Design a results table: A table scoring one mark: Mass/kg Force/N A table drawn with columns for force / N and mass / kg with units given; [1 mark] Explain how you would use the results to reach a conclusion: Any one from: Calculate the work done and compare it for the different masses; [1 mark] Plot a graph of work done against mass; [1 mark] [Total: 7 marks] The instruction to list any other equipment needed, can be done as a labelled diagram or by annotating the diagram provided on the exam paper. Control variables should only be factors that would affect the results, make sure you chose ones that are contextually relevant! Remember that you do not need to waste time making up data to put in your results table! The mark scheme shows the kind of short descriptions which easily score full marks in the exam. The most common mistakes with investigation questions are; Saying what the result will be, rather than how to draw the conclusion; Forgetting that only one variable can change, and changing all of them; Showing repeat readings or the range in the table, but not mentioning them in the description (it seems unfair, but this won't get you the mark); Wasting time by inventing data for the table. If you find yourself doing one of these - stop! And finally, the examiner will award marks for the diagram, so anything which is explained there will count.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: For equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero, and the resultant moment must be zero. questions.stem: Which metal could not be used for electroplating by using an aqueous solution?

questions.stem: The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a battery is
options: A. the charge that flows through the battery per unit time
B. the energy transferred per unit charge in driving charge around a complete circuit
C. the force that pushes electrons through the circuit
D. the potential difference across the terminals of the battery when no current flows
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a source is defined as the energy transferred per unit charge in driving charge around a complete circuit It is measured in volts (V), where 1 V = 1 J/C The e.m.f. represents the total energy the battery gives to each coulomb of charge A is incorrect because this is the definition of current (  ), not e.m.f. C is incorrect because, despite the word "force" in its name, e.m.f. is not a force. It is an energy transfer per unit charge. This is a common misconception. D is incorrect because this describes the terminal potential difference when no current flows, which happens to equal the e.m.f. numerically. However, this is not the definition of e.m.f. — it is a consequence of there being no internal energy losses.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C In Group VII reactivity decreases moving down the group and the atomic radius increases, so the outer shell gets further from the nucleus. The attraction between the nucleus and electrons gets weaker, so an electron is less easily gained, making it more difficult for the halogens to receive electrons. For the halogen in solution to displace the halide from the lithium halide, it must sit above the halide Chlorine in above iodine in the Periodic Table so chlorine will displace iodine from lithium iodide to produce lithium chloride and iodine chlorine + lithium iodide → lithium chloride + iodine Aqueous iodine is a brown solution, so as iodine is produced, the reaction mixture will darken A and B are incorrect as bromine sits below both chlorine and fluorine and cannot displace them as it is less reactive than both. D is incorrect as chlorine sits below fluorine.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Brass is an alloy; it is 70% copper and 30% zinc. Copper is used for electrical wiring as it has low resistance which makes it a good conductor of electricity. Zinc is used in galvanising steel as it is more reactive and will oxidise before the steel does (sacrificial protection!). A is incorrect as aircraft are made from aluminium, a metal not found in brass. Aluminum is light which makes it suitable for building airplanes. C is incorrect as aluminium would be used to make aircraft and stainless steel (alloy of carbon) is used to make cutlery. D is incorrect as cooking pans are made from copper as it is a good conductor of heat. Electrical wiring is also made from copper due to its low resistance

questions.stem:
Small blocks of zinc are attached to ship hulls which are commonly made from steel, an alloy of iron. This is done to prevent the hull from rusting.
Which statement explains this process?
options: A. Zinc is higher up on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become reduced.
B. Zinc is lower down on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become reduced.
C. Zinc is higher up on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become oxidised.
D. Zinc is lower down on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become oxidised.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Sacrificial rust protection works by using a metal placed higher up on the reactivity series and connecting it to the object that needs to be protected. Zinc is a more reactive metal so is more likely to lose  electrons (and become oxidised) than iron and it readily donates its electrons to any iron ions that might have formed, stopping them from corroding. The zinc metal will be corroded  in  preference to the steel hull, hence preventing it from rusting. A , B and D are incorrect as the sacrificial metal must be above iron on the reactivity series to be able to oxidise before the iron atoms do.

questions.stem:
Ethanol can be produced from substance Y.
substance Y + steam  ethanol
What is substance Y?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because ethanol is formed by the catalytic hydration of ethene with steam. A, C and D are incorrect as these substances are not used to make ethanol.

questions.stem:
A beaker of water, at its boiling point of 100 oC, is heated so that the liquid starts to become a gas, also at 100 oC.
Which row of the table correctly compares the liquid phase with the gas phase under these conditions?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Average distance between the particles | Average speed of the particles |
| A | the same in the liquid and the gas | the same in the liquid and the gas |
| B | greater in the liquid | greater in the gas |
| C | greater in the gas | greater in the liquid |
| D | greater in the gas | the same in the liquid and the gas |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The particles in a liquid are in contact with each other, while those in a gas are considerably further apart. The average kinetic energy of each molecule is related to the temperature of the substance. This means that, if a substance has a higher temperature, its molecules will, on average, have a higher kinetic energy. As Kinetic energy =  , the speed of the molecules will also be greater. Since both the liquid water and the gaseous water are both at a temperature of 100 o C, their molecules both have the same kinetic energy, and are travelling at the same speed. Each of the other answers has made at least one error. Liquid particles are always closer together than gas particles. Most students incorrectly think that gas particles have a higher kinetic energy than liquid particles. This is only true  if the gas is also at a higher temperature than the liquid (which is usually, but not always, the case)

questions.stem:

questions.stem:
A car tyre is inflated with air.
As the car drives, the temperature of the tyre increases, which also causes the temperature of the air inside the tyre to increase. This increases the pressure of the air inside the tyre.
Which of the following is a correct explanation as to why?
options: A. The mass of air inside the tyre has increased.
B. The area of the tyre has decreased, thus increasing the pressure.
C. The air molecules collide with each other less frequently.
D. The average kinetic energy of the air molecules has increased.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy (KE) per molecule. If the temperature increases , then so does the average KE per molecule. If the particles have more KE , they move with a greater velocity . This causes them to hit the walls of the tyre at a greater speed, and to exert more force when they bounce off. This increased force increases the pressure in the tyre. A is incorrect as the tyre has not been pumped up, so no more air has been added. Therefore the mass cannot have increased. B is incorrect as the tyre has a (very nearly) fixed volume therefore the area with which air molecules can collide could not have changed. C is incorrect as if anything, the molecules will collide with each other more frequently, but it is collisions with the wall of the tyre that increase the pressure.

B is incorrect as a still day will not increase the rate of evaporation, although the high temperature will. questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Ultrasound is used to find breaks in materials such as the steel of railway lines, where an echo will reflect off a broken surface, indicating the distance to the damaged part Option 1 is correct In situations where x-rays would be too damaging, such as scans of the fetus or soft tissues, ultrasound is extensively used Option 2 is correct Radar stands for radio detection and ranging and uses radio waves, not sound waves, to detect distances and velocities Option 3 is not correct

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D For use as a medical tracer, the radioactive source must: be penetrating enough to be detected outside the body - gamma rays are the best for this have a short half-life, so that the source decays quickly and the patient is not exposed to radiation for a prolonged period A is incorrect because alpha and beta particles would be absorbed by body tissue and could not be detected externally. C is incorrect because, although gamma rays are the correct type of emission, a long half-life would mean prolonged exposure to ionising radiation.

questions.stem:
An oven is wired into somebody’s kitchen. The oven is protected by a fuse, and functions normally, but the owner notices that the wires that connect the oven to the mains electricity supply get quite hot.
What could be done to reduce the temperature of the wires?
options: A. Add a circuit breaker to the circuit.
B. Put thicker insulation on the wires.
C. Replace the wires with thicker diameter wires.
D. Replace the wires with thinner diameter wires.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The problem here is that the wires used to connect the oven are not rated for the amount of current the oven uses. This is an easy mistake to make, as ovens use more current than normal electrical devices. Thicker diameter wires are required, since thicker wires have a smaller resistance, and therefore dissipate less heat when current flows through them. Remember:  gives the power dissipated by a component which has resistance. A is incorrect as this would have no effect, as the oven is operating properly. B is incorrect as thicker insulation might cause the wires to feel cooler, but they would still be just as hot. They would actually be less able to dissipate the heat they are generating, and are in greater danger of causing a fire. D is incorrect as thinner wires would exacerbate the problem. They have a higher resistance, and would dissipate more heat, becoming even hotter.

questions.stem:

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because Step Working out 1 The ratio of N 2 : NH 3 is  14 : 16.8. Divide across by the smallest number (14) to find the simplest ratio . So for every 1 tonne of nitrogen, 1.2 tonnes of ammonia are produced. 2 Divide the amount of NH 3 desired (51 tonnes) by 1.2 to calculate the amount of nitrogen required. questions.stem:

questions.stem:

options: A. Calcium ions lose electrons to form positive charges. .
B. Calcium atoms gain 3 electrons to form positive ions.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because calcium atoms have 20 electrons , with two electrons in its outermost shell. It loses these two electrons to form a 2 + positive ion. questions.stem: The atom of element Z has 6 electrons in its outer shell. How would this element react?
options: A. It shares two electrons with four from another atom to form two covalent bonds
B. It shares four electrons with four from another atom to form four covalent bonds
C. It shares four electrons with two from another atom to form two covalent bonds

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Element Z is a Group 6 element since it has 6 electrons in its outer shell. Group 6 elements are nonmetals and metalloids that form covalent bonds by sharing electrons. By sharing 2 electrons with 2 from another atom it achieves a full outer shell configuration. A , B and C are incorrect as the combinations in these formulae do not provide a full outer shell for each atom.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the structure of macromolecules?

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Macromolecular structures form giant crystals. All the atoms in the structure are linked to each other by strong covalent bonds. The atoms are joined to each other forming a regular arrangement . A is incorrect as intermolecular forces are not present within the crystal structure. B and C are incorrect as macromolecules are covalently bonded.

questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for the reaction of methane and oxygen?

CH 4 (g) + 2 O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + 2 H 2 O(g) C x 1 H x 4 O x 4 C x 1 H x 4 O x 4 A , B and C are incorrect as these options do not provide the correct balanced equation.

questions.stem:
Comets travel faster within the Solar System than they do when they are outside it.
Which of the following gives the correct reason for this?
options: A. A comet near to the Sun has more gravitational potential energy.
B. Comets closer to the Sun transfer gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy due to conservation of energy.
C. A comet which is outside the Solar System has less energy than one which is passing through it.
D. Comets closer to the Sun transfer kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy due to conservation of energy.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Energy is always conserved This means that throughout the orbit of a comet, the total of its kinetic energy and gravitational energy must always be the same Gravitational potential energy increases when the comet is far from the Sun (and about to be pulled back towards it) and decreases when it is close to the Sun The decrease in gravitational potential energy is balanced by an increase in kinetic energy

questions.stem:
A student gradually added excess potassium hydroxide from a burette to a conical flask containing sulfuric acid as part of a rate of reaction investigation.
Which statement describes the change in pH of the sulfuric acid as the aqueous potassium hydroxide was added?
options: A. The pH decreases from 14 to neutrality and remains constant
B. The pH decreases from 12 to 2
C. The pH increases from 1 to neutrality and remains constant
D. The pH increases from 1 to around 13
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Potassium hydroxide is a strong base and reacts with sulfuric acid to produce salt and water: 2 KOH + H 2 SO 4 → K 2 SO 4 + 2 H 2 O At the beginning of the reaction and before any alkali has been added the pH of the sulfuric acid is 1. As the alkali is added and neutralisation begins, more and more of the acid is neutralised as the alkali is added and the pH rises. As the alkali is added in excess , the pH continues to rise until it reaches pH 14 which indicates a strong alkaline solution. A and B are  incorrect as the pH of the acid increases from 1 to 14 as more alkali is added C is incorrect as if the alkali is added in excess then the pH increases beyond neutrality

questions.stem:

What kind of substance was the student given?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Ammonium chloride, NH 4 Cl, when reacted with a base will produce ammonia gas , salt and water: NH 4 Cl(aq) + X-OH(aq) → NH 3 (g) + H 2 O(l) + XCl(aq) Methyl orange indicator turned yellow which means the substance is a base. A and B are incorrect as salts and metals are neutral compounds and do not cause a colour change in methyl orange. D is incorrect as potassium carbonate is a base and would react with an acid.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of Fe in Fe2O3?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Oxidation number refers to a single atom or ion which can be on their own or in a compound. The oxidation number of a compound is 0 and of an element is also 0 . The oxidation number of an ion is equal to the charge of that ion e.g. F ー is  -1. The oxidation number of oxygen in a compound is always -2 (except in peroxide R-O-O-R, where it is -1 ). There are 3 oxygens in Fe 2 O 3 ,  so 3 x -2 = -6. As it is a compound, the overall charge must be 0, hence each Fe atom must be +3 since 2 x 3 = 6  and +6 - 6 = 0. A , B and C are incorrect as these options do not provide an oxidation number of 0 for the compound.

questions.stem:
The results of two tests on a solid are shown below.

|---|---|
| Test | Observation |
| Acidified silver nitrate added | Cream precipitate formed |

questions.stem:
Copper(II) sulfate can be prepared by reacting solid copper(II) carbonate with hot sulfuric acid. The copper(II) carbonate is always added in excess.
Why is the solid reactant added in excess?
options: A. To ensure all of the acid reacts.
B. To make the reaction go faster.
C. To ensure all of the solid reactant has reacted.
D. To increase the product yield.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A Copper(II) carbonate reacts with sulfuric acid to produce copper(II) sulfate: CuCO 3 + H 2 SO 4 → CuSO 4 + H 2 O + CO 2 Copper(II) sulfate is soluble and is separated from the mixture by evaporation . If there is any acid remaining in the solution it would become dangerously concentrated during this phase of the preparation. For this reason the carbonate is added in excess to make sure that all of the acid has reacted. B and D are incorrect as the rate of reaction and yield are not dependent on there being an excess of only one of the reactants. C is incorrect as any unreacted copper(II) carbonate is removed by filtration .

questions.stem: Which one of the following names does not correspond to a group of elements on the Periodic table?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Alloys are mixtures of different metals or metals with nonmetals and are not found on the Periodic table. A , B and D are incorrect as these terms all correspond to groups of elements from the Periodic table. Alkali metals are Group 1 elements. Group 7 elements are known as the halogens.

questions.stem:
The reactivity of the halogens decreases moving down the group.
Which statement explains this observation?
options: A. Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the atom to attract electrons.
B. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the atom to attract electrons.
C. Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it harder for the atom to attract electrons.
D. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it harder for the atom to attract electrons.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D The Group I elements are metals and lose their outer shell electron whereas the Group VII elements are nonmetals and need to gain just one more electron to achieve an octet (and full outer shell). The atomic radius increases moving down the group so the outer shell gets further  away from the nucleus the further down you go. The attraction between the nucleus and electrons gets weaker, so an electron is less  easily  gained as there is greater shielding of the nucleus. A and C are incorrect as the distance between the nucleus and outermost shell increases moving down the group. B is incorrect as the longer distance makes it harder to remove the valence electrons, not harder.

questions.stem: Which strategy for reducing the effect of environmental issues would not help reduce climate change?

questions.stem:
Butene and octene belong to the same homologous series.

options: B. Number of hydrogen atoms per molecule
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: A homologous series is a family of chemicals with similar properties that share the same general formula and which have the same functional group . Butene, C 4 H 8 and octene, C 8 H 16 , each have a carbon-carbon double bond . This is the functional group of the alkenes . A, B and C are incorrect because each of these properties will be different between each member of a homologous series.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D The Group I metals are also called the alkali metals and they produce alkaline solutions in reaction with water. Lithium for example reacts to produce a lithium hydroxide solution which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas: 2 Li (s) + 2 H 2 O (l) → 2 LiOH (aq) + H 2 (g) A , B and C are incorrect as these are all characteristics of the Group I metals.

questions.stem:
A rifle fires a bullet of mass 0.020 kg vertically upwards through the air. As it leaves the rifle, the speed of the bullet is 350 m/s.
Calculate
 
(i) the energy in the kinetic store of the bullet as it leaves the rifle, 
energy = ...........................................................[3]
 
(ii) the maximum possible height that the bullet can reach.
 
maximum height = ...........................................................[2]
questions.explanation: (i) To calculate the energy: List the known quantities: Mass of bullet = 0.020 kg Initial speed = 350 m/s Recall the equation for kinetic energy: [1 mark] Substitute in known values to calculate: [1 mark] = 1200 J [1 mark] (ii) To calculate the maximum height: List the known quantities: Mass of bullet, m = 0.020 kg Initial speed = 350 m/s Recall the equation for gravitational potential energy:  Recall the link between   and  : All the energy will be transferred from the kinetic store to the gravitational potential store at maximum height Substitute in known values: [1 mark] Calculate h : h = 6000 m (1.s.f) [1 mark] [Total: 5 marks] An object fired upwards will reach a maximum height where velocity will momentarily be 0. This point occurs when all the energy has been transferred from the kinetic store of the bullet to the gravitational potential store. The transfer of energy between the kinetic and gravitational potential stores are very common. When an object is lifted, energy is transferred from the kinetic store to the gravitational potential store When a object is falling, energy is being transferred from the gravitational potential store to the kinetic store
