questions.stem:
Potassium and krypton are elements in Period 4. Potassium is at the beginning of the period and is more metallic than krypton which is at the end of the period.
What makes potassium more metallic than krypton?
options: A. It has less electrons than krypton.
B. It has less protons than krypton.
C. It has less electron shells.
D. It has less outer shell electrons.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D The change in metallic to non-metallic character as we move across the Periodic table from left to right is linked to the electronic configuration of the elements. Non-metals have more electrons in their outer shells than metals. Potassium is in Group I and has 1 electron in its outer shell whereas krypton is in Group VIII and has 8 electrons in its outer shell. A and B are incorrect as although potassium has fewer electrons and protons than krypton, it is the outer shell electrons that determine its chemical properties. C is incorrect as both elements are in the same period they have the same number of electron shells.

questions.stem: Which of the following observations does not apply to Group I elements?
options: A. They are relatively soft metals.
B. They corrode quickly when exposed to air.
C. They react very quickly with water releasing hydrogen gas
D. They produce acidic solutions in reaction with water.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D The Group I metals are also called the alkali metals and they produce alkaline solutions in reaction with water. Lithium for example reacts to produce a lithium hydroxide solution which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas: 2 Li (s) + 2 H 2 O (l) → 2 LiOH (aq) + H 2 (g) A , B and C are incorrect as these are all characteristics of the Group I metals.

questions.stem:
Ionic equations 1 and 2 show how substance X behaves in aqueous solution.


|  |  |
|---|---|
| 1 | X - + H + → XH |
| 2 | X → X - + H + |
Which row correctly describes substance X?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | acid | base |
| A | 1 | 1 |
| B | 1 | 2 |
| C | 2 | 2 |
| D | 2 | 1 |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D In equation 1 substance X accepts a proton so is behaving as a base. In equation 2 substance X donates a proton so it behaves as an acid. A , B and C are incorrect as these options do not match with the behaviour of substance X in equations 1 and 2.

questions.stem:
An element has an electronic configuration of 2,8,6.
Which group and period can the element be found in?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | group | period |
| A | 6 | 3 |
| B | 6 | 8 |
| C | 3 | 6 |
| D | 8 | 2 |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The electronic configuration shows the arrangement of electrons in their shells The last notation is the number of electrons in the outer shell The number of electrons in the outer shell correlates to the group number 2,8, 6 shows there are six electrons in the outer shell so the element is in Group 6 The period number refers to the number of shells an atom has The number of notations shows the number of shells 2,8,6 has three notations so the element has three shells and is in Period 3 B , C and D are incorrect as the group or period number is wrong

questions.stem:
Calcium, copper, iron and magnesium are metals. They can be placed in order of reactivity.
Which of the following statements about these metals is correct?
options: A. Iron reacts with steam but magnesium does not.
B. Copper reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form copper (II) chloride.
C. Magnesium and calcium both react with hot water.
D. Iron (II) oxide cannot be reduced by heating strongly with carbon.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because both magnesium and calcium are reactive enough to react with hot water. A is incorrect as magnesium is more reactive than iron so would burn in steam producing magnesium oxide and H 2 gas. B is incorrect as copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid D is incorrect as iron (II) oxide is reduced with carbon in a blast furnace

questions.stem:
Aqueous sodium hydroxide is used in chemical analysis.
Which statement about aqueous NaOH is correct?
options: A. A white precipitate is formed when added to a solution containing sulfate ions
B. A green precipitate is formed upon addition to a solution of iron(II) ions which does not dissolve in excess
C. A green precipitate is formed upon addition to a solution of iron(II) ions which dissolves in excess
D. An acidic gas is produced when added to ammonium chloride
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: Iron(II) ions react with aqueous sodium hydroxide to produce a green-coloured precipitate which is iron(II) hydroxide: Fe 2+ (aq) + 2OH – (aq) → Fe(OH) 2 (s) Iron(II) is insoluble in excess NaOH A is incorrect as sodium sulfate is produced which is highly soluble, hence a precipitate is not formed C is incorrect as the iron(II) hydroxide produced is insoluble in excess NaOH, hence it does not dissolve D is incorrect as ammonia gas is produced which is basic, not acidic:  NH 4 Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH 3 + H 2 O

questions.stem: Define the term isotope.
questions.explanation: The definition of an isotope is: Atoms of the same element/ atoms with same proton number/ atoms with same atomic number; [1 mark] (But a) different neutron number/ nucleon number/ mass number; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] Make sure you are specific in your answer and refer to atoms This is underlined as it is important and will result in you losing the first mark if you miss it out

questions.stem: The transition elements are used extensively as catalysts. Which statement explains why they are such good catalysts?
options: A. Their oxidation state does not change.
B. They have a large surface area.
C. They can have variable oxidation states.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C The transition metals often have various  oxidation states, e.g. the common oxidation states of chromium are +2, +3 or +6. This gives them the ability to easily transfer electrons to and from other species in a reaction. A is incorrect as their oxidation state is variable and so can change. B is incorrect as surface area is a physical property which can easily be increased by grinding metals into finer sized particles. D is incorrect as they do form coloured compounds but this property is irrelevant to their catalytic ability.

questions.stem:
Five different metals P, Q, R, S and T were reacted with dilute hydrochloric acid.
The volume of hydrogen gas produced after one minute was measured. The results are shown in the bar chart below:


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/q2-hard-9-2-cie-igcse-chemistry.png)What is the order of reactivity of the metals?


|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | most reactive | → | → | → | least reactive |
| A | P | Q | R | S | T |
| B | R | P | S | Q | T |
| C | T | Q | S | P | R |
| D | T | S | R | Q | P |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: When a metal reacts with an acid it produces a metal salt and hydrogen gas. M(metal) + H 2 SO 4 → MSO 4 + H 2 The more reactive the metal the more hydrogen gas will be produced in the same amount of time. The bar chart shows that metal T is the most reactive as this reaction produces the largest volume of gas, followed by Q. The bar chart then shows the order of reactivity by the decreasing volume of hydrogen gas produced.

questions.stem: Which pair of substances would make an NPK fertiliser?
options: A. ammonium phosphate and potassium chloride
B. calcium phosphate and potassium chloride
C. ammonium sulfate and potassium nitrate
D. potassium nitrate and calcium carbonate
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: The elements present in an NPK fertiliser are nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium Ammonium phosphate, (NH 4 ) 3 PO 3 and potassium chloride, KCl provide these three elements B is incorrect as calcium phosphate and potassium chloride do not provide nitrogen C is incorrect as ammonium sulfate and potassium nitrate do not provide phosphorus D is incorrect as potassium nitrate and calcium carbonate do not provide phosphorus

questions.stem:
The production of sulfur trioxide during Stage 2 of the Contact process involves a reversible reaction. Which row describes the conditions of temperature and pressure and the percentage yield of sulfur trioxide?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | temperature / | pressure / atm | percentage yield |
| A | 150 | 1 - 2 | 70 |
| B | 450 | 1 - 2 | 98 |
| C | 450 | 200 | 98 |
| D | 150 | 200 | 70 |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B The conditions are 450  and 1 - 2 atm pressure which provide a percentage yield of 98%. A higher pressure is not used as it is too dangerous given that SO 3 is an acidic gas. In economic terms it isn't worth the expense to use a higher pressure when a 98% yield is achievable at 1 - 2 atm. A, C and D are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe the conditions used for the reaction.

questions.stem:
A student is determining the refractive index n of the material of a transparent block.
    Fig. 3.1 shows the outline ABCD of the transparent block.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/11/screenshot-2022-11-08-at-11-42-32.png)(i) On Fig. 3.1: 
• draw a normal NL at the centre of side AB
• continue the normal so that it passes through side CD of the block

• label the point F where NL crosses AB

• label the point G where NL crosses CD.


[1]
 
(ii) Draw a line EF at an angle i = 30° to the left of the normal and above side AB.
[1]
 
(iii) Mark the positions of two pins P1 and P2 on line EF placed at a suitable distance apart for this type of ray-tracing experiment.
[1]
questions.explanation: (i) Draw a normal which passes through the centre of AB and passes through CD , labelling points F and G :  The normal passes through the block AND through the centre of AB AND is perpendicular to AB ; [1 mark]  (ii) Draw a line EF at an angle i = 30° to the left of the normal and above side AB :  Lines EF and FG are at an angle of 30° to each other AND  EF is on the left side of FG ; [1 mark]  (iii) Mark the positions of two pins P1 and P2 on line EF placed at a suitable distance apart:  Points P 1 and P 2 are at least 5.0 cm apart ; [1 mark] This can either be indicated as above, or is measurably more than 5.0 cm [Total: 3 marks] When considering the position of the pins for this experiment, think practically. You place the pins so that when the light source is switched off, you can draw a straight line in the same place that the path of light was. If the pins are very close together, it is easy for your ruler to draw the wrong angle of line. With the pins further apart, your ruler is less likely to rotate around the pins, so the line will better represent the path of the light.

questions.stem:
Carbon monoxide and steam react together exothermically to produce the alcohol methanol, as shown in the equation.
CO(g) + 2H2(g) ⇌ CH3OH(g)
Both reactants and the product are gaseous. Which conditions of pressure and temperature would provide the highest yield of CH3OH?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C Increasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium in the direction of an endothermic reaction . The reaction is exothermic , therefore an increase in temperature would favour the reverse reaction and decrease the yield of methanol. From the balanced equation, there are 3 moles of reactants to 1 mole of product. An increase in pressure would shift the equilibrium to the side with less  volume , so it would favour the forward reaction and increase the yield of methanol. A , B and D are incorrect as these conditions would not provide the highest yield of methanol.

questions.stem: Which statement about the extraction of iron from its ore is not correct?
options: A. Iron can be extracted by reduction with carbon
B. Iron is easier to extract than zinc
C. Iron is easier to extract than copper
D. Iron is extracted from the ore, hematite
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Iron is higher up the reactivity series than copper The higher up the metal is, the harder it is to extract from its ore due to stronger bonds with its oxide A is incorrect as iron is less reactive than carbon so can be extracted by reduction with carbon B is incorrect as iron is easier to extract than zinc as it is lower in the reactivity series D is incorrect as iron ore is called haematite

questions.stem:
Hydrocarbons separated by fractional distillation of petroleum can be cracked to make useful shorter chain products.
Which substance is not a product of the cracking of propane, Mr 44?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: The process of cracking involves breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller molecules. Cracking alkanes can produce; a shorter chain alkane or alkene or 1 or more shorter alkenes and hydrogen . The molecule C 4 H 8 has one more carbon and the original molecule of propane C 3 H 8 . B, C and D are incorrect as all of these molecules could be a product of cracking of propane.

questions.stem:
The following reaction takes place in the presence of light.
CH4 + Cl2 + light → CH3Cl + HCl
What is the name for this reaction?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Halogenation is the replacement of one or more hydrogen atoms in an organic molecule by a halogen (fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine). The halogenation of an alkane is an example of a substitution reaction. A is incorrect as the combination of alkanes with oxygen, generating heat is known as combustion. B is incorrect as polymerisation is the joining of simple single repeating units into a polymer. C is incorrect as thermal decomposition is the breakdown of a molecule using heat.

questions.stem: Which of these is an advantage of producing ethanol by fermentation of sugar compared to the catalytic addition of steam to ethene?
options: A. The process uses high temperatures.
B. The alcohol produced is purer.
D. The process uses renewable raw materials.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Fermentation is a metabolic process that produces ethanol from glucose and other sugars. The sugars used in fermentation are from plants and so are a renewable resource. Ethene is extracted from petroleum (crude oil) and so is non-renewable. A, B and C are incorrect as all of the processes are features of ethanol production from ethene.

questions.stem: Element X is an unreactive non-metal element. Where could this element be found on the Periodic table?
options: A. At the far left hand side
B. At the far right hand side
C. At the top of Group VI
D. At the bottom of Group VII
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B The noble gases are a group of unreactive non metal elements. They are in Group VIII / 0 at the far right hand side of the table. A is incorrect as this position corresponds to the Group I elements which are all reactive metals . C is incorrect as carbon sits at the top of Group VI and does react with other elements to form compounds. D is incorrect as elements in Group VII are reactive and combine with other elements.

questions.stem:
A student is investigating the work required to pull a box containing some masses up a sloping wooden board. Fig. 4.1 shows the board and the box.
  Plan an experiment to investigate how the work required to pull the box up the slope depends on the mass of the box and its contents.
  Work done is calculated using the equation:
work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force.
The following apparatus is available to the students:
a wooden board a box with a length of string attached a selection of masses that fit in the box a metre rule an electronic balance.
In your plan, you should:
• list any other apparatus that you would use

• explain briefly how you would carry out the investigation, including the measurements you would take

• state the key variables that you would control

• draw a suitable table, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table)

• explain how you would use the results to reach a conclusion.

 You may add to the diagram if it helps your explanation.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/11/p2-4.PNG)
questions.explanation: To investigate how the work required to pull the box up the slope depends on the mass of the box and its contents: List any other apparatus that you would use: Forcemeter / newtonmeter OR Pully and weights; [1 mark] Outline the method: Pull the box up the slope and measure the force and the distance moved; [1 mark] Repeat with different masses in the box; [1 mark] List the control variables: The angle of the slope / height of the blocks; [1 mark] The distanced moved up the slope; [1 mark] Design a results table: A table scoring one mark: Mass/kg Force/N A table drawn with columns for force / N and mass / kg with units given; [1 mark] Explain how you would use the results to reach a conclusion: Any one from: Calculate the work done and compare it for the different masses; [1 mark] Plot a graph of work done against mass; [1 mark] [Total: 7 marks] The instruction to list any other equipment needed, can be done as a labelled diagram or by annotating the diagram provided on the exam paper. Control variables should only be factors that would affect the results, make sure you chose ones that are contextually relevant! Remember that you do not need to waste time making up data to put in your results table! The mark scheme shows the kind of short descriptions which easily score full marks in the exam. The most common mistakes with investigation questions are; Saying what the result will be, rather than how to draw the conclusion; Forgetting that only one variable can change, and changing all of them; Showing repeat readings or the range in the table, but not mentioning them in the description (it seems unfair, but this won't get you the mark); Wasting time by inventing data for the table. If you find yourself doing one of these - stop! And finally, the examiner will award marks for the diagram, so anything which is explained there will count.

questions.stem:
When nitrogen dioxide is cooled, it forms a yellow liquid and then pale yellow crystals. These crystals are heated and the temperature is measured every minute. The following graph can be drawn.
 


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/09/time-temp-no2.png) 
i) Describe the arrangement and movement of the molecules in the region A–B.
 ii)  Name the change that occurs in the region B–C
questions.explanation: i) The arrangement and movement of the molecules in the region A–B are: Close / tightly packed; [1 mark] Ordered / lattice; [1 mark] Vibrating; [1 mark] ii) The change that occurs in the region B–C is: Melting / freezing / fusion / solidification; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] The region A-B is labelled as pale yellow crystals This means that you are being asked to describe the arrangement of particles in a solid The region B-C is where it changes from pale yellow crystals (solid) to a yellow liquid The most common correct answer to this question is melting

questions.stem:
Nitrogen dioxide is a brown gas. It can be made by heating certain metal nitrates.
2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2
At most temperatures, samples of nitrogen dioxide are equilibrium mixtures.
2NO2 (g)     N2O4 (g) 
dark brown            pale yellow
i) At 25 °C, the mixture contains 20 % of nitrogen dioxide. At 100 °C this has risen to 90%. Is the forward reaction exothermic or endothermic? Give a reason for your choice.
[2]
ii) Explain why the colour of the equilibrium mixture becomes lighter when the pressure on the mixture is increased.
[2]
questions.explanation: i) The forward reaction is: Exothermic; [1 mark] The forward reaction is favoured by low temperature / reverse reaction is favoured by high temperature; [1 mark] ii) The colour of the equilibrium mixture becomes lighter when the pressure on the mixture is increased because: The equilibrium shifts to the right / side of the product; [1 mark] Because this side has a smaller volume / fewer moles of gas produced; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] According to Le Chatalier's principle, when a change is made to a system, the system will shift the position of the equilibrium counteract the change Be careful in part i)- the question states that more of the reactant is formed at high temperatures, the focus is not on the product When temperature is increased, more reactant is formed so the system must have favoured the reverse reaction to decrease the temperature. The reverse reaction is therefore endothermic and the forward reaction exothermic You must give your answer in terms of the forward reaction as this is what has been asked for The forward reaction produces 1 mole of gas, whereas the reverse produces 2 For the mixture to become lighter the equilibrium must have shifted to the right

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: A. Ammonia is released when a base reacts with an ammonium salt.
B. Neutralisation occurs when an acid and an alkali react together.
C. Carbon dioxide is released when an acid and a carbonate react together.
D. The higher the pH of a solution, the higher its acidity.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Acids have low pH values and bases have high pH values. The lower the pH value then the higher the acidity of the solution. A is incorrect as ammonia gas is produced in this reaction: NH 4 Cl + NaOH → NH 3 + NaCl + H 2 O B is incorrect as acid-base reactions are neutralisation reactions. C is incorrect as CO 2 is a product in this reaction: CaCO 3 + 2HCl → CaCl 2 + CO 2  + H 2 O

questions.stem:
A teacher has a hot cup of tea.
Some of the liquid in the cup evaporates.
Choose the line from the table below that correctly describes what happens to the mass and the weight of the tea in the cup.


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Mass | Weight |
| A | increases | decreases |
| B | increases | increases |
| C | decreases | decreases |
| D | decreases | increases |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Mass is the amount of matter in the cup, while weight is the strength of the gravitational force pulling that matter downwards. As liquid leaves the cup, matter leaves the cup as evaporated vapour, and both the mass and weight decrease. A is incorrect because the mass does not increase. B is incorrect because neither the mass nor the weight increase. D is incorrect because the weight does not increase.

questions.stem:
Aluminium and iron are extracted from their ores by different methods.
Aluminium is extracted from its purified oxide ore by electrolysis.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/09/screen-shot-2022-09-14-at-14-45-29.png)What is the name of the ore of aluminium which consists mainly of aluminium oxide?
questions.explanation: The name of the ore of aluminium which consists mainly of aluminium oxide is: Bauxite; [1 mark] [Total: 1 mark] There are other ores of aluminium, however bauxite is used as it has the highest percentage of aluminium oxide Roughly 4 tonnes of bauxite are required to make 1 tonne of aluminium

questions.stem:
Use your copy of the Periodic Table to answer these questions.
Choose an element from the Periodic Table to match each description. You may give either the name or the symbol.
i) It is the most reactive metal.
[1]
ii) It is the only non-metal which is a liquid at r.t.p.
[1]
iii) This Group VII element is a solid at r.t.p.
[1]
iv) This element is in Group V and Period 4.
[1]
v) This unreactive gas is used to fill lamps.
[1]
questions.explanation: i) The element that is the most reactive metal is: Cs / Fr; [1 mark] ii) The element that is the only non-metal which is a liquid at r.t.p. is: Br; [1 mark] iii) The Group VII element that is a solid at r.t.p. is: I or At; [1 mark] iv) The element that is in Group V and Period 4 is: As; [1 mark] v) The element that is an unreactive gas used to fill lamps is: He / Ne / Ar / Kr / Xe; [1 mark] [Total: 5 marks] Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series with sodium second, showing that the Group I metals are the most reactive of the metals The reactivity of Group I metals increase as you down the group so the Group I metal at the bottom of the group will be the most reactive element This is francium but caesium is also accepted, as there is such a small amount of francium found naturally (there is estimated to be about 30 g in the whole of the Earth's crust!)

questions.stem:
The structures of six organic compounds are shown.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/09/6-compounds-cie-igcse.png)Give the name of F.
questions.explanation: The name of F is: Butane; [1 mark] [Total: 1 mark] The main carbon chain / backbone contains 4 carbons This means that the name will be based on "but-" There are only single bonds and no other atoms apart from hydrogens Therefore, the name will be "-ane" based This leads to the overall name being butane

questions.stem:
Ammonia is produced when aqueous sodium hydroxide is warmed with ammonium sulfate. Ammonia is less dense than air and very soluble in water. The apparatus below was used to prepare a sample of dry ammonia gas.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/11/42637_cie-igcse-atp-2003-paper-6-q5.jpg)
Name substance C.
questions.explanation: Substance C is: Sodium hydroxide; [1 mark] [Total: 1 mark] Sodium hydroxide is a solution and ammonium sulfate is a solid (as it is an ionic compound which are usually solids) The burette will hold the solution which is substance C

questions.stem:
The diagrams show the apparatus used to obtain crystals of calcium chloride from a mixture of solid calcium chloride and solid calcium carbonate. Calcium chloride is soluble in water and calcium carbonate is insoluble in water.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/09/making-calcium-chloride-crystals.png) Complete the boxes to name the apparatus.
questions.explanation: The names of the apparatus are: Tripod; [1 mark] Stirring rod / stirrer; [1 mark] [Total: 2 marks] You should be familiar with both of these pieces of equipment and be able to name the other equipment used when making soluble and insoluble salts

questions.stem:
Four substances are shown below. 
In which of these substances are the particles close together and moving slowly past each other?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Particles which are close together but can move slowly past each other are in the liquid state. A is incorrect as ice is a solid so the particles cannot move. B and C are incorrect as air is a mixture of gaseous particles, and steam is water in the gaseous state, which move faster and are also further apart than particles in a liquid.

questions.stem:
Pure H2O boils at 100 oC and freezes at 0 oC.
What is the melting point and boiling point of water after the addition of potassium chloride?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Boiling point / o C | Freezing point / o C |
| A | 103 | -3 |
| B | 103 | 3 |
| C | 97 | -3 |
| D | 97 | No change |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Potassium chloride in water is an impurity which affects its physical properties. Pure water boils at 100 ºC and freezes at 0 ºC. In water, potassium chloride causes the boiling point to increase and the freezing point to decrease . This is why salt is used to prevent icing on roads as it lowers the freezing point, making it more difficult for ice to form at temperature close to 0 ºC. B and D are incorrect as the freezing point of water decreases when potassium chloride is added to it. C is incorrect as the boiling point of water increases when potassium chloride is added to it.

questions.stem:
The table gives the composition of three particles.


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
| particle | number of protons | number of electrons | number of neutrons |
| A | 15 | 15 | 16 |
| B | 15 | 15 | 16 |
| C | 15 | 15 | 17 |
What is the evidence in the table for each of the following? 
i) Particle A is an atom.
 [1]
 ii) A, B and C are all particles of the same element.
 [1]
iii) Particles A and C are isotopes of the same element.
[2]
questions.explanation: The evidence for each of the following is: i) Particle A is an atom. (Particle A has the) same number of protons and electrons; [1 mark] ii) A , B and C are all particles of the same element. (Particles A , B and C ) all have the same number of protons / same proton number / same atomic number; [1 mark] iii) Particles A and C are isotopes of the same element. (Particles A and C have the) same number of protons / same proton number / same atomic number; [1 mark] (But a) different number of neutrons / different nucleon number / different mass number; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] Make sure you are aware of the difference between an atom, isotope and ion in terms of subatomic particles Atoms of the same element have the same number of protons and electrons Isotopes of the same element have different numbers of neutrons but the same number of protons Ions of the same element have different numbers of electrons but the same number of protons

Look at the diagrams of common laboratory apparatus.

questions.explanation:
The pieces of equipment are: A = mortar; [1 mark] B = stirrer / stirring rod; [1 mark] 
 A thermometer is not accepted C = tripod; [1 mark] D = Bunsen burner; [1 mark] [Total: 4 marks] The main issues with naming the equipment in this question are A and B For A, the mortar (bowl) and pestle (stick) are commonly jumbled For B, several students will put a thermometer even though a thermometer is used to measure temperature, not stir

questions.stem:
Most of the elements on the Periodic Table are metals. Metals can be distinguished from non-metals by differences in their physical properties.
Which row correctly describes a metal?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Malleability | Heat & electrical conductivity |
| A |  |  |
| B |  |  |
| C |  |  |
| D |  |  |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Metals are malleable meaning they can be beaten into different shapes. Metals also conduct heat and electricity. A, B and D are incorrect as metals have both of these properties due to the close packing of the metal ions and the delocalised electrons. Non-metals cannot conduct heat or electricity.

questions.stem:
A beaker of water, at its boiling point of 100 oC, is heated so that the liquid starts to become a gas, also at 100 oC.
Which row of the table correctly compares the liquid phase with the gas phase under these conditions?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Average distance between the particles | Average speed of the particles |
| A | the same in the liquid and the gas | the same in the liquid and the gas |
| B | greater in the liquid | greater in the gas |
| C | greater in the gas | greater in the liquid |
| D | greater in the gas | the same in the liquid and the gas |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The particles in a liquid are in contact with each other, while those in a gas are considerably further apart. The average kinetic energy of each molecule is related to the temperature of the substance. This means that, if a substance has a higher temperature, its molecules will, on average, have a higher kinetic energy. As Kinetic energy =  , the speed of the molecules will also be greater. Since both the liquid water and the gaseous water are both at a temperature of 100 o C, their molecules both have the same kinetic energy, and are travelling at the same speed. Each of the other answers has made at least one error. Liquid particles are always closer together than gas particles. Most students incorrectly think that gas particles have a higher kinetic energy than liquid particles. This is only true  if the gas is also at a higher temperature than the liquid (which is usually, but not always, the case)

questions.stem:
CH4, H2O and HCl are covalent compounds.
Which atoms in these compounds do not use all of their outer shell electrons in bonding?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Oxygen in water and chlorine in hydrogen chloride both have nonbonding electron pairs in their outer shells whereas methane does not as shown.  A, B and D are incorrect as in these options; there is either carbon or hydrogen, both of these atoms used all of their outer shell electrons in bonding.

questions.stem:
Which is true about chemical energy changes?


|  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | Reaction type | Energy flows | Temperature of surroundings |
| A | exothermic | to the surroundings | increases |
| B | exothermic | from the surroundings | decreases |
| C | endothermic | to the surroundings | decreases |
| D | endothermic | from the surroundings | increases |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: In an exothermic reaction the energy transferred from the reacting chemicals heats up the surroundings and results in a rise in temperature B is incorrect as the energy flow and temperature change are the wrong way around for an exothermic reaction C is incorrect as the energy flow is the wrong way around for an endothermic reaction D is incorrect as the temperature change is the wrong away around

questions.stem: Which of the following processes represents a physical change?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C A physical change involves a change in a physical property . Ethanol boils at 78 o C so at this temperature or higher it changes its physical state from a liquid to a gas . A , B and D are incorrect as these processes involve chemical changes where substances react together chemically, breaking and forming bonds.

questions.stem: Which statement about graphite and diamond is not correct?
options: A. Graphite is a good lubricant due to the weak forces in between the layers.
B. Diamond is used as a drill tip because it is an extremely hard substance.
C. Graphite has a low melting point due to the weak forces in between the layers.
D. Diamond is an allotrope of carbon.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because Graphite has a giant covalent structure and these compounds have high melting points due to the high number of covalent bonds holding atoms together within them. A is incorrect as in graphite the carbon atoms are arranged in layers which can slide over each other easily as there are only weak  forces between the layers, making it useful as a lubricant. B is incorrect as in diamond each carbon atom is covalently bonded to 4  others, forming a giant covalent structure. This makes it very hard as it requires a lot of energy to break so many  strong  covalent bonds and so it is useful as a tip for drills. D is incorrect as diamond contains carbon atoms only and is in the solid  state , hence it is an allotrope of carbon.

questions.stem:

| C | bromine | hydrogen |

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Molten metal bromides consist of positive metal ions and negative bromide ions The positive metal ion will be discharged at the cathode (negative electrode) where they will gain electrons to form the metal The negative bromide ions will be discharged at the anode (positive electrode) where they will lose electrons to form bromine B , C and D are incorrect as the products at the electrodes are incorrect

questions.explanation: This reaction show that chlorine is more reactive than bromine because: Chlorine has displaced / taken the place of bromine in magnesium bromide; [1 mark] [Total: 1 mark] The halogens get more reactive as you move up the group Since chlorine is above bromine, this means that chlorine will displace bromide from compounds

questions.stem:
Two cars sit side by side, a black car and a white car. It is Summer.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/q2-hard-mcq-2-3-thermal-processes-cie-igcse-physics.png)During the day both cars absorb infrared radiation from the Sun, and during the night, both cars lose energy by emitting infrared radiation.
Which car heats up more quickly during the day, and which car cools down more quickly at night?


|  |  |  |
|---|---|---|
|  | Car which heats up more quickly during the day | Car which cools down more quickly at night |
| A | black | black |
| B | black | white |
| C | white | black |
| D | white | white |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: Darker coloured objects emit and absorb infrared radiation at a greater rate than their light coloured counterparts. A greater rate of absorption of infrared radiation raises the temperature more quickly. A greater rate of emission of infrared radiation lowers the temperature more quickly. In general: black objects change temperature quickly, while white objects change temperature slowly. B is incorrect as the white car will cool more slowly at night. C is incorrect as the white car will heat up more slowly during the day. D is incorrect as the white car will both heat up and cool more slowly than the black car.

questions.stem:
Which two points on the wave are exactly one wavelength apart?


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/03/q4-easy-mcq-3-1-general-properties-of-wave-cie-igcse-physics.png)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: A wavelength is the distance between two identical points on a wave. Q and S are identical points because they are both in the equilibrium position and the string is pointing in identical directions to their left and right, i.e. up on the left and down on the right. A common mistake is to think Q and R are 1 wavelength apart because they are both on the equilibrium line. However, the string is pointing in opposite directions at each of these points. There are plenty more ways to explain wavelength, like: to complete a wave you have to go up, down and back up again, but I rather like the first explanation. It’s much easier to explain with a diagram:  A is incorrect as P and S are 1.25 wavelengths apart. B is incorrect as Q and R are half a wavelength apart. D is incorrect as P and R are 0.75 wavelengths apart.

questions.stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used in remote controls?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: Remote controls contain an infrared LED at the front. This is used to send coded signals to the TV that cannot be seen by the human eye. It won’t work with Apple phones as they include an IR filter over the lens of their cameras. A is incorrect as microwaves are used for mobile phone and satellite communication, and for cooking in microwave ovens. B is incorrect as visible light is used to see things. C is incorrect as ultraviolet radiation is used to kill bacteria, to make security features in secure documents and banknotes glow and to make people’s clothes and teeth glow at nightclubs. Oh, it also gives you a suntan and causes skin cancer.

questions.stem:
Reversible reactions occur when products formed in the forward reaction behave as reactants and proceed in the reverse direction to produce the original reactants again.
Which of the following statements is correct for a reversible reaction?


|  |  |
|---|---|
| 1 | If the forward reaction is exothermic, then the reverse reaction must be endothermic |
| 2 | If the forward reaction is endothermic, then the reverse reaction must be exothermic |
| 3 | Both directions are exothermic |
| 4 | Both directions are endothermic |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A The energetics of reversible reactions are such that if the forward direction is exothermic, then the reverse direction is the opposite , hence endothermic. This applies in both cases, so if the forward reaction is endothermic, then the reverse reaction must be exothermic. B and D are incorrect as both directions will not have the same energy change. C is incorrect as statements 1 and 2 are both true.

questions.stem:
A book shop owner sets up the circuit below, but they find that the lamp is too dim.


![diagram](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2023/04/q9-medium-mcq-4-3-electrical-circuits-cie-igcse-physics.png)What change can be made to the circuit to increase the brightness of the bulb?
options: A. Putting another resistor in parallel with the battery.
B. Putting a resistor in parallel with the bulb.
C. Putting another resistor in series with the resistor.
D. Putting another resistor in parallel with the resistor.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D because: The brightness of the bulb depends on the power it dissipates, P = IV , so any increase to the voltage or current in the part of the circuit containing the bulb (assuming the other does not change in the opposite direction) would increase its brightness. Resistances in parallel are smaller than the smallest resistor in the combination. Adding another resistor in parallel with the original resistor would decrease the overall resistance of the circuit, and would increase the brightness of the bulb. A is incorrect as this would not change the voltage across either the bulb or the resistor, and would not change the current through them. It would, however, give another branch for current to flow down, draining the battery more quickly. B is incorrect as this would decrease the resistance of the bulb/new resistor combo, increasing the total current in the circuit (but not the current through the bulb), and decreasing the voltage across the bulb. Remember that voltage splits according to resistance, so lowering the resistance also lowers the voltage across it. The bulb would get dimmer. C is incorrect as this would increase the total resistance of the circuit, thus limiting the current and decreasing the brightness of the bulb.

questions.stem: Which statement about graphite and diamond is not correct?

What mass of oxygen is required to combine with the hydrogen?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Step Working out 1 The information given in the questions is used to find the ratio in grams of each reactant. 48 g O 2 : 6 g H 2 Divide by 6 to get the smallest ratio, so 8 g O 2 : 1 g H 2 2 The mass of oxygen that combines with 2 g of hydrogen is found by multiplying across by 2, since the amount of hydrogen has been doubled . questions.stem: A bullet is shot from a gun. The bullet moves forward and the gun moves in the opposite direction. Which of the following statements is true?
options: A. They move with the same velocity in opposite directions.
B. The bullet moves with a slower velocity due to its mass.
C. The total momentum of the system is zero.
D. The total momentum of the system does not stay constant before and after the collision.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The total momentum of the bullet and gun before shooting = the total momentum of the bullet and gun after shooting. Before shooting the bullet and the gun are stationary so overall the total momentum will be zero. A is incorrect as the velocities of the bullet and the gun will be different due to their different masses. However, they will move in opposite directions. B is incorrect as the bullet will actually move faster due to having a smaller mass. D is incorrect as the law of conservation of momentum states that momentum will always be constant before and after a collision.

questions.stem:

options: A. The air molecules expand and become less dense.
B. The air molecules move further apart, making the air less dense.

D. The air molecules move closer together, making the air less dense.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because: As the temperature of air molecules increases, they move more quickly, and tend to be further apart, on average. This makes the air less dense. Less dense substances float on more dense substances. A is incorrect as the molecules themselves remain exactly the same size and shape. They absolutely do not expand. This is a very common misconception among students. C is incorrect as the air molecules do not contract, either. D is incorrect as if the air molecules moved closer together, the density of the air would increase .

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: Carbon monoxide is a product of the incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon. questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Adding concentrated hydrochloric acid increases the concentration of acid particles This leads to more frequent collisions , the rate of reaction is faster , so the yellow precipitate forms faster A is incorrect because ice lowers the temperature , which slows down particle movement and reduces the rate of reaction B is incorrect because adding water dilutes the sodium thiosulphate, lowering the concentration, reducing the rate of reaction C is incorrect because a catalyst increase the rate of reaction by finding an alternate pathway with lower E A (Activation Energy)

questions.stem:

|---|---|---|
|  | Option | Explanation |
| A | ceiling-mounted | hot air is more dense and falls |
| B | ceiling-mounted | hot air is less dense and falls |
| C | underfloor | hot air is less dense and rises |
| D | underfloor | hot air is more dense and rises |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C because: The fact that hotter air is less dense, and so it rises, is what makes underfloor heating the best. Heat given off from underfloor heating will rise to the ceiling, and heat the whole room on the way up. If the heater were in the ceiling, on the other hand, all the warm air would be created at the ceiling, and would stay there, leaving the floor rather cold. It's also nice on your toes! Ceiling-mounted heaters are a thing, but you tend to need a fan with them to blow the hot air back down to the ground. Or at least really, really good air circulation. A is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense. B is incorrect as hot air is less dense, but it does not fall D is incorrect as hot air is less dense, not more dense.

| C | less than critical angle | greater refractive index than B |
| D | less than critical angle | smaller refractive index than B |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A because: This question is about total internal reflection. questions.stem: In what way are microwaves different from ultraviolet waves?
options: A. Ultraviolet waves travel faster than microwaves in a vacuum.
B. Microwaves have a longer wavelength than ultraviolet waves.
C. Microwaves have a higher frequency than ultraviolet waves.
D. Microwaves are longitudinal while ultraviolet waves are transverse.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B because The electromagnetic spectrum contains the following types of waves in the order you have probably learned them. This is in order of increasing  frequency and decreasing  wavelength Radio waves Microwaves Infrared Visible light Ultra violet X-Rays Gamma rays We can see that ultraviolet waves have both a higher  frequency and a smaller  wavelength than microwaves . Therefore, the only correct answer is B A is incorrect as all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum. C is incorrect as microwaves have a lower frequency than ultraviolet. D is incorrect as both microwaves and ultraviolet are transverse waves. All electromagnetic waves are transverse.

questions.stem:
X, Y and Z are the halogens chlorine, bromine and iodine, but not necessarily in that order.
When aqueous Y is added to an aqueous solution containing ions of Z, a brown solution is formed. When aqueous X is added to an aqueous solution containing ions of Z, no reaction occurs
Which row correctly identifies halogens X, Y and Z?

|  | X | Y | Z |
| A | bromine | chlorine | iodine |
| B | iodine | chlorine | bromine |
| C | iodine | bromine | chlorine |
| D | chlorine | iodine | bromine |
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B Halogens are Group VII non-metals In terms of reactivity, a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide ion from its aqueous solution The reactivity decreases down the group (chlorine > bromine > iodine) When a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen in aqueous state, the less reactive halogen will be observed in the mixture It is important to recap the  appearance of the halogens Chlorine is a pale yellow-green gas, bromine is a red-brown liquid, and iodine is a grey-black solid (brown in solution) A brown solution is formed when aqueous Y is added to ions of Z A brown solution in water can indicate that bromine (red-brown liquid) or iodine (typically grey solid, but brown in aqueous) was formed This means that Z is less reactive than Y When aqueous X is added to Z ions, no reaction occurs This means X is less reactive than Z In consequence, X is  less reactive than Y Therefore, in order of decreasing reactivity: Y >  Z  >  X Since, reactivity decreases down the group (chlorine > bromine > iodine) Y = chlorine, Z = bromine, X = iodine

questions.stem: Which statement explains why alloys are harder and stronger than pure metals?
options: A. Alloys contain strong covalent bonds between the different atoms.
B. The metallic bonds in an alloy are stronger because there are more delocalised electrons.
C. The atoms in an alloy are packed more closely together than in a pure metal.
D. The different sized atoms in an alloy mean the layers can no longer slide over each other.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D Pure metals have a regular arrangement of identical atoms in layers that can easily slide over each other when a force is applied An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, in which the extra elements are added in the spaces between the positive metal ions from the lattice Because these added elements have different sized atoms, they disrupt the regular lattice arrangement This means the layers can no longer slide over each other, which makes the alloy harder and stronger than the pure metal A is incorrect as metals and alloys are held together by metallic bonding (the electrostatic attraction between positive ions and a sea of delocalised electrons), not covalent bonds B is incorrect  as even if the number of delocalised electrons might vary depending on the metals mixed, the primary reason for the physical hardness of an alloy is the disruption of the layers (a structural change), not a change in the electrostatic strength of the metallic bonds C is incorrect as introducing different sized atoms into a lattice usually disrupts the neat, close-packed structure; it does not necessarily pack them more tightly together
